  as `_mainInboxMessages`, children via the executor) — messages land as
  sender-attributed user messages, so they persist in the session and read
  like a chat. Idle wake: an inbox watcher (2s CLI / 3s app) starts a turn
  when mail arrives while idle — two Fa instances chat live; a 10-run
  streak cap without user input breaks agent-to-agent ping-pong loops.
  The lanes live in `InboxWakePolicy` (gh-1180): user-kind mail always
  wakes and resets the streak (gating it would deadlock:
  no run → no reset → no run); a delivered `schedule_message`
  self-reminder (`[scheduled] ` prefix, from == to) is EXEMPT from the
  cap — a deliberate agent-chosen cadence (night watch, periodic sweep)
  wakes forever, with a 30s cadence floor so a zero-delay re-schedule
  spin is still bounded like chatter; foreign agent chatter stays
  capped. A refused wake is never silent: one dim `[mail] wake refused`
  line per episode and a `wake_refused` receipt.
  UI: `/agents` rows show a `mail:N` pending marker (the CLI
  font has no ✉ glyph), the app's AgentsSection shows `✉N`; observe/detail
  views list the pending inbox.
  Issue #27 adds the hub-first composition: with `DAP_MASTER_SECRET` set
  and the hub plugin enabled, `bin/fah.dart` wraps the hub as
  `HubFabricRepository` (bin/, IO-bound) and routes the fabric through
  `FallbackMessagingRepository` (lib) — hub-first for hub-resolvable
  targets, file inboxes as offline fallback, queued mail forwarded on
  reconnect, merged drains deduped by id. `AgentCliConfig.hubFabric`
  hosts inject it; the plugin host skips its separate inbox when the
  fabric owns delivery (one hub-mail consumer). Subagent drains never
  touch the hub. Issue #304 adds the one-step CLI surface over it:
  `fa dap start|stop|status` (bin/fah_dap_command.dart —
  `DapHubController`, every IO a seam) probes the port (`/healthz` + a
  `/ws` presence handshake; foreign server = clear error naming the
  port, no enrollment), spawns `fa hub serve` detached, prompts the
  master key ONCE (hidden; empty = open hub, the zero-config extension
  default; non-interactive starts prompt nothing), enrolls per the
  DAP_MASTER_SECRET flow and persists only the hub-issued clientSecret
  (0600 `~/.dap/config.json`; wrong key re-prompts 3x then a manual
  hint — a rejected secret is never persisted). The hub pid/state file
  `~/.dap/hub.pid` (parse in lib/src/hub/dap_local_hub_state.dart) lets
  a second CLI attach (no double-spawn) and `fa dap stop` work from ANY
  instance exactly once — stop names connected peers (e.g. "Browser")
  and SIGTERMs the owning pid; the fabric falls back to file inboxes.
  The `/dap` menu's leading row is state-dependent (AC7): "Start DAP
  locally (one step)" stopped, "Stop DAP" running
  (lib/src/cli/dap_menu_options.dart `dapMenuOptions(hubRunning:)`).
  `agent_directory` renders hub roster entries (MailboxEntry.source ==
  'hub') with a `[hub]` marker; the `fabric.hub: false` kill switch
  (FabricConfig.hub, gate `hubFabricWired` in bin/hub_fabric_
  repository.dart, mirrors images.registry) leaves the fabric the bare
  file layer — byte-identical legacy listing (REG test
  test/messaging/fabric_kill_switch_reg_test.dart).
  Issue #27 phase 3 adds the A2A boundary gateway: `agent_message` accepts
  `name@machine` for OTHER machines — `A2aMailGateway` (lib/src/a2a/
  a2a_mail_gateway.dart) resolves the machine against the `a2a:` config
  section (the server named like the machine) and sends the mail as an A2A
  `message/send` with a `faMail` metadata envelope (id/from/to/text/sentAt/
  hops, sender address stamped `mailbox@machine` for replies); a failed
  remote task errors instead of dead-dropping. Inbound: `fa serve --a2a`
  mounts a mail sink — envelope-carrying sends deposit into the project's
  file inboxes (resolved by mailbox id or session display name) instead of
  running a turn; endpoints without a sink fail such sends honestly. The
  hub stays the intra-machine transport; A2A stays the interop boundary.
- `lib/src/session/attach/` — attached-session infrastructure (the Fa app
  watching a live `fa` CLI session 1:1 and handing it input): three
  INTERFACES so a later network impl (`fa serve --attach`, remote headless)
  drops in without touching consumers — `SessionPresenceStore`
  (register/touch/unregister/list; stale heartbeats auto-drop, crash
  coverage), `SessionEventSource.watch` (transcript tail as
  `AttachedMessage` rows: user/assistant/tool), `SessionInputChannel.send`
  (user input to the owning process). File impls:
  `FileSessionPresenceStore` (`<sessionsRoot>/.presence/<id>.json`,
  15s staleness) and `FileSessionEventSource` (JSONL tail via
  `readTextLines` deltas) + `FileSessionInputChannel` (fabric mail,
  `AgentMessageKind.user`, to `<sessionId>/main`). CLI wiring: `run()`
  registers presence, the 2s inbox timer touches it every other tick,
  `finally` unregisters; `AgentCliConfig.presenceStore` is injectable
  (bin/fah.dart builds the file store; tests inject fakes). CLI sessions
  carry `agent: cli` metadata (the app writes `fa`). App wiring:
  `CliSessionPresence` service (3s poll) + green-dot `live` on
  `SessionTile`; a live tap in the chat-sheet drawer opens
  `AttachedSessionScreen` (controller `attached_session_controller.dart`)
  instead of a second writer on the same JSONL.
- `lib/src/memory/` — long-term memory: `MemoryController` over the
  `flutter_agent_memory` package (hosted pub.dev dep),
  `execution_env_kb_storage` (KbStorage → ExecutionEnv), `memory_add`/
  `memory_search`/`memory_list` tools (`memoryTools(controller, onChanged:)`),
  and the `<memory>` prompt section: `formatPromptSection()` (BOTH scopes,
  entities parsed via `KBFileParser` — the raw file's first line is the
  `---` delimiter, not the fact) is cached by the host and recomposed into
  the system prompt asynchronously after startup + on every `memory_add`
  (CLI `_refreshMemorySection` in agent_cli.dart, app in AgentService);
  phase 2:
  `compaction_memory_hook` (compaction-time durable-fact extraction on the
  smol role, non-blocking), `maintain()` (levels + consolidate, running
  guard, 24h stamp), triggers on session start + `/memory maintain`;
  `/memory` shows stats.
- Git-backed memory (the repo IS the memory): storage paths come from the
  `memory:` config section — project `.fah/config.yaml` wins over
  `~/.fah/config.yaml` (`loadProjectMemoryConfig`); a relative
  `projectPath` resolves against the project root. This repo dogfoods it:
  `.fah/config.yaml` points at the COMMITTED `memory/` directory — clone
  the repo, get its memory. Inside the store dir: `MemoryRepoInit.
  ensureGitSupport()` (flutter_agent_memory 0.2.0) keeps `.gitignore`
  (derived artifacts: GRAPH.md, MEMORY.revision, INDEX.md,
  .last_maintenance — rebuilt on load, never committed) and
  `.gitattributes` (`DELETIONS.md merge=union` — the append-only
  tombstone ledger merges by union). Note ids are merge-friendly since
  0.2.0: `n_0447_a1b2` = sequential index + 4-hex md5 of the normalized
  text (parallel branches union-merge; legacy `n_0001` ids stay valid
  forever). The `memory_add` description IS the package's
  `MemoryPolicy.memoryAddPolicy` (docs/memory/memory_add_policy.md in
  the memory repo): durable facts only, solved problems are superseded
  via delete+add (never left to rot), project scope is PUBLIC (git) —
  no secrets/personal data there, user scope stays machine-local.
  `.gitignore` whitelists `.fah/config.yaml` (+rules/lsp/mcp/agents/
  skills/packages); logs/sessions/bash_jobs stay local. Commit memory/
  changes with the task that produced them (`memory:` prefix for
  memory-only commits).
- `lib/src/a2a/` — A2A (Agent2Agent) interop: `a2a_client.dart` (Agent Card
  + JSON-RPC + SSE), `a2a_config.dart` (`a2a:` yaml section, `${NAME}`
  env tokens), `a2a_manager.dart` (lazy per-server connect, A2A task state
  → subagent lifecycle mapping), `a2a_server.dart` (request handler).
  `task` tool agent type `a2a:<name>` runs remote agents as subagents
  (uniform `task_status`/`task_send`); `/a2a` shows server status;
  `fa serve --a2a [--port N] [--token T]` mounts this agent as an endpoint
  (`bin/serve_a2a.dart`).
- `lib/src/cli/hep.dart` + `agent_cli_hep_io.dart` — HEP v1, the Harness
  Event Protocol (`fa --output events[=full]`, issue #155): strict JSONL
  on stdout for server-side supervisors, one JSON object per line,
  flushed per line. A TURN is one assistant LLM ROUND, not one user
  message — a user turn that runs tools yields SEVERAL terminal frames
  (`turn_done` per round, ids incrementing). `HepWriter` is
  `AgentListener`-shaped (`agent.subscribe(hep.handleEvent)`); the
  `HepEventsIO` decorator (a `part of agent_cli.dart`) drops
  `CliIO.write` so stdout stays pure while diagnostics keep stderr.
  Frame catalog, ordering/flush guarantees and versioning policy:
  docs/hep.md; byte shape pinned by golden tests (test/cli/hep_test.dart).
  `--attach` sniffs image mimes by magic bytes (png/jpeg/gif/webp ride
  as base64 blocks); any other file passes through as an
  `[attached file: …]` path reference appended to the prompt (issue
  #196) — never an octet-stream image block.
- `bin/fah.dart` — the `fah`/`fa` CLI. REPL (no args) or headless
  (`fa "prompt"` / `-p` / `--prompt-file <path>` (alias `-f`), mutually
  exclusive). First positional naming an EXISTING file is the prompt source
  (`.md`/`.txt` inlined, others attached by reference; `-p` is verbatim;
  `--prompt-file` reads ANY path verbatim, missing/unreadable = usage
  error exit 64). Args parsed in `lib/src/cli/cli_args.dart`

  stream, `writeln` = diagnostics (stderr headless). The TUI captures the
  mouse by default (wheel scrolling + click routing — the alternate screen
  has no native scrollback): SGR 1002+1006 with a per-frame hit-region
  registry (`tui_hit_regions.dart`, topmost-region click/drag/release

  works via the terminal's bypass modifier (Shift), and `FA_TUI_MOUSE=0`

  native select-to-copy.
  Shift+Enter's HID poll is resolved once at startup

  the one-shot CoreGraphics probe (sacrificial isolate, ~300 ms timeout)

Senior Developer Engineer specializing in root cause analysis and bug fixing ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Coding Guidelines — follow existing codebase patterns and conventions"] G2["Before implementing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists in project root or subdirectories → READ and FOLLOW it — it contains agent-specific instructions, coding styles, and conventions"] G4["If skills are available in the project → USE them — they provide specialized capabilities, workflows, and tool integrations"] G5["Instructions may be extended via project configuration — always follow the full set of provided instructions"] G6["Never invent new patterns when the codebase already has an established way of doing things"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 --> G5 --> G6 ``` ## input_context_reading.md ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph INPUT_ORDER["⚠️ MANDATORY: Read input files FIRST before anything else"] I0["find input/ -type f | sort — list all available files"] I1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, deployment constraints, approved frameworks"] I2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/request.md — ticket description, requirements, solution design, diagrams"] I3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — existing discussion, prior decisions, linked info"] I4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/existing_questions.json — answered questions = binding requirements"] I5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — specifications already downloaded"] I6["6️⃣ Check for images in input/TICKET/ — *.png *.jpg *.gif *.svg"] I7["7️⃣ If present: input/TICKET/parent-KEY.md — parent story summary, description, ACs"] I8["8️⃣ If present: input/TICKET/parent_context_ba.md / sa.md / vd.md — BA/SA/VD context"] I0 --> I1 --> I2 --> I3 --> I4 --> I5 --> I6 --> I7 --> I8 end subgraph CONFLUENCE_RULE["Confluence pages in input/ — READ THEM, don't re-fetch"] C1["✅ DO: read input/TICKET/confluence/PageName.md"] C2["❌ DON'T: call dmtools confluence_* to re-fetch pages already in input/"] C3["✅ DO: read image files in input/TICKET/confluence/ — they are attachments from that page"] end subgraph ATTACH_RULE["Attachments — check before fetching via API"] A1["Search glob 'input/**/*.png' and 'input/**/*.jpg' — find pre-downloaded images"] A2["If image found locally → analyze it directly, no API call needed"] A3["If attachment NOT in input/ → use dmtools confluence_get_content_attachments "] A1 --> A2 A1 -->|not found| A3 end subgraph DMTOOLS_RULE["When to use dmtools for external data"] D1["ONLY if you need data NOT already in input/"] D2["dmtools jira_get_ticket KEY, dmtools confluence_search QUERY, etc."] D3["See instructions/common/dmtools_cli.md for full reference"] end INPUT_ORDER --> CONFLUENCE_RULE --> ATTACH_RULE --> DMTOOLS_RULE ``` ## general_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD START([Bug ticket ready for fix]) --> READ["⚠️ MANDATORY: Read ALL input files FIRST — see instructions/common/input_context_reading.md"] READ --> RETURNED{Ticket returned to development?} RETURNED -->|Yes| PREV["Review previous PR diff and QA feedback in comments.md"] PREV --> RCA_RET["Write/Update RCA explaining why previous fix failed — see output_rules.md for rca.md format"] RETURNED -->|No| RCA_FRESH["Write fresh RCA from ticket description and linked_tests.md"] RCA_RET --> REPRO RCA_FRESH --> REPRO["Write a unit test that reproduces the bug. Run it — it MUST FAIL"] REPRO --> EXISTS{Test fails?} EXISTS -->|No| ALREADY["Check git history, current code, and linked tests.
⚠️ If linked test exists: verify it passes AND the test was created/updated BEFORE the fix commit — not after.
If bug is genuinely fixed — write outputs/already_fixed.json and stop"] ALREADY --> END_FIXED([End — bug already fixed]) EXISTS -->|Yes| BLOCKED{Fix requires external decision, secrets, or infra changes?} BLOCKED -->|Yes| BLOCK["Write outputs/blocked.json and stop — see output_rules.md"] BLOCK --> END_BLOCKED([End — blocked awaiting human input]) BLOCKED -->|No| FIX["Make minimum targeted fix for the root cause ONLY"] FIX --> VERIFY["Run reproduction test (must PASS) and full test suite (no regressions)"] VERIFY --> PASS{All tests pass?} PASS -->|No| ADJUST["Adjust fix and re-run tests"] ADJUST --> VERIFY PASS -->|Yes| GITSTATUS["Run git status and review every new/modified file"] GITSTATUS --> SECRETS{Sensitive or untracked non-code files present?} SECRETS -->|Yes| IGNORE["Add appropriate patterns to .gitignore"] SECRETS -->|No| SUMMARY["Write concise bug fix summary to outputs/response.md — see output_rules.md"] IGNORE --> SUMMARY SUMMARY --> END([End — post-processing handles git/PR]) ``` ## Returning from test-automation failure When this Bug has been sent back to development because a linked Test Case failed: 1. Read the `Failed Reason` field of every linked Test Case. 2. If the failure is caused by a missing token, missing permission, missing secret, or any other access/credential/infra issue that you cannot fix in product code, write `outputs/blocked.json` and stop. Do **not** try to code a fix for an access problem. 3. Only attempt a product-code fix when the failure is a genuine product regression. ## tdd_approach.md ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph TDD["TDD for Bug Fixes — RED-GREEN-REFACTOR"] T0["Start with a clear understanding of the bug from RCA"] T1["RED: Write a unit test that REPRODUCES the bug
— must describe the exact failure scenario
— run it to confirm it FAILS"] T2["GREEN: Write minimum fix to make the reproduction test PASS
— simplest possible change
— do not refactor unrelated code"] T3["REFACTOR: Clean up while keeping tests GREEN
— improve naming, remove duplication
— run full suite after every change"] T4{"More edge cases to cover?"} T5["Repeat RED-GREEN-REFACTOR for next edge case"] T0 --> T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 T4 -->|Yes| T5 --> T1 T4 -->|No| DONE([Bug fixed with regression tests]) end subgraph RULES["Bug TDD Rules"] R1["❌ NEVER fix code without a failing reproduction test first"] R2["❌ NEVER write more code than needed to fix the bug"] R3["✅ Returned bugs: your fix must differ from the previous attempt"] R4["✅ If the bug involves a loop/collection, add a reproduction case with 2+ items, not only a single-item scenario — a single-item test can pass while multi-item logic is still broken"] R5["✅ Run the FULL test suite before finishing — no regressions allowed"] end TDD --> RULES ``` ## output_rules.md ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph OUTPUTS["Required outputs for bug development"] O1["outputs/rca.md — write FIRST, update as you learn"] O2["outputs/already_fixed.json — only if bug is genuinely fixed in current code AND tests pass"] O3["outputs/blocked.json — only if fix requires external input/credentials/infra"] O4["outputs/response.md — concise PR description (see formatting_rules.md)"] end subgraph RCA["rca.md format"] R1["## Root Cause Analysis"] R2["**Bug**: one-sentence description"] R3["**Root cause**: exact technical reason — file, function, line"] R4["**Impact**: what is broken and under what conditions"] R5["**Fix approach**: what needs to change and why"] R6["**Previous attempt**: PR #, what changed, why insufficient (only if returned bug)"] R1…
Let me start by reading the input files as mandated by the instructions.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill

Run it — it MUST FAIL"] REPRO --> EXISTS{Test fails?} EXISTS -->|No| ALREADY["Check git history, current code, and linked tests.

# Daily auto-publish (issue #161): thin orchestrator over the existing
# publish channels. Each channel is an isolated leg — one leg failing never
# kills the others — and every failure self-files a deduplicated GitHub
# issue (label `bug`, assigned to the owner) that auto-closes when the leg
# goes green again. No publish logic is duplicated here: legs dispatch the
# existing workflows via `gh workflow run` and watch them.
#
#   testflight  build-mobile.yml   ios_content=all (the iOS half of the
#                                 mobile build)
#   play        build-mobile.yml   android_content=all,
#                                 android_track=beta (Android external
#                                 beta / open testing — issue #289 lifts
#                                 the standing "Android excluded" owner
#                                 decision for the release track; #947
#                                 adds the listing deploy — texts +
#                                 whole-set image replace + verify — so
#                                 the listing never trails the goldens;
#                                 the leg green-skips while the Play
#                                 secrets are absent)
#   pubdev      in-job OIDC publish, only when pubspec > pub.dev; otherwise
#               a green up-to-date check. The tag-time OIDC publish job
#               (ci.yml) stays the primary path; this leg is the catch-up +
#               loud-failure detector (e.g. expired publish credentials)
#   cli         build-macos.yml    desktop DMG + macOS CLI bundles +
#                                 extension, attached to the next-tag
#                                 release (version passed explicitly so
#                                 mobile/desktop never mint diverging tags)
#   website     pages.yml          fa1.dev (landing + web demo +
#                                 the /outlook add-in slice; gh-1684:
#                                 the extension zip moved to GitHub
#                                 Releases and is no longer site-hosted)
#   addin       office-addin.yml   manifest/taskpane acceptance suite; the
#                                 fa1.dev publish itself rides the website
#                                 leg (pages.yml assembles /outlook)
#
# Legs run only when main moved since the last GREEN daily run — skip-no-
# change is green-neutral, never red (#159 lesson). One exception (gh-1192):
# while main's pubspec version is not yet served by pub.dev the plan gate
# (scripts/daily_plan.sh) forces the legs anyway — a release-in-flight
# green must not become a skip baseline that stalls re-verification and
# rerun-recovery on a quiet main. Versioning stays the
# existing scheme: auto_release.sh patch-bumps + tags every main push
# (2h coalesce); the daily attaches mobile/desktop artifacts to the next
# tag and verifies/republishes pub.dev. See docs/ci.md.
#
# Pause: gh workflow disable daily-publish.yml -R IstiN/flutter_agent_harness

name: Daily auto-publish

run-name: "Daily auto-publish (${{ inputs.legs || 'all' }})"

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '17 5 * * *' # once daily, 05:17 UTC
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      legs:
        description: 'Leg(s) to run'
        type: choice
        default: all
        options:
          - all
          - testflight
          - play
          - pubdev
          - cli
          - website
          - addin
      force:
        description: 'Run even if main has not moved since the last green daily'
        type: boolean
        default: false
      inject_failure:
        description: 'TEST ONLY — fail this leg before any dispatch, to exercise the self-filing issue cycle'
        type: choice
        default: none
        options:
          - none
          - testflight
          - play
          - pubdev
          - cli
          - website
          - addin

permissions:
  contents: read

# One daily at a time; a queued run must not cancel an in-flight one.
concurrency:
  group: daily-publish
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  plan:
    name: Plan (change detection + versions)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # gh-1477: 10m was the same time bomb as the derive-version jobs — a
    # full-history fetch under a 10m ceiling. 20m + the blobless filter
    # below.
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: read
    outputs:
      changed: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.changed }}
      next_tag: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.next_tag }}
      latest_tag: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.latest_tag }}
      pubspec_version: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.pubspec_version }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # gh-1477: daily_plan.sh reads tags / commit metadata / one file
          # at origin/main — never historical blobs. Blobless keeps full
          # tag/commit metadata without the blobs (the full fetch outgrew
          # the old 10m ceiling in the twin derive-version job, run
          # 38027695551).
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none

      - name: Detect main movement and derive versions
        id: plan
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          FORCE: ${{ inputs.force }}
        # gh-1192: the gate (baseline + the release-unresolved re-arm that
        # keeps AC1's «the next daily re-verifies» true on a quiet main)
        # lives in the extracted script — shell-harness tested by
        # test/release_flow_race_test.dart.
        run: bash scripts/daily_plan.sh

  # ── Dispatch legs ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Shape per leg: dispatch the child workflow pinned to main, capture the
  # new run id, watch it, fail on any non-success conclusion. The child run
  # URL is exported even on failure so the report can excerpt its log.
  #
  # ── Timeout arithmetic (#351) ────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Invariants: watch budget > child worst-case (a legitimate slow child is
  # NEVER cancelled by the watcher — that was the #351 bug), leg
  # timeout > budget (the watcher, including its one cancel + re-dispatch
  # cycle, always outlives the child), and where the math fits under
  # GitHub's 360m job cap, leg timeout ≥ 2×budget + ~15m so the SECOND
  # wedge's fail-fast can actually fire inside the leg.
  #
  # Child worst-case = sum of the serialized job timeout-minutes along the
  # child's critical path (every job in a watched chain carries an explicit
  # timeout for exactly this). Margin = appear window (60×10s) + cancel
  # wait (180s) + poll slack ≈ 15m.
  #
  #   leg        child worst-case (serialized chain)          budget    leg timeout
  #   testflight version 20 → build-ios 90 → submit-ios 120   230m  →  250m (15000s) ; 360m
  #             (∥ release-mobile 15, covered by the max)
  #   play       version 20 → build-android 45 →              95m   →  110m (6600s) ; 240m
  #             submit-android 30 (∥ release-mobile 15)
  #   cli        version 20 → build-macos 150×2 (arm64 +      335m  →  350m (21000s) ; 360m
  #             x86_64 SERIALIZE on the single self-hosted
  #             runner) → release-macos 15
  #             (∥ cli matrix 45, extension 30 — shorter paths)
  #   (gh-1477: the version/plan jobs' ceiling moved 10 → 20m — a
  #   full-history fetch outgrew the 10m bomb; the fetch is now blobless
  #   and 20m is the seatbelt. Worst-cases and budgets grew by exactly
  #   the +10m.)
  #   website    pages build 45 → deploy 15                   60m   →   75m (4500s)  ; 180m
  #   addin      office-addin-suite 45 (single job)           45m   →   60m (3600s)  ; 150m
  #
  # Second-wedge headroom (2×budget + ~15m vs leg timeout): play 235 ≤
  # 240 ✓, website 163 ≤ 180 ✓, addin 133 ≤ 150 ✓. testflight (515 > 360)
  # and cli (715 > 360) CANNOT fit two full budgets under GitHub's 360m
  # job cap — their first wedge still self-heals (cancel at budget +
  # re-dispatch ≈ budget+13m), and a second wedge is bounded by the leg
  # timeout instead of the watcher's fail-fast; both children carry
  # per-job server-side timeouts (#344) so a wedged job self-fails even
  # without the watcher.
  #
  # gh-172 (run 39374894901, 2026-10-20): the re-dispatched testflight
  # child sat queued FOREVER on the zombie self-hosted worker (a job-level
  # timeout is enforced BY the runner, so a hung worker outlives its own
  # 90m ceiling and never processes the run cancel either) — the leg burned
  # its remaining ~107m watching a child that could never start and died as
  # a bare 360m ceiling kill. The watcher now also treats "not completed
  # but NO job in_progress for DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS (default
  # max(600, budget/8) — 15000s/8 = 1875s ≈ 31m here; it cannot tell a
  # zombie-held pool from a sibling leg's job legitimately occupying the
  # shared fa-m5-1, so it waits out realistic sibling occupancy)" as a
  # wedge riding the same one self-heal, and cancels the child on the fail
  # path so an orphaned queued run can't publish unattended when the pool
  # revives. Second wedge now ends in a diagnostic inside the leg
  # (testflight ≈ 250m + 13m + 31m stall = 294m < 360m).

  testflight:
    name: 'Leg: TestFlight'
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # #351 arithmetic: child wc 230m (version 20 + build-ios 90 +
    # submit-ios 120) → budget 250m; 360m leg > budget. Two full budgets
    # (515m) exceed GitHub's 360m cap — a second wedge is bounded by this
    # leg timeout, not the watcher fail-fast.
    timeout-minutes: 360
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write
    if: >-
      (needs.plan.outputs.changed == 'true' || inputs.force == true) &&
      (inputs.legs == '' || inputs.legs == 'all' || inputs.legs == 'testflight')
    outputs:
      run_url: ${{ steps.dispatch.outputs.run_url }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Inject failure (test)
        if: inputs.inject_failure == 'testflight'
        run: |
          echo "::error::injected failure (inject_failure=testflight) — exercising the self-filing issue path, nothing dispatched"
          exit 1

      - name: Dispatch build-mobile.yml and watch
        id: dispatch
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Shared watcher (issues #343/#344): correlates OUR run by the
          # child's run-name ("build-mobile (none/all)" — displayTitle is
          # the only distinguisher in the run-list API), newest match in a
          # tight window; a wedged run (self-hosted slot lost, #344) is
          # cancelled and re-dispatched once before failing.
          # Budget 250m = child worst-case 230m (version 20 + build-ios 90
          # + submit-ios 120, #351; gh-1477 moved the version ceiling
          # 10 → 20m — blobless fetch + seatbelt) + 20m margin — a healthy
          # slow TestFlight
          # submit (Apple processing can legitimately take the full 90m
          # ASC wait + 15m verify) is never cancelled by the watcher.
          rc=0
          bash scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh build-mobile.yml \
            --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --ref main \
            --title 'build-mobile (none/all)' \
            --budget-seconds 15000 \
            -f android_content=none -f ios_content=all \
            --out-run-id run_id.txt || rc=$?
          if [ -s run_id.txt ]; then
            echo "run_url=https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/$(cat run_id.txt)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          exit "$rc"

  play:
    name: 'Leg: Play (Android external beta)'
    # Independent of the testflight leg (#359). The #348 serialization was
    # a mitigation for the #343 sibling-dispatch race; #351 eliminated that
    # race structurally — exact displayTitle correlation (this leg's child
    # runs as "build-mobile (all/none)", the testflight leg's as
    # "(none/all)"), NEWEST match, a tight 30s window, and build-mobile's
    # per-run_id concurrency group (no dispatch can cancel another). With
    # the race gone the needs-edge only bought harm: a cancelled testflight
    # watcher skipped Play behind it and the edge added up to 360m of start
    # latency (one leg's external blocker stopped the train — run
    # 34827074052, BETA_REVIEW_CONTACT_EMAIL user-owned).
    #
    # The two residual #346 concerns are handled structurally, not by
    # ordering:
    #   * same-tag convergence — both children independently derive
    #     latest-tag+1, so they can attach to ONE release concurrently;
    #     release_attach_or_create.sh is race-idempotent (a lost create
    #     uploads into the winner's release) with an ownership-scoped draft
    #     guard, and the asset sets never collide (AAB vs IPA).
    #   * runner contention — none: the Android chain is all GitHub-hosted
    #     runners; only build-ios touches the single self-hosted macOS
    #     runner (which already serializes physically with the cli leg's
    #     build-macos children — that pair has always been independent).
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # #351 arithmetic (unchanged by #359 — only the leg's START moved):
    # child wc 95m (version 20 + build-android 45 + submit-android 30) →
    # budget 110m; 240m leg ≥ 2×budget + 15m, so the second-wedge
    # fail-fast fits inside the leg.
    timeout-minutes: 240
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write
    if: >-
      (needs.plan.outputs.changed == 'true' || inputs.force == true) &&
      (inputs.legs == '' || inputs.legs == 'all' || inputs.legs == 'play')
    outputs:
      run_url: ${{ steps.dispatch.outputs.run_url }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
      # Secrets presence is checked in the first step — while the Play
      # upload keystore/service account are not configured, the leg green-
      # skips with a notice (existing neutral-skip leg semantics); it goes
      # live the moment the owner sets them (issue #289).
      PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON: ${{ secrets.PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON }}
      ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 }}
      ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD }}
      ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS }}
      ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Inject failure (test)
        if: inputs.inject_failure == 'play'
        run: |
          echo "::error::injected failure (inject_failure=play) — exercising the self-filing issue path, nothing dispatched"
          exit 1

      - name: Skip without Play secrets (green-neutral)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          missing=""
          [ -z "${ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64:-}" ] && missing="$missing ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64"
          [ -z "${ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD:-}" ] && missing="$missing ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD"
          [ -z "${ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS:-}" ] && missing="$missing ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS"
          [ -z "${ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD:-}" ] && missing="$missing ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD"
          if [ -z "${PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON:-}" ]; then
            missing="$missing PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON"
          fi
          if [ -n "$missing" ]; then
            echo "::notice::Play secrets not configured (missing:${missing}) — the Android leg skips green-neutrally until the upload keystore + Play service account secrets exist (issue #289 owner checklist)."
            exit 0
          fi
          echo "All Play secrets present — dispatching the Android build+upload."

      - name: Dispatch build-mobile.yml and watch
        id: dispatch
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # all: build + Play upload + LISTING deploy (issue #947) — the
          # listing lane replaces the whole image set per locale + device
          # type and verifies it via edits.images.list, so the listing can
          # never trail the committed goldens by more than one train.
          # beta = the external/open testing track, mirroring the iOS leg's
          # external TestFlight group (#239 pattern).
          # Shared watcher (issues #343/#344). Since #359 the TestFlight
          # sibling leg fires CONCURRENTLY with this one (both needs: plan)
          # and dispatches the SAME workflow in the same minute —
          # correlation is by the child's run-name ("build-mobile
          # (all/none)" vs the sibling's "(none/all)", pinned by
          # test), never by "first run in the window", with newest-match +
          # the 30s window; a wedged run is cancelled and re-dispatched
          # once (with the same distinct inputs → same distinct title).
          # Budget 110m = child worst-case 95m (#351: version 20 +
          # build-android 45 + submit-android 30; the #947 listing
          # deploy rides the submit-android job's slack; gh-1477 moved
          # the version ceiling 10 → 20m) + 15m margin.
          rc=0
          bash scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh build-mobile.yml \
            --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --ref main \
            --title 'build-mobile (all/none)' \
            --budget-seconds 6600 \
            -f android_content=all -f android_track=beta -f ios_content=none \
            --out-run-id run_id.txt || rc=$?
          if [ -s run_id.txt ]; then
            echo "run_url=https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/$(cat run_id.txt)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          exit "$rc"

  cli:
    name: 'Leg: CLI + macOS desktop'
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # #351 arithmetic: child wc 335m (version 20 + build-macos 150×2 — the
    # arm64 AND x86_64 matrix legs SERIALIZE on the single self-hosted
    # macOS runner — + release-macos 15) → budget 350m; 360m leg > budget.
    # Two full budgets (715m) far exceed GitHub's 360m cap — a second
    # wedge is bounded by this leg timeout, not the watcher fail-fast
    # (both build-macos jobs carry 150m server-side timeouts, #344).
    timeout-minutes: 360
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write
    if: >-
      (needs.plan.outputs.changed == 'true' || inputs.force == true) &&
      (inputs.legs == '' || inputs.legs == 'all' || inputs.legs == 'cli')
    outputs:
      run_url: ${{ steps.dispatch.outputs.run_url }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Inject failure (test)
        if: inputs.inject_failure == 'cli'
        run: |
          echo "::error::injected failure (inject_failure=cli) — exercising the self-filing issue path, nothing dispatched"
          exit 1

      - name: Dispatch build-macos.yml and watch
        id: dispatch
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Children derive version themselves (latest tag + 1 at their own
          # dispatch moment) — a tag pinned here would race auto_release and
          # could attach assets to a tag pointing at a different commit.
          # Shared watcher (issues #343/#344): correlates OUR run by the
          # child's run-name ("build-macos (create_release=true)") so a
          # concurrent human dispatch is never adopted; a wedged self-hosted
          # run is cancelled and re-dispatched once. Budget 350m = child
          # worst-case 335m (#351: version 20 + build-macos 150 ×2 arches
          # serialized on the one self-hosted runner + release-macos 15;
          # gh-1477 moved the version ceiling 10 → 20m)
          # + 15m margin.
          rc=0
          bash scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh build-macos.yml \
            --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --ref main \
            --title 'build-macos (create_release=true)' \
            --budget-seconds 21000 \
            -f create_release=true \
            --out-run-id run_id.txt || rc=$?
          if [ -s run_id.txt ]; then
            echo "run_url=https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/$(cat run_id.txt)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          exit "$rc"

  website:
    name: 'Leg: Website'
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # #351 arithmetic: child wc 60m (pages build 45 + deploy 15) → budget
    # 75m; 180m leg ≥ 2×budget + 15m, so the second-wedge fail-fast fits
    # (the old 45m leg made the self-heal dead code: 40m budget + 10m
    # appear window never completed inside it).
    timeout-minutes: 180
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write
    if: >-
      (needs.plan.outputs.changed == 'true' || inputs.force == true) &&
      (inputs.legs == '' || inputs.legs == 'all' || inputs.legs == 'website')
    outputs:
      run_url: ${{ steps.dispatch.outputs.run_url }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Inject failure (test)
        if: inputs.inject_failure == 'website'
        run: |
          echo "::error::injected failure (inject_failure=website) — exercising the self-filing issue path, nothing dispatched"
          exit 1

      # pages.yml is path-filtered on push, so routine pushes (e.g. lib/
      # changes outside its filters) never redeploy — the daily guarantees
      # fa1.dev tracks main.
      - name: Dispatch pages.yml and watch
        id: dispatch
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Shared watcher (issues #343/#344). pages.yml takes no inputs, so
          # there is no displayTitle to disambiguate on — the watcher falls
          # back to newest-in-tight-window, and still bounds the watch
          # (cancel + one re-dispatch) instead of blocking forever.
          # Budget 75m = child worst-case 60m (#351: pages build 45 +
          # deploy 15) + 15m margin.
          rc=0
          bash scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh pages.yml \
            --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --ref main \
            --budget-seconds 4500 \
            --out-run-id run_id.txt || rc=$?
          if [ -s run_id.txt ]; then
            echo "run_url=https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/$(cat run_id.txt)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          exit "$rc"

  addin:
    name: 'Leg: Outlook add-in'
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # #351 arithmetic: child wc 45m (single office-addin-suite job) →
    # budget 60m; 150m leg ≥ 2×budget + 15m, so the second-wedge fail-fast
    # fits (the old 45m leg made the self-heal dead code).
    timeout-minutes: 150
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write
    if: >-
      (needs.plan.outputs.changed == 'true' || inputs.force == true) &&
      (inputs.legs == '' || inputs.legs == 'all' || inputs.legs == 'addin')
    outputs:
      run_url: ${{ steps.dispatch.outputs.run_url }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Inject failure (test)
        if: inputs.inject_failure == 'addin'
        run: |
          echo "::error::injected failure (inject_failure=addin) — exercising the self-filing issue path, nothing dispatched"
          exit 1

      # Acceptance suite (manifest validation, dart2js taskpane, Node +
      # Playwright e2e). The fa1.dev /outlook publish itself rides the
      # website leg — pages.yml assembles the same add-in into the deploy.
      - name: Dispatch office-addin.yml and watch
        id: dispatch
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Shared watcher (issues #343/#344). No inputs to disambiguate on
          # (newest-in-tight-window fallback), watch bounded at 60m =
          # child worst-case 45m (#351) + 15m margin.
          rc=0
          bash scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh office-addin.yml \
            --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --ref main \
            --budget-seconds 3600 \
            --out-run-id run_id.txt || rc=$?
          if [ -s run_id.txt ]; then
            echo "run_url=https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/$(cat run_id.txt)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          exit "$rc"

  # ── pub.dev leg ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # The ONLY publish path is the ci.yml tag job (pub.dev trusted publishing
  # only accepts OIDC from tag-push runs — a schedule/dispatch run can never
  # satisfy it). This leg VERIFIES pub.dev serves the pubspec version and,
  # when behind, recovers by re-running the failed tag-push publish run —
  # a rerun keeps the original push-tag event and OIDC claims, so the real
  # publish path retries. Unrecoverable states fail loudly and self-file an
  # issue with a manual-publish instruction instead of silently hanging.
  # gh-1192: a tag-publish still EXECUTING (tag pushed, ci run not visible
  # yet or queued/in_progress, tag younger than the grace window) is
  # classified «release in flight» by scripts/verify_pubdev_release.sh —
  # a neutral skip (no error, no auto-filed issue); the next scheduled
  # daily re-verifies. The 2026-10-03 collision fired the old «no ci.yml
  # run» error one minute before the healthy run completed (#1189, false
  # alarm). gh-1522: the version under test is the LATEST REMOTE TAG (the
  # committed pubspec is the 0.0.0-dev placeholder), so the «tag not cut
  # yet» state no longer exists.

  pubdev:
    name: 'Leg: pub.dev'
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write # gh run rerun of the tag-publish run
    if: >-
      (needs.plan.outputs.changed == 'true' || inputs.force == true) &&
      (inputs.legs == '' || inputs.legs == 'all' || inputs.legs == 'pubdev')
    outputs:
      status: ${{ steps.check.outputs.status }}
      pubspec_version: ${{ steps.check.outputs.pubspec }}
      published_version: ${{ steps.check.outputs.published }}
      run_url: ${{ steps.check.outputs.run_url }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Inject failure (test)
        if: inputs.inject_failure == 'pubdev'
        run: |
          echo "::error::injected failure (inject_failure=pubdev) — exercising the self-filing issue path, nothing published"
          exit 1

      # gh-1561: the never-triggered self-heal re-pushes the latest tag with
      # the fa-release-bot App token — a GITHUB_TOKEN push can never cascade
      # (gh-1172), the App's push can (the same mechanism ci.yml's release
      # job uses to cut tags). Job-scoped, expires with the job; this job's
      # own GITHUB_TOKEN stays read-scoped (job-level permissions block).
      # Shape mirrors the validator-proven precedent (ci.yml release job,
      # the create-github-app-token step): NO `if:` at all — secrets
      # context in a step-if trips GitHub's workflow validator; and a mint
      # on an unconfigured App (forks, rotation gap) fails, is SWALLOWED by
      # continue-on-error, outputs.token stays empty, and the script's
      # manual-re-push alarm fires exactly as before this change.
      # Least privilege, verified against the PINNED action (v3.2.0,
      # bcd2ba49 — review thread 10): the composite `permissions` input
      # does NOT exist there (action.yml defines only the generated
      # `permission-*` inputs — GitHub warns `Unexpected input(s)
      # 'permissions'` and the action never reads it; ci.yml:3980 rides
      # that warning). The HONORED ceiling is the granular
      # `permission-contents` input, which the action turns into the mint
      # request's permissions map: contents:write only — the tag re-push —
      # instead of the installation's full grant set. Without it the token
      # inherits every permission the fa-release-bot installation has.
      - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@64ab729a6294000f5aa4a4bc0b73d1f32bc45510 # v3.3.0
        id: app-token
        continue-on-error: true
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          permission-contents: write

      - name: Verify pub.dev serves the pubspec version
        id: check
        # gh-1192: the classification (up-to-date / release-in-flight /
        # recovered + the unchanged alarms) lives in the extracted script so
        # it is shell-harness testable (test/release_flow_race_test.dart).
        # RELEASE_APP_TOKEN is empty when the mint above skipped (App not
        # configured) — the script then fails over to the manual-re-push
        # alarm instead of attempting a re-arm.
        env:
          RELEASE_APP_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
        run: bash scripts/verify_pubdev_release.sh

  # ── Release-draft sweeper (issue #282) ────────────────────────────────────
  # Hygiene leg: no pipeline step may leave a draft release behind (the
  # 3-week-old v0.1.190 rot). The per-job guards in build-macos/build-mobile
  # own the failure path; this sweeper is the daily backstop — anything that
  # slips through (a cancelled run, a path without a guard) is deleted after
  # 24h and a deduplicated self-closing issue names the creating run so a
  # RECURRING stuck draft points at its broken step instead of rotting.
  # Runs on every daily (and manual) invocation regardless of leg results —
  # change-gating must not gate hygiene.
  sweep-drafts:
    name: Sweep stale release drafts
    needs: plan
    if: always() # even when plan failed or all legs skipped
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: write # delete draft releases
      actions: read # name each swept draft's creating run (gh run list 403s without it, review of #294)
      issues: write # deduplicated self-closing sweep issue
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Delete drafts older than 24h and file the dedup issue
        run: bash scripts/sweep_stale_drafts.sh

  # ── Report + self-healing issues ─────────────────────────────────────────
  report:
    name: Summary + self-filed issues
    needs: [plan, testflight, play, pubdev, cli, website, addin]
    if: always() # runs even when plan failed, so plan failures enter the self-healing loop too
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: read
      issues: write
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Job summary table and issue lifecycle
        env:
          NEXT_TAG: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.next_tag }}
          PLAN_RESULT: ${{ needs.plan.result }}
          DAILY_PUBLISH_ASSIGNEE: ai-teammate
          LEG_TESTFLIGHT: ${{ needs.testflight.result }}
          LEG_TESTFLIGHT_URL: ${{ needs.testflight.outputs.run_url }}
          LEG_PLAY: ${{ needs.play.result }}
          LEG_PLAY_URL: ${{ needs.play.outputs.run_url }}
          LEG_PUBDEV: ${{ needs.pubdev.result }}
          LEG_PUBDEV_STATUS: ${{ needs.pubdev.outputs.status }}
          LEG_PUBDEV_PUBSPEC: ${{ needs.pubdev.outputs.pubspec_version }}
          LEG_PUBDEV_PUBLISHED: ${{ needs.pubdev.outputs.published_version }}
          LEG_PUBDEV_URL: ${{ needs.pubdev.outputs.run_url }}
          LEG_CLI: ${{ needs.cli.result }}
          LEG_CLI_URL: ${{ needs.cli.outputs.run_url }}
          LEG_WEBSITE: ${{ needs.website.result }}
          LEG_WEBSITE_URL: ${{ needs.website.outputs.run_url }}
          LEG_ADDIN: ${{ needs.addin.result }}
          LEG_ADDIN_URL: ${{ needs.addin.outputs.run_url }}
        run: bash scripts/daily_publish_report.sh

      # gh-1478: the inject_failure TEST hook must prove the filed digest
      # QUOTES the injected ::error:: line (signal-first excerpt via the
      # per-job log endpoint), not merely that an issue exists — the #1473
      # tree-noise regression class.
      # The `!= ''` guard matters: on schedule triggers the `inputs` context
      # is EMPTY (the dispatch `default: none` does not apply), so gating
      # only on `!= 'none'` would run — and fail — this step every cron run.
      - name: Verify injected-failure excerpt (TEST)
        if: always() && inputs.inject_failure != '' && inputs.inject_failure != 'none'
        env:
          INJECTED: ${{ inputs.inject_failure }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          title="[daily-publish] ${INJECTED} leg failed"
          n=$(gh issue list --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --state open \
                --label daily-publish --limit 200 \
                --json number,title --jq '.[] | [.number, .title] | @tsv' \
                | while IFS=$'\t' read -r num t; do
                    [ "$t" = "$title" ] && echo "$num"
                  done | head -1)
          if [ -z "$n" ]; then
            echo "::error::inject_failure verify: no open issue titled '${title}' — the self-filing path regressed"
            exit 1
          fi
          text=$(gh issue view "$n" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" \
                   --json body,comments --jq '.body, (.comments[]?.body // empty)')
          if ! grep -qF "injected failure (inject_failure=${INJECTED})" <<< "$text"; then
            echo "::error::inject_failure verify: issue #${n} never quotes the injected ::error:: line — the signal-first excerpt regressed (gh-1478)"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "inject_failure verify OK: issue #${n} quotes the injected error line (gh-1478)"

Senior Developer Engineer specializing in root cause analysis and bug fixing ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Coding Guidelines — follow existing codebase patterns and conventions"] G2["Before implementing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists in project root or subdirectories → READ and FOLLOW it — it contains agent-specific instructions, coding styles, and conventions"] G4["If skills are available in the project → USE them — they provide specialized capabilities, workflows, and tool integrations"] G5["Instructions may be extended via project configuration — always follow the full set of provided instructions"] G6["Never invent new patterns when the codebase already has an established way of doing things"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 --> G5 --> G6 ``` ## input_context_reading.md ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph INPUT_ORDER["⚠️ MANDATORY: Read input files FIRST before anything else"] I0["find input/ -type f | sort — list all available files"] I1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, deployment constraints, approved frameworks"] I2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/request.md — ticket description, requirements, solution design, diagrams"] I3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — existing discussion, prior decisions, linked info"] I4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/existing_questions.json — answered questions = binding requirements"] I5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — specifications already downloaded"] I6["6️⃣ Check for images in input/TICKET/ — *.png *.jpg *.gif *.svg"] I7["7️⃣ If present: input/TICKET/parent-KEY.md — parent story summary, description, ACs"] I8["8️⃣ If present: input/TICKET/parent_context_ba.md / sa.md / vd.md — BA/SA/VD context"] I0 --> I1 --> I2 --> I3 --> I4 --> I5 --> I6 --> I7 --> I8 end subgraph CONFLUENCE_RULE["Confluence pages in input/ — READ THEM, don't re-fetch"] C1["✅ DO: read input/TICKET/confluence/PageName.md"] C2["❌ DON'T: call dmtools confluence_* to re-fetch pages already in input/"] C3["✅ DO: read image files in input/TICKET/confluence/ — they are attachments from that page"] end subgraph ATTACH_RULE["Attachments — check before fetching via API"] A1["Search glob 'input/**/*.png' and 'input/**/*.jpg' — find pre-downloaded images"] A2["If image found locally → analyze it directly, no API call needed"] A3["If attachment NOT in input/ → use dmtools confluence_get_content_attachments "] A1 --> A2 A1 -->|not found| A3 end subgraph DMTOOLS_RULE["When to use dmtools for external data"] D1["ONLY if you need data NOT already in input/"] D2["dmtools jira_get_ticket KEY, dmtools confluence_search QUERY, etc."] D3["See instructions/common/dmtools_cli.md for full reference"] end INPUT_ORDER --> CONFLUENCE_RULE --> ATTACH_RULE --> DMTOOLS_RULE ``` ## general_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD START([Bug ticket ready for fix]) --> READ["⚠️ MANDATORY: Read ALL input files FIRST — see instructions/common/input_context_reading.md"] READ --> RETURNED{Ticket returned to development?} RETURNED -->|Yes| PREV["Review previous PR diff and QA feedback in comments.md"] PREV --> RCA_RET["Write/Update RCA explaining why previous fix failed — see output_rules.md for rca.md format"] RETURNED -->|No| RCA_FRESH["Write fresh RCA from ticket description and linked_tests.md"] RCA_RET --> REPRO RCA_FRESH --> REPRO["Write a unit test that reproduces the bug. Run it — it MUST FAIL"] REPRO --> EXISTS{Test fails?} EXISTS -->|No| ALREADY["Check git history, current code, and linked tests.
⚠️ If linked test exists: verify it passes AND the test was created/updated BEFORE the fix commit — not after.
If bug is genuinely fixed — write outputs/already_fixed.json and stop"] ALREADY --> END_FIXED([End — bug already fixed]) EXISTS -->|Yes| BLOCKED{Fix requires external decision, secrets, or infra changes?} BLOCKED -->|Yes| BLOCK["Write outputs/blocked.json and stop — see output_rules.md"] BLOCK --> END_BLOCKED([End — blocked awaiting human input]) BLOCKED -->|No| FIX["Make minimum targeted fix for the root cause ONLY"] FIX --> VERIFY["Run reproduction test (must PASS) and full test suite (no regressions)"] VERIFY --> PASS{All tests pass?} PASS -->|No| ADJUST["Adjust fix and re-run tests"] ADJUST --> VERIFY PASS -->|Yes| GITSTATUS["Run git status and review every new/modified file"] GITSTATUS --> SECRETS{Sensitive or untracked non-code files present?} SECRETS -->|Yes| IGNORE["Add appropriate patterns to .gitignore"] SECRETS -->|No| SUMMARY["Write concise bug fix summary to outputs/response.md — see output_rules.md"] IGNORE --> SUMMARY SUMMARY --> END([End — post-processing handles git/PR]) ``` ## Returning from test-automation failure When this Bug has been sent back to development because a linked Test Case failed: 1. Read the `Failed Reason` field of every linked Test Case. 2. If the failure is caused by a missing token, missing permission, missing secret, or any other access/credential/infra issue that you cannot fix in product code, write `outputs/blocked.json` and stop. Do **not** try to code a fix for an access problem. 3. Only attempt a product-code fix when the failure is a genuine product regression. ## tdd_approach.md ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph TDD["TDD for Bug Fixes — RED-GREEN-REFACTOR"] T0["Start with a clear understanding of the bug from RCA"] T1["RED: Write a unit test that REPRODUCES the bug
— must describe the exact failure scenario
— run it to confirm it FAILS"] T2["GREEN: Write minimum fix to make the reproduction test PASS
— simplest possible change
— do not refactor unrelated code"] T3["REFACTOR: Clean up while keeping tests GREEN
— improve naming, remove duplication
— run full suite after every change"] T4{"More edge cases to cover?"} T5["Repeat RED-GREEN-REFACTOR for next edge case"] T0 --> T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 T4 -->|Yes| T5 --> T1 T4 -->|No| DONE([Bug fixed with regression tests]) end subgraph RULES["Bug TDD Rules"] R1["❌ NEVER fix code without a failing reproduction test first"] R2["❌ NEVER write more code than needed to fix the bug"] R3["✅ Returned bugs: your fix must differ from the previous attempt"] R4["✅ If the bug involves a loop/collection, add a reproduction case with 2+ items, not only a single-item scenario — a single-item test can pass while multi-item logic is still broken"] R5["✅ Run the FULL test suite before finishing — no regressions allowed"] end TDD --> RULES ``` ## output_rules.md ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph OUTPUTS["Required outputs for bug development"] O1["outputs/rca.md — write FIRST, update as you learn"] O2["outputs/already_fixed.json — only if bug is genuinely fixed in current code AND tests pass"] O3["outputs/blocked.json — only if fix requires external input/credentials/infra"] O4["outputs/response.md — concise PR description (see formatting_rules.md)"] end subgraph RCA["rca.md format"] R1["## Root Cause Analysis"] R2["**Bug**: one-sentence description"] R3["**Root cause**: exact technical reason — file, function, line"] R4["**Impact**: what is broken and under what conditions"] R5["**Fix approach**: what needs to change and why"] R6["**Previous attempt**: PR #, what changed, why insufficient (only if returned bug)"] R1…
Let me start by reading the input files as mandated by the instructions.

blocks.text:
# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +

blocks.text:
# Daily auto-publish (issue #161): thin orchestrator over the existing
# publish channels. Each channel is an isolated leg — one leg failing never
# kills the others — and every failure self-files a deduplicated GitHub
# issue (label `bug`, assigned to the owner) that auto-closes when the leg
# goes green again. No publish logic is duplicated here: legs dispatch the
# existing workflows via `gh workflow run` and watch them.
#
#   testflight  build-mobile.yml   ios_content=all (the iOS half of the
#                                 mobile build)
#   play        build-mobile.yml   android_content=all,
#                                 android_track=beta (Android external
#                                 beta / open testing — issue #289 lifts
#                                 the standing "Android excluded" owner
#                                 decision for the release track; #947
#                                 adds the listing deploy — texts +
#                                 whole-set image replace + verify — so
#                                 the listing never trails the goldens;
#                                 the leg green-skips while the Play
#                                 secrets are absent)
#   pubdev      in-job OIDC publish, only when pubspec > pub.dev; otherwise
#               a green up-to-date check. The tag-time OIDC publish job
#               (ci.yml) stays the primary path; this leg is the catch-up +
#               loud-failure detector (e.g. expired publish credentials)
#   cli         build-macos.yml    desktop DMG + macOS CLI bundles +
#                                 extension, attached to the next-tag
#                                 release (version passed explicitly so
#                                 mobile/desktop never mint diverging tags)
#   website     pages.yml          fa1.dev (landing + web demo +
#                                 the /outlook add-in slice; gh-1684:
#                                 the extension zip moved to GitHub
#                                 Releases and is no longer site-hosted)
#   addin       office-addin.yml   manifest/taskpane acceptance suite; the
#                                 fa1.dev publish itself rides the website
#                                 leg (pages.yml assembles /outlook)
#
# Legs run only when main moved since the last GREEN daily run — skip-no-
# change is green-neutral, never red (#159 lesson). One exception (gh-1192):
# while main's pubspec version is not yet served by pub.dev the plan gate
# (scripts/daily_plan.sh) forces the legs anyway — a release-in-flight
# green must not become a skip baseline that stalls re-verification and
# rerun-recovery on a quiet main. Versioning stays the
# existing scheme: auto_release.sh patch-bumps + tags every main push
# (2h coalesce); the daily attaches mobile/desktop artifacts to the next
# tag and verifies/republishes pub.dev. See docs/ci.md.
#
# Pause: gh workflow disable daily-publish.yml -R IstiN/flutter_agent_harness

name: Daily auto-publish

run-name: "Daily auto-publish (${{ inputs.legs || 'all' }})"

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '17 5 * * *' # once daily, 05:17 UTC
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      legs:
        description: 'Leg(s) to run'
        type: choice
        default: all
        options:
          - all
          - testflight
          - play
          - pubdev
          - cli
          - website
          - addin
      force:
        description: 'Run even if main has not moved since the last green daily'
        type: boolean
        default: false
      inject_failure:
        description: 'TEST ONLY — fail this leg before any dispatch, to exercise the self-filing issue cycle'
        type: choice
        default: none
        options:
          - none
          - testflight
          - play
          - pubdev
          - cli
          - website
          - addin

permissions:
  contents: read

# One daily at a time; a queued run must not cancel an in-flight one.
concurrency:
  group: daily-publish
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  plan:
    name: Plan (change detection + versions)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # gh-1477: 10m was the same time bomb as the derive-version jobs — a
    # full-history fetch under a 10m ceiling. 20m + the blobless filter
    # below.
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: read
    outputs:
      changed: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.changed }}
      next_tag: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.next_tag }}
      latest_tag: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.latest_tag }}
      pubspec_version: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.pubspec_version }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # gh-1477: daily_plan.sh reads tags / commit metadata / one file
          # at origin/main — never historical blobs. Blobless keeps full
          # tag/commit metadata without the blobs (the full fetch outgrew
          # the old 10m ceiling in the twin derive-version job, run
          # 38027695551).
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none

      - name: Detect main movement and derive versions
        id: plan
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          FORCE: ${{ inputs.force }}
        # gh-1192: the gate (baseline + the release-unresolved re-arm that
        # keeps AC1's «the next daily re-verifies» true on a quiet main)
        # lives in the extracted script — shell-harness tested by
        # test/release_flow_race_test.dart.
        run: bash scripts/daily_plan.sh

  # ── Dispatch legs ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Shape per leg: dispatch the child workflow pinned to main, capture the
  # new run id, watch it, fail on any non-success conclusion. The child run
  # URL is exported even on failure so the report can excerpt its log.
  #
  # ── Timeout arithmetic (#351) ────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Invariants: watch budget > child worst-case (a legitimate slow child is
  # NEVER cancelled by the watcher — that was the #351 bug), leg
  # timeout > budget (the watcher, including its one cancel + re-dispatch
  # cycle, always outlives the child), and where the math fits under
  # GitHub's 360m job cap, leg timeout ≥ 2×budget + ~15m so the SECOND
  # wedge's fail-fast can actually fire inside the leg.
  #
  # Child worst-case = sum of the serialized job timeout-minutes along the
  # child's critical path (every job in a watched chain carries an explicit
  # timeout for exactly this). Margin = appear window (60×10s) + cancel
  # wait (180s) + poll slack ≈ 15m.
  #
  #   leg        child worst-case (serialized chain)          budget    leg timeout
  #   testflight version 20 → build-ios 90 → submit-ios 120   230m  →  250m (15000s) ; 360m
  #             (∥ release-mobile 15, covered by the max)
  #   play       version 20 → build-android 45 →              95m   →  110m (6600s) ; 240m
  #             submit-android 30 (∥ release-mobile 15)
  #   cli        version 20 → build-macos 150×2 (arm64 +      335m  →  350m (21000s) ; 360m
  #             x86_64 SERIALIZE on the single self-hosted
  #             runner) → release-macos 15
  #             (∥ cli matrix 45, extension 30 — shorter paths)
  #   (gh-1477: the version/plan jobs' ceiling moved 10 → 20m — a
  #   full-history fetch outgrew the 10m bomb; the fetch is now blobless
  #   and 20m is the seatbelt. Worst-cases and budgets grew by exactly
  #   the +10m.)
  #   website    pages build 45 → deploy 15                   60m   →   75m (4500s)  ; 180m
  #   addin      office-addin-suite 45 (single job)           45m   →   60m (3600s)  ; 150m
  #
  # Second-wedge headroom (2×budget + ~15m vs leg timeout): play 235 ≤
  # 240 ✓, website 163 ≤ 180 ✓, addin 133 ≤ 150 ✓. testflight (515 > 360)
  # and cli (715 > 360) CANNOT fit two full budgets under GitHub's 360m
  # job cap — their first wedge still self-heals (cancel at budget +
  # re-dispatch ≈ budget+13m), and a second wedge is bounded by the leg
  # timeout instead of the watcher's fail-fast; both children carry
  # per-job server-side timeouts (#344) so a wedged job self-fails even
  # without the watch…
