IOS_LIVE_ACTIVITY_PROFILE_NAME="$LA_PROFILE_NAME" \
          IOS_SIGNING_IDENTITY="iPhone Distribution" \
          bundle exec fastlane ios build_only

      # gh-1692 AC2: the gym log holds the REAL xcodebuild error — without
      # this artifact an archive failure was undiagnosable from GitHub (the
      # log lived only ON the runner; xcpretty printed no error line). The
      # lane also dumps the newest log tail into the job log on failure;
      # this artifact is the full-fidelity copy. Failure-gated so green
      # runs upload nothing.
      - name: Upload gym logs on archive failure (gh-1692)
        if: failure()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: ios-gym-logs
          path: ~/Library/Logs/gym/
          retention-days: 14

      # #1331 size diet: the exported IPA ships ~99 MB (uncompressed) of
      # debug dSYMs under Symbols/. App Store Connect strips that directory
      # from device delivery anyway (TestFlight reports ~157 MB — the
      # payload WITHOUT Symbols), so it is dead weight in the artifact.
      # Repack without it: Payload/ is untouched (codesign validity lives
      # inside the bundle), zip -y preserves the framework symlinks so the
      # manifest shape is unchanged. Idempotent — a future export that
      # omits Symbols/ skips straight through.
      - name: Strip debug symbols from IPA (#1331)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          IPA_PATH=$(find flutter_app/build/ios -name "*.ipa" -type f | head -1)
          if [ -z "$IPA_PATH" ]; then
            echo "::error::IPA file not found in flutter_app/build/ios"
            exit 1
          fi
          # gh-1403: absolutize BEFORE the rezip — find yields a RELATIVE
          # path, and the `(cd "$STRIP" && …)` subshell resolved
          # "$IPA_PATH.stripped" against the mktemp dir (no flutter_app/
          # ancestor) → "zip error: Could not create output file". The
          # atomic-swap mv below carried the same hazard.
          # (realpath: /usr/bin/realpath, macOS 13+ — the runner is newer.)
          IPA_PATH=$(realpath "$IPA_PATH")
          if ! unzip -l "$IPA_PATH" "Symbols/*" | grep -q "Symbols/"; then
            echo "no Symbols/ in the IPA — nothing to strip"
            exit 0
          fi
          STRIP=$(mktemp -d)
          trap 'rm -rf "$STRIP"' EXIT
          unzip -q "$IPA_PATH" -d "$STRIP"
          rm -rf "$STRIP/Symbols"
          BEFORE=$(stat -f%z "$IPA_PATH")
          # Atomic swap: the original IPA survives a failed rezip (the
          # un-stripped copy still beats no artifact for debugging).
          (cd "$STRIP" && find . -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -exec zip -qyr9 "$IPA_PATH.stripped" {} +)
          mv -f "$IPA_PATH.stripped" "$IPA_PATH"
          AFTER=$(stat -f%z "$IPA_PATH")
          echo "IPA stripped: $BEFORE -> $AFTER bytes ($((BEFORE - AFTER)) saved compressed)"

      - name: Upload IPA Artifact
        # Uploaded before the symbol gate so a failed gate still leaves the
        # IPA available for debugging.
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: ios-ipa
          path: flutter_app/build/ios/ipa/*.ipa
          retention-days: 14

      # #1331 ratchet: per-file uncompressed floor seeded from the last
      # release-shape CI artifact (run 37495702186 fa.ipa) with the diet
      # applied. Growth >5% on any line or TOTAL fails the leg — same gate
      # family as the macOS pass (#1227). Eviction is pinned separately by
      # the --forbid deny-list: the NEW-line guard alone only catches
      # re-adds above 5% of TOTAL (Symbols/ qualifies at 99 MB; the 5.6 MB
      # glb does not — +3.8% TOTAL, sub-share NEW), so a returning evicted
      # artifact fails via --forbid in the same step. Also pins the owner
      # hard constraint: the js-apps WASM runtime and LiteRT LM always ship.
      - name: Size manifest ratchet + wasm keep-set (#1331)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          IPA_PATH=$(find flutter_app/build/ios -name "*.ipa" -type f | head -1)
          MANIFEST=$(mktemp)
          trap 'rm -f "$MANIFEST"' EXIT
          python3 scripts/size_manifest.py check "$IPA_PATH" \
            --baseline scripts/size_budget/fa-ios.tsv \
            --forbid '^Symbols/' --forbid 'coach_anny\.glb$' \
            --manifest-out "$MANIFEST"
          for ASSET in \
            flutter_assets/assets/wasm/python.wasm \
            flutter_assets/assets/wasm/qjs.wasm \
            flutter_assets/assets/wasm/coreutils.wasm \
            flutter_assets/assets/wasm/lua.wasm; do
            grep -q "$ASSET" "$MANIFEST" || {
              echo "::error::$ASSET missing from the IPA — the js-apps WASM runtime must always ship (owner directive, #1331)"
              exit 1
            }
          done
          grep -q "LiteRtLm.framework/LiteRtLm" "$MANIFEST" || {
            echo "::error::LiteRtLm.framework missing from the IPA — on-device LLM stack must always ship (owner directive, #1331)"
            exit 1
          }
          echo "✅ wasm runtime + LiteRT keep-set present; iOS size ratchet green"

      - name: Verify IPA and FFI symbols
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          IPA_PATH=$(find flutter_app/build/ios -name "*.ipa" -type f | head -1)
          if [ -z "$IPA_PATH" ]; then
            echo "::error::IPA file not found in flutter_app/build/ios"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "IPA built successfully: $(ls -la "$IPA_PATH")"

          # The Dart side resolves the wasm_run FFI surface via dlsym on the
          # main executable. If the symbols were dead-stripped or not exported
          # the app boots to a white screen on TestFlight — fail here instead.
          CHECK_DIR=$(mktemp -d)
          unzip -q "$IPA_PATH" -d "$CHECK_DIR"
          PLIST=$(echo "$CHECK_DIR"/Payload/*.app/Info.plist)
          EXEC_NAME=$(plutil -extract CFBundleExecutable raw "$PLIST")
          BIN="$(dirname "$PLIST")/$EXEC_NAME"
          # dyld_info reads the exports trie, which survives stripping
          # (nm -gD fails on stripped binaries with "no dynamic symbol table").
          EXPORTS=$(xcrun dyld_info -exports "$BIN" 2>/dev/null || true)
          WIRE_COUNT=$(echo "$EXPORTS" | grep -c " _wire_" || true)
          echo "wasm_run wire_* exports in binary: $WIRE_COUNT"
          for SYM in _wire_compile_wasm _store_dart_post_cobject _init_frb_dart_api_dl; do
            if ! echo "$EXPORTS" | grep -qE " ${SYM}\$"; then
              echo "::error::$SYM is not exported from the app binary — wasm_run would crash at runtime (white screen)"
              exit 1
            fi
          done
          echo "✅ wasm_run FFI symbols are exported"

          # cupertino_http trampolines (_NativeCupertinoHttp_*) live in a
          # static pod framework nothing native references; without the
          # Podfile force_load the Release link drops them and every network
          # call fails at runtime ('No asset with id package:cupertino_http/
          # src/native_cupertino_bindings.dart found'). Gate on it here so a
          # broken IPA never reaches TestFlight again.
          CUPERTINO_COUNT=$(echo "$EXPORTS" | grep -c " __NativeCupertinoHttp_" || true)
          echo "cupertino_http _NativeCupertinoHttp_* exports in binary: $CUPERTINO_COUNT"
          if [ "$CUPERTINO_COUNT" -eq 0 ]; then
            echo "::error::no _NativeCupertinoHttp_* symbols exported from the app binary — networking via NSURLSession would fail at runtime"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "✅ cupertino_http FFI symbols are exported"
          rm -rf "$CHECK_DIR"

      - name: Cleanup
        if: always()
        run: |
          security delete-keychain build.keychain || true
          rm -f certificate.p12

  submit-ios:
    name: Submit iOS to TestFlight
    needs: [build-ios]
    # gh-1600 F-A + gh-1692: same runner-name pin as build-ios above — the
    # generic [self-hosted, macOS, ARM64] list also matched the Linux box,
    # and `macos-m5` alone is a coin flip between fa-m5-1 (good) and
    # fa-m5-2 (broken signing env).
    runs-on: [self-hosted, macos-m5, fa-m5-1]
    # Issue #344 wedge bound + #351 arithmetic: the submit_only lane waits
    # for Apple processing (TESTFLIGHT_WAIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, default 5400s
    # = 90m — a healthy slow ASC processing is NOT a wedge); distribution
    # appearance is verified by the DEFERRED store-appearance-check
    # workflow (gh-1041 — a single non-failing probe runs after the upload,
    # the 900s wait-loop is gone). Job ceiling must exceed the lane worst
    # case:
    #   ~5m setup (mirror clone + artifact + bundle install)
    # + ~10m IPA upload to ASC
    # + 90m wait_processing_timeout_duration
    # + ~1m one-shot appearance probe
    # = 120m. The old 45m killed healthy slow submits mid-wait (the exact
    # failure #351 was filed for); a genuinely wedged job is still bounded
    # server-side at 120m, and the daily testflight watch budget (240m)
    # covers the whole version→build-ios(90)→submit-ios(120) chain.
    timeout-minutes: 120
    if: needs.build-ios.result == 'success'
    steps:
      - name: Update local git mirror
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          MIRROR="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/mirror/flutter_agent_harness.git"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$MIRROR")"
          # gh-1644: shared resilient updater — fetch retries + blobless
          # recreate with partial-dir cleanup (was single-shot; run
          # 38855793382 died exit 128 on a mid-clone network drop).
          # gh-1665 review: first step of the job, before any checkout —
          # the workspace may hold a pre-merge tree, so bootstrap the
          # script from the commit-pinned raw URL (mirror copy as the
          # no-network fallback), never from $GITHUB_WORKSPACE.
          SCRIPT="$RUNNER_TEMP/update_git_mirror.sh"
          RAW="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/${{ github.sha }}/scripts/update_git_mirror.sh"
          if ! curl -fsSL --retry 5 --retry-all-errors --retry-delay 5 "$RAW" -o "$SCRIPT" \
             || [ ! -s "$SCRIPT" ]; then
            echo "raw bootstrap failed — syncing the mirror and falling back to its copy" >&2
            # gh-1665 review (returned IMPORTANT): in the one-run-wide
            # first-post-merge window the persistent mirror is still a
            # PRE-MERGE tree. Cheap single-shot ensure (bounded resilience
            # stays owned by $SCRIPT below) so the extraction that follows
            # succeeds on any runner that can reach github.com at all —
            # raw.githubusercontent.com being down degrades to the
            # fallback instead of a red leg.
            if [ -d "$MIRROR" ] && git -C "$MIRROR" rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              git -C "$MIRROR" fetch origin || true
            else
              rm -rf "$MIRROR"
              git clone --mirror https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$MIRROR" || true
            fi
            BRANCH="$(git --git-dir="$MIRROR" symbolic-ref --short HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo main)"
            git --git-dir="$MIRROR" show "$BRANCH:scripts/update_git_mirror.sh" > "$SCRIPT" \
              || { echo "::error::could not bootstrap update_git_mirror.sh (raw URL unreachable and mirror lacks the script)" >&2; exit 1; }
          fi
          bash "$SCRIPT" \
            https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$MIRROR"

      # gh-1600 AC2: hardened mirror-checkout (see build-ios) — the bare
      # workspace rm -rf must never fail this checkout on stale unremovable
      # leftovers in the persistent shared workspace. INLINE (not a composite
      # action) on purpose: local `uses: ./...` actions resolve against
      # $GITHUB_WORKSPACE at step time — on this box that is the PREVIOUS
      # run's tree, and this step IS the checkout.
      - name: Checkout repository from local mirror
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          MIRROR="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/mirror/flutter_agent_harness.git"
          cd /tmp
          echo "GITHUB_WORKSPACE=$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          echo "MIRROR=$MIRROR"

          if ! rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE not fully removable — stale paths held by another process (gh-1600); pruning what is removable"
            rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" || true
          fi
          if [ -d "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" ] && [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
            # gh-1600 rework (review thread): best-effort prune of previous
            # sidecars BEFORE creating a new one — the containers that held
            # them may have died since, so the retry often succeeds. On
            # this persistent box the runner's own _temp cleanup cannot
            # remove mount-held content either; without the prune every
            # degraded checkout would leave another timestamped dir behind
            # (unbounded growth until manual cleanup).
            rm -rf "${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}"/stale-workspace-* 2>/dev/null || true
            STALE="${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/stale-workspace-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
            echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE still non-empty after prune — moving the remainder to $STALE (gh-1600)"
            mkdir -p "$(dirname "$STALE")" 2>/dev/null || true
            if ! mv "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" "$STALE" 2>/dev/null; then
              echo "::warning::$GITHUB_WORKSPACE could not be moved aside either — cloning around the stub (gh-1600)"
            fi
          fi
          mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"

          CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          if [ -n "$(ls -A "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
            CLONE_TARGET="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE.checkout"
            rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
          fi

          # the runner's flaky link — the 10-16 submit leg died on "2876
          # bytes of body are still expected" (exit 128) with NO retry and
          # cost a whole TestFlight day. Bounded retry; a failed attempt
          # leaves a partial dir at $CLONE_TARGET which git refuses to
          # clone into, so it is removed before the next attempt.
          CLONE_RETRIES=3
          for attempt in $(seq 1 "$CLONE_RETRIES"); do
            if git clone --reference "$MIRROR" --depth=1 \
              https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$CLONE_TARGET"; then
              break
            fi
            echo "git clone attempt ${attempt}/${CLONE_RETRIES} failed" >&2
            if [ "$attempt" -eq "$CLONE_RETRIES" ]; then
              echo "::error::git clone from origin failed after ${CLONE_RETRIES} attempts (gh-1692 AC3)" >&2

              name="$(basename "$entry")"

                # gh-1600 rework (review thread): fresh content must win —
                # park the stale stub in the same $STALE sidecar and move
                # the fresh entry in. The old path skipped the fresh entry
                # (warning-only) and the trailing rm -rf "$CLONE_TARGET"
                # then DELETED it, silently keeping the stale leftover at
                # that repo path. Skip-with-warning remains only as the
                # last-resort fallback when even parking the stub fails.
                STALE_DIR="${STALE:-${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/stale-workspace-sidecar}"

      - name: Setup environment (self-hosted)
        run: |
          echo "/opt/homebrew/opt/ruby/bin" >> $GITHUB_PATH
          echo "/opt/homebrew/bin" >> $GITHUB_PATH

      - name: Download IPA artifact
        uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          name: ios-ipa

        run: bundle install

      - name: Upload IPA to TestFlight
        working-directory: flutter_app

          APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_CONTENT: ${{ secrets.APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_CONTENT }}

          # loudly when these are unset — set them once as repo variables.
          TESTFLIGHT_EXTERNAL_GROUP: ${{ vars.TESTFLIGHT_EXTERNAL_GROUP }}
          BETA_APP_FEEDBACK_EMAIL: ${{ vars.BETA_APP_FEEDBACK_EMAIL }}
          BETA_REVIEW_CONTACT_EMAIL: ${{ vars.BETA_REVIEW_CONTACT_EMAIL }}
          BETA_REVIEW_CONTACT_PHONE: ${{ vars.BETA_REVIEW_CONTACT_PHONE }}

            exit 0

  release-mobile:
    name: Create Mobile GitHub Release
    needs: [version, build-android, build-android-apks, build-ios]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Ceiling for the daily watchers' budget arithmetic (#351).
    timeout-minutes: 15
    if: |
      always() &&
      ((needs.build-android.result == 'success' || needs.build-android.result == 'skipped') ||
       (needs.build-android-apks.result == 'success' || needs.build-android-apks.result == 'skipped')) &&
      (needs.build-ios.result == 'success' || needs.build-ios.result == 'skipped')
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - name: Nothing to release
        # Both platforms picked a no-binary content mode (none /
        # metadata_only / screenshots_only) — nothing was built, so there
        # is nothing to download or release. Record it in the job summary
        # and skip every release step instead of failing on `ls artifacts/`.
        if: needs.build-android.result != 'success' && needs.build-android-apks.result != 'success' && needs.build-ios.result != 'success'
        run: |
          {
            echo '### Nothing to release'
            echo '`android_content` and `ios_content` both selected no binary build (none / metadata_only / screenshots_only) — no release created.'
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      - name: Checkout repository
        if: needs.build-android.result == 'success' || needs.build-android-apks.result == 'success' || needs.build-ios.result == 'success'
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # Full history: release_notes.sh falls back to "commits since the
          # previous tag" when the CHANGELOG has no section for this version.
          # gh-1477: blobless — the notes read commit MESSAGES, never
          # historical file blobs.
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none

      - name: Download iOS IPA artifact
        if: needs.build-ios.result == 'success'
        uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          name: ios-ipa
          path: artifacts/

      - name: Download Android AAB artifact
        if: needs.build-android.result == 'success'
        uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          name: android-aab
          path: artifacts/

      - name: Download store APK artifact
        if: needs.build-android-apks.result == 'success'
        uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          name: android-apk-store
          path: artifacts/

      - name: Download god APK artifact
        if: needs.build-android-apks.result == 'success'
        uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          name: android-apk-god
          path: artifacts/

      - name: List downloaded artifacts
        if: needs.build-android.result == 'success' || needs.build-android-apks.result == 'success' || needs.build-ios.result == 'success'
        run: ls -laR artifacts/

      - name: Create or update GitHub Release
        if: needs.build-android.result == 'success' || needs.build-android-apks.result == 'success' || needs.build-ios.result == 'success'
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ needs.version.outputs.tag }}
          VERSION: ${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          AAB=$(find artifacts -name "*.aab" -type f | head -1)
          IPA=$(find artifacts -name "*.ipa" -type f | head -1)
          STORE_APK=$(find artifacts -name "app-store-release.apk" -type f | head -1)
          GOD_APK=$(find artifacts -name "app-god-release.apk" -type f | head -1)
          echo "AAB: $AAB"
          echo "IPA: $IPA"
          echo "store APK: $STORE_APK"
          echo "god APK: $GOD_APK"

          ASSETS=()
          [ -n "$AAB" ] && ASSETS+=("$AAB")
          [ -n "$IPA" ] && ASSETS+=("$IPA")
          [ -n "$STORE_APK" ] && ASSETS+=("$STORE_APK")
          [ -n "$GOD_APK" ] && ASSETS+=("$GOD_APK")

          # Notes come from the CHANGELOG section for this version, with a
          # conventional-commit fallback (issue #282: no more filler
          # bodies); the install hints stay as a footer.
          bash scripts/release_notes.sh "$RELEASE_TAG" > release-notes.md || true
          printf '\n## Installation\n- **Android**: Download the AAB and upload to Play Store, or use `flutter install`.\n- **Android god flavor (sideload only)**: install the god APK directly — see https://fa1.dev/android.\n- **iOS**: Download the IPA and upload to TestFlight via Xcode or Transporter.\n- **macOS**: Download the DMG from the macOS build workflow.\n' >> release-notes.md

          # Attach-or-create (issue #282 E3 + review of #294): idempotent
          # against the view->create race - a lost race uploads into the
          # winner's release instead of failing - and the create stamps an
          # ownership marker into the draft body, so the guard step below
          # only ever deletes THIS job's draft, never the macOS leg's
          # mid-upload draft on the same derived tag.
          bash scripts/release_attach_or_create.sh "$RELEASE_TAG" "${ASSETS[@]}"

      # Draft lifecycle invariant (issue #282): the create above uploads
      # assets through a draft — a failed/cancelled run must delete it,
      # never orphan it (the v0.1.190 rot). Ownership-scoped (review of
      # #294): the guard deletes only a draft whose body carries THIS
      # run+job's marker — a sibling leg's draft is never touched.
      - name: Draft lifecycle guard (delete orphaned draft on failure)
        if: >-
          always() && job.status != 'success' &&
          (needs.build-android.result == 'success' || needs.build-android-apks.result == 'success' || needs.build-ios.result == 'success')
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ needs.version.outputs.tag }}
        run: bash scripts/release_draft_guard.sh "$RELEASE_TAG"

Run it — it MUST FAIL"] REPRO --> EXISTS{Test fails?} EXISTS -->|No| ALREADY["Check git history, current code, and linked tests.

If bug is genuinely fixed — write outputs/already_fixed.json and stop"] ALREADY --> END_FIXED([End — bug already fixed]) EXISTS -->|Yes| BLOCKED{Fix requires external decision, secrets, or infra changes?} BLOCKED -->|Yes| BLOCK["Write outputs/blocked.json and stop — see output_rules.md"] BLOCK --> END_BLOCKED([End — blocked awaiting human input]) BLOCKED -->|No| FIX["Make minimum targeted fix for the root cause ONLY"] FIX --> VERIFY["Run reproduction test (must PASS) and full test suite (no regressions)"] VERIFY --> PASS{All tests pass?} PASS -->|No| ADJUST["Adjust fix and re-run tests"] ADJUST --> VERIFY PASS -->|Yes| GITSTATUS["Run git status and review every new/modified file"] GITSTATUS --> SECRETS{Sensitive or untracked non-code files present?} SECRETS -->|Yes| IGNORE["Add appropriate patterns to .gitignore"] SECRETS -->|No| SUMMARY["Write concise bug fix summary to outputs/response.md — see output_rules.md"] IGNORE --> SUMMARY SUMMARY --> END([End — post-processing handles git/PR]) ``` ## Returning from test-automation failure When this Bug has been sent back to development because a linked Test Case failed: 1. blocks.text:
# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

blocks.text:
# Daily auto-publish (issue #161): thin orchestrator over the existing
# publish channels. Each channel is an isolated leg — one leg failing never
# kills the others — and every failure self-files a deduplicated GitHub
# issue (label `bug`, assigned to the owner) that auto-closes when the leg
# goes green again. No publish logic is duplicated here: legs dispatch the
# existing workflows via `gh workflow run` and watch them.
#
#   testflight  build-mobile.yml   ios_content=all (the iOS half of the
#                                 mobile build)
#   play        build-mobile.yml   android_content=all,
#                                 android_track=beta (Android external
#                                 beta / open testing — issue #289 lifts
#                                 the standing "Android excluded" owner
#                                 decision for the release track; #947
#                                 adds the listing deploy — texts +
#                                 whole-set image replace + verify — so
#                                 the listing never trails the goldens;
#                                 the leg green-skips while the Play
#                                 secrets are absent)
#   pubdev      in-job OIDC publish, only when pubspec > pub.dev; otherwise
#               a green up-to-date check. The tag-time OIDC publish job
#               (ci.yml) stays the primary path; this leg is the catch-up +
#               loud-failure detector (e.g. expired publish credentials)
#   cli         build-macos.yml    desktop DMG + macOS CLI bundles +
#                                 extension, attached to the next-tag
#                                 release (version passed explicitly so
#                                 mobile/desktop never mint diverging tags)
#   website     pages.yml          fa1.dev (landing + web demo +
#                                 the /outlook add-in slice; gh-1684:
#                                 the extension zip moved to GitHub
#                                 Releases and is no longer site-hosted)
#   addin       office-addin.yml   manifest/taskpane acceptance suite; the
#                                 fa1.dev publish itself rides the website
#                                 leg (pages.yml assembles /outlook)
#
# Legs run only when main moved since the last GREEN daily run — skip-no-
# change is green-neutral, never red (#159 lesson). One exception (gh-1192):
# while main's pubspec version is not yet served by pub.dev the plan gate
# (scripts/daily_plan.sh) forces the legs anyway — a release-in-flight
# green must not become a skip baseline that stalls re-verification and
# rerun-recovery on a quiet main. Versioning stays the
# existing scheme: auto_release.sh patch-bumps + tags every main push
# (2h coalesce); the daily attaches mobile/desktop artifacts to the next
# tag and verifies/republishes pub.dev. See docs/ci.md.
#
# Pause: gh workflow disable daily-publish.yml -R IstiN/flutter_agent_harness

name: Daily auto-publish

run-name: "Daily auto-publish (${{ inputs.legs || 'all' }})"

on:

      # inside the bundle), zip -y preserves the framework symlinks so the
      # manifest shape is unchanged. Idempotent — a future export that
      # omits Symbols/ skips straight through.
      - name: Strip debug symbols from IPA (#1331)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          IPA_PATH=$(find flutter_app/build/ios -name "*.ipa" -type f | head -1)
          if [ -z "$IPA_PATH" ]; then
            echo "::error::IPA file not found in flutter_app/build/ios"
            exit 1
          fi
          # gh-1403: absolutize BEFORE the rezip — find yields a RELATIVE
          # path, and the `(cd "$STRIP" && …)` subshell resolved
          # "$IPA_PATH.stripped" against the mktemp dir (no flutter_app/
          # ancestor) → "zip error: Could not create output file". The
          # atomic-swap mv below carried the same hazard.
          # (realpath: /usr/bin/realpath, macOS 13+ — the runner is newer.)
          IPA_PATH=$(realpath "$IPA_PATH")
          if ! unzip -l "$IPA_PATH" "Symbols/*" | grep -q "Symbols/"; then
            echo "no Symbols/ in the IPA — nothing to strip"
            exit 0
          fi
          STRIP=$(mktemp -d)
          trap 'rm -rf "$STRIP"' EXIT
          unzip -q "$IPA_PATH" -d "$STRIP"
          rm -rf "$STRIP/Symbols"
          BEFORE=$(stat -f%z "$IPA_PATH")
          # Atomic swap: the original IPA survives a failed rezip (the
          # un-stripped copy still beats no artifact for debugging).
          (cd "$STRIP" && find . -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -exec zip -qyr9 "$IPA_PATH.stripped" {} +)
          mv -f "$IPA_PATH.stripped" "$IPA_PATH"
          AFTER=$(stat -f%z "$IPA_PATH")
          echo "IPA stripped: $BEFORE -> $AFTER bytes ($((BEFORE - AFTER)) saved compressed)"

      - name: Upload IPA Artifact

#   PLAN_RESULT         needs.plan.result — a plan failure files its own issue
#   LEG_<NAME>          needs result: success | failure | skipped | cancelled
#   LEG_<NAME>_URL      child run URL (empty on internal/skip paths)
#   LEG_PUBDEV_*        status (up-to-date/private/recovered/release-in-flight),
#                       versions, tag-run URL
#   NEXT_TAG            estimated next tag (informational; legs derive latest+1 themselves)
#   GITHUB_RUN_ID, GITHUB_REPOSITORY, GITHUB_SERVER_URL   runner defaults
#
# Exits non-zero when any leg failed or was cancelled (the daily run goes
# red too); all-skipped stays green (#159 lesson).
set -euo pipefail

repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"
daily_url="${GITHUB_SERVER_URL}/${repo}/actions/runs/${GITHUB_RUN_ID}"
assignee="${DAILY_PUBLISH_ASSIGNEE:-ai-teammate}"
next_tag="${NEXT_TAG:-}"
failed_legs=""
actions=""
rows="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$rows"' EXIT

gh label create daily-publish --repo "$repo" --color B60205 \
  --description "Auto-filed by the daily auto-publish pipeline" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

# ── log collection ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Failing job/step names and the last ~50 log lines, from the child run when
# one exists, else from this daily run's leg job (jobs API — the run is
# still in progress here, and GitHub serves no logs for it mid-run).
failing_steps() { # $1 = child run id ("" = this run), $2 = log prefix
  if [ -n "$1" ]; then
    gh run view "$1" --repo "$repo" --json jobs --jq '
      [.jobs[] | select(.conclusion == "failure" or .conclusion == "cancelled")
        | .name + " — " +
          ([.steps[] | select(.conclusion == "failure" or .conclusion == "cancelled")
            | .name] | join(", "))]
      | join("\n")' 2>/dev/null || true
  else
    # The report job runs INSIDE the daily run, so the run is still in
    # progress here — and GitHub serves no logs for in-progress runs
    # (--log-failed returns empty: issue #208 was filed as "unknown (job
    # cancelled or timed out)" for a leg that died in 4s with a clear
    # error). Job/step data IS served mid-run — read failed steps from it.
    gh run view "$GITHUB_RUN_ID" --repo "$repo" --json jobs 2>/dev/null \
      | jq -r --arg job "$2" '
          [.jobs[] | select(.name == $job
                              and (.conclusion == "failure"
                                or .conclusion == "cancelled"))
            | .name + " — " +
              ([.steps[] | select(.conclusion == "failure"
                               or .conclusion == "cancelled")
                | .name] | join(", "))]
          | join("\n")' 2>/dev/null || true
  fi
}

log_excerpt() { # $1 = child run id ("" = this run), $2 = job-name fragment
  # gh-1478: signal-first excerpt. Grep the failed log for error signal
  # lines and quote the first matches with context; the raw tail is only
  # the fallback when nothing matches (the #1473 tree-noise digest).
  local raw=""
  if [ -n "$1" ]; then
    raw=$(gh run view "$1" --repo "$repo" --log-failed 2>/dev/null \
      | tail -n 400 || true)
  fi
  if [ -z "$raw" ]; then
    # No child log (child in flight/cancelled, or never dispatched). The
    # RUN-level log zip is 409 while the daily run is in progress, but the
    # per-JOB log endpoint serves completed jobs — resolve the failed or
    # cancelled leg job and take ITS log (the #1472 empty-shrug class, and
    # the inject_failure TEST hook shape: a failed leg job, no child run).
    local job_id
    job_id=$(gh run view "$GITHUB_RUN_ID" --repo "$repo" --json jobs \
      2>/dev/null | jq -r --arg frag "$2" '
        [.jobs[] | select((.conclusion == "failure" or .conclusion == "cancelled")
                          and (.name | contains($frag))) | .databaseId]
        | last // empty' 2>/dev/null || true)
    if [ -n "$job_id" ]; then
      raw=$(gh run view --job "$job_id" --repo "$repo" --log 2>/dev/null \
        | tail -n 400 || true)
    fi
  fi
  [ -n "$raw" ] || return 0
  printf '%s\n' "$raw" | signal_excerpt
}

signal_excerpt() { # stdin: log text; stdout: first signal matches w/ context, else tail
  awk '
    { lines[NR] = $0
      if ($0 ~ /::error::|Message from server|(^|[^A-Za-z])error:|(^|[^A-Za-z])FAIL|[Ee]xit code|exited with/) {
        if (++hits <= 3)
          for (i = NR - 3; i <= NR + 3; i++) if (i >= 1) want[i] = 1
      }
    }
    END {
      if (hits == 0) { # no signal line — the raw tail is the fallback
        start = NR - 49; if (start < 1) start = 1
        for (i = start; i <= NR; i++) print lines[i]
        exit
      }
      i = 1; snip = 0
      while (i <= NR) {
        if (!want[i]) { i++; continue }
        if (snip++) print "[...]"
        while (i <= NR && want[i]) { print lines[i]; i++ }
      }
    }'
}

error_signature() { # stdin: excerpt/log; stdout: normalized root-cause signature
  # Priority order: ::error::, Message from server, error:, FAIL, exit-code
  # lines. The signature is the first line of the highest-priority class,
  # stripped of gh log prefixes (job<TAB>step<TAB>timestamp) — the dedup
  # key for the root-cause search (#1473 vs #1452).
  awk '
    {
      pr = 0
      if ($0 ~ /::error::/) pr = 1
      else if ($0 ~ /Message from server/) pr = 2
      else if ($0 ~ /(^|[^A-Za-z])error:/) pr = 3
      else if ($0 ~ /(^|[^A-Za-z])FAIL/) pr = 4
      else if ($0 ~ /[Ee]xit code|exited with/) pr = 5
      if (pr && (best == 0 || pr < best)) { best = pr; sig = $0 }
    }
    END { if (best) print sig }' \
    | awk -F '\t' '{print $NF}' \
    | sed -e 's/^[0-9]\{4\}-[0-9]\{2\}-[0-9]\{2\}T[0-9:.]\{1,\}Z *//' \
        -e 's/^::error:://' \
        -e 's/^Message from server: *//' \
        -e 's/[[:space:]][[:space:]]*/ /g' \
        -e 's/^ //' -e 's/ $//' \
    | cut -c1-200
}

find_issue_by_signature() { # $1 = normalized signature; echoes an open issue number or nothing
  # gh-1478 root-cause dedup: GitHub issue search matches open issues'
  # bodies AND comments — a hit means the root cause is already tracked, so
  # the caller comments there instead of filing a symptom duplicate.
  local q
  q=$(printf '%s' "$1" \
      | tr -cs '[:alnum:]./+-' ' ' \
      | sed -e 's/^ *//' -e 's/ *$//' \
      | cut -c1-200)
  [ -n "$q" ] || return 0
  gh search issues "\"$q\"" --repo "$repo" --state open \
    --match body,comments --limit 5 --json number \
    --jq '.[0].number // empty' 2>/dev/null || true
}

cancelled_job_info() { # $1 = job-name fragment; "name<TAB>startedAt<TAB>completedAt" or nothing
  gh run view "$GITHUB_RUN_ID" --repo "$repo" --json jobs 2>/dev/null \
    | jq -r --arg frag "$1" '
        [.jobs[] | select(.conclusion == "cancelled"
                          and (.name | contains($frag)))]
        | .[0] | if . == null then "" else [.name, .startedAt, .completedAt] | @tsv end' \
    2>/dev/null || true
}

leg_ceiling_minutes() { # $1 = job-name fragment; echoes timeout-minutes from the workflow or nothing
  local wf="${DAILY_PUBLISH_WORKFLOW:-${GITHUB_WORKSPACE:-.}/.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml}"
  [ -f "$wf" ] || return 0
  # The fragment is matched LITERALLY (index, not ~): it contains the CLI
  # leg's `+` ("Leg: CLI + macOS desktop"), which as an unescaped awk ERE
  # operator never matches the workflow yaml — that silently dropped the
  # CLI leg's timeout ceiling from cancelled digests.
  awk -v frag="$1" '
    index($0, "name: ") > 0 && index($0, frag) > 0 { injob = 1; next }
    injob && /^  [A-Za-z0-9_-]+:/ { injob = 0 }
    injob && /^    timeout-minutes:/ {
      line = $0
      sub(/^ *timeout-minutes: */, "", line)
      sub(/[^0-9].*/, "", line)
      if (line != "") print line
      exit
    }' "$wf"
}

fmt_elapsed() { # $1 = seconds -> "359m53s" / "1h2m3s" (unpadded components)
  local s="$1" h m
  h=$((s / 3600)); m=$(((s % 3600) / 60)); s=$((s % 60))
  if [ "$h" -gt 0 ]; then echo "${h}h${m}m${s}s"; else echo "${m}m${s}s"; fi
}

# ISO-UTC → epoch seconds: GNU date (Linux CI) and BSD date (local macOS)
# — the same portable pair release_dedupe_check.sh uses. A bare GNU
# `date -u -d` silently resolved nothing on dev hosts without GNU date and
# degraded the cancelled digest to "killed after unknown elapsed" (gh-1649).
iso_to_epoch() {
  date -u -d "$1" +%s 2>/dev/null && return 0
  date -u -j -f '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' "$1" +%s 2>/dev/null
}

# ── issue lifecycle ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
find_open_issue() { # $1 = exact title; echoes the issue number or nothing
  gh issue list --repo "$repo" --state open --label daily-publish \
    --limit 200 --json number,title --jq '.[] | [.number, .title] | @tsv' 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS=$'\t' read -r n t; do
        if [ "$t" = "$1" ]; then echo "$n"; fi
      done | head -1
}

file_or_comment() { # $1 = leg id, $2 = log prefix, $3 = child run url, $4 = leg result
  local leg="$1" prefix="$2" url="$3" result="${4:-failure}"
  # Job-name fragment for the own-run jobs API (the yaml display names add
  # parentheticals the report's display names don't carry).
  local frag="${prefix%% (*}"
  local child_id title steps excerpt body sig
  child_id="${url##*/}"
  title="[daily-publish] $leg leg failed"
  steps=$(failing_steps "$child_id" "$prefix")
  excerpt=$(log_excerpt "$child_id" "$frag")
  sig=""
  [ -z "$excerpt" ] || sig=$(printf '%s\n' "$excerpt" | error_signature)

  body="$(mktemp)"
  {
    echo "**Leg:** \`$leg\`"
    # #345/#347: a cancelled leg job means the WATCHER died (whole-run
    # cancellation or leg timeout) — not a child-workflow failure verdict.
    # The child may still be in flight, which is also why the steps/log
    # excerpts below can come up empty mid-run. Say so up front instead of
    # letting "unknown (job cancelled or timed out)" read like a leg defect.
    if [ "$result" = "cancelled" ]; then
      echo "**Leg job result:** cancelled — the leg's watcher was killed mid-watch (whole-run cancellation or leg timeout), NOT a child-workflow failure verdict. The child run may have been healthy or still in flight; correlate its timeline before treating this as a leg defect."
      # gh-1478: a cancelled run gets a real digest — which job was in
      # flight, its timeout-minutes ceiling, elapsed-vs-ceiling — instead of
      # the #1472 empty "no failed-step log available" shrug.
      local cinfo cname cstart cend ceiling
      cinfo=$(cancelled_job_info "$frag")
      ceiling=$(leg_ceiling_minutes "$frag")
      if [ -n "$cinfo" ]; then
        IFS=$'\t' read -r cname cstart cend <<< "$cinfo"
        local celapsed="unknown"
        local cs="" ce=""
        cs=$(iso_to_epoch "$cstart" || true)
        ce=$(iso_to_epoch "$cend" || true)
        if [ -n "$cs" ] && [ -n "$ce" ] && [ "$ce" -ge "$cs" ]; then
          celapsed=$(fmt_elapsed $((ce - cs)))
        fi
        echo "**Cancelled while running:** job \`$cname\` — killed after ${celapsed} elapsed."
        if [ -n "$ceiling" ]; then
          echo "**Timeout ceiling:** \`${ceiling}m\` (timeout-minutes in daily-publish.yml)."
          if [ "$celapsed" != "unknown" ]; then
            local csec_elapsed=$((ce - cs)) csec_ceiling=$((ceiling * 60))
            if [ "$csec_elapsed" -ge $((csec_ceiling - 60)) ]; then
              echo "**Elapsed vs ceiling:** ${celapsed} of ${ceiling}m — at the ceiling, so the leg hit its own timeout (a wedged child or too-tight ceiling; the child chain timeouts are the #351 arithmetic)."
            elif [ "$((csec_elapsed * 2))" -le "$csec_ceiling" ]; then
              echo "**Elapsed vs ceiling:** ${celapsed} of ${ceiling}m — far below the ceiling, so this looks like a whole-run/operator cancellation or an infrastructure kill, not the leg's own timeout."
            else
              echo "**Elapsed vs ceiling:** ${celapsed} of ${ceiling}m — below the ceiling; check the run timeline for a whole-run cancellation before treating this as a leg defect."
            fi
          fi
        fi
      else
        echo "**Cancelled while running:** could not resolve which job was in flight from the jobs API — see the run timeline."
      fi
    fi
    echo "**Daily run:** $daily_url"
    [ -n "$url" ] && echo "**Leg run:** $url"
    echo "**Failing job/step:** ${steps:-unknown (job cancelled or timed out)}"
    if [ -n "$sig" ]; then
      # The normalized signature is both human-visible and machine-matchable
      # (root-cause dedup searches open issues' bodies/comments for it).
      echo "**Error signature:** \`$sig\`"
      echo "<!-- daily-publish-sig: $sig -->"
    fi
    echo
    echo "Failure excerpt (signal-first: error lines with context; raw tail when no signal line matches):"
    echo
    if [ -n "$excerpt" ]; then
      sed -e 's/\t/  /g' -e 's/^/    /' <<< "$excerpt"
    else
      echo "    (no failed-step log available — see the run link)"
    fi
    echo
    echo "---"
    echo "Auto-filed by the daily auto-publish pipeline; auto-closes when this leg goes green. Pause the pipeline with \`gh workflow disable daily-publish.yml -R $repo\`."
  } > "$body"

  # gh-1478 root-cause dedup: when the normalized signature matches an OPEN
  # issue's body/comments (any label — #1452 is not a daily-publish issue),
  # the root cause is already tracked: comment there with the new run link
  # instead of filing a symptom duplicate that re-fires every day.
  if [ -n "$sig" ]; then
    local sigmatch
    sigmatch=$(find_issue_by_signature "$sig")
    if [ -n "$sigmatch" ]; then
      {
        echo "**Root-cause dedup (gh-1478):** this failure's error signature matches #$sigmatch — the digest below is a fresh data point for that issue, not a new bug."
        echo
        cat "$body"
      } > "$body.sig"
      gh issue comment "$sigmatch" --repo "$repo" --body-file "$body.sig" >/dev/null
      actions+="updated #${sigmatch} ($leg — signature matches an open root cause)"$'\n'
      rm -f "$body" "$body.sig"
      return 0
    fi
  fi

  local existing
  existing=$(find_open_issue "$title")
  if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
    gh issue comment "$existing" --repo "$repo" --body-file "$body" >/dev/null
    actions+="updated #${existing} ($leg still failing)"$'\n'
  else
    local created
    created=$(gh issue create --repo "$repo" --title "$title" --body-file "$body" \
      --label bug --label daily-publish --assignee "$assignee" 2>/dev/null || true)
    if [ -n "$created" ]; then
      actions+="filed ${created} ($leg failed)"$'\n'
    else
      echo "::warning::could not file the self-healing issue for leg '$leg' (permissions?)"
      actions+="FAILED to file an issue for $leg"$'\n'
    fi
  fi
  rm -f "$body"
}

close_if_open() { # $1 = leg id
  local title="[daily-publish] $1 leg failed"
  local existing
  existing=$(find_open_issue "$title")
  if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
    gh issue close "$existing" --repo "$repo" \
      --comment "✅ leg \`$1\` went green again in $daily_url — auto-closing." >/dev/null
    actions+="auto-closed #${existing} ($1 green again)"$'\n'
  fi
}

# ── per-leg processing ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# process_leg <id> <display> <result> <url> <version> <links> <status-override>
process_leg() {
  local id="$1" display="$2" result="${3:-}" url="${4:-}" version="${5:-}" links="${6:-}" override="${7:-}"
  local prefix="Leg: $2" icon status
  case "$result" in
    success)
      # A neutral-skip override («skipped: …») marks an UNOBSERVED outcome
      # (#1368 false green: release-in-flight rendered ✅ and auto-closed the
      # leg's stuck-release issue without ever seeing the publish). Render it
      # as a skip — never ✅ — and keep any open leg issue open; only a
      # verified outcome (up-to-date/recovered/private) closes it.
      if [[ "$override" == "skipped:"* ]]; then
        icon="⏭️"
        status="$override"
      else
        icon="✅"
        status="${override:-success}"
        close_if_open "$id"
      fi
      ;;
    failure)
      icon="❌"; status="failure"; failed_legs+="$id "
      file_or_comment "$id" "$prefix" "$url"
      ;;
    cancelled)
      icon="⚠️"; status="cancelled (timeout?)"; failed_legs+="$id "
      file_or_comment "$id" "$prefix" "$url" "cancelled"
      ;;
    *)
      icon="⏭️"; status="skipped"
      ;;
  esac

  local link_cell="-"
  if [ -n "$url" ]; then
    link_cell="[run]($url)"
    [ -n "$links" ] && link_cell+=" • $links"
  elif [ -n "$links" ]; then
    if [ "$result" = "success" ]; then
      link_cell="$links"
    else
      link_cell="$links • [daily run]($daily_url)"
    fi
  fi
  [ -n "$version" ] || version="-"
  echo "| $display | \`$version\` | $icon $status | $link_cell |" >> "$rows"
}

# Plan job: a failure here means legs never ran correctly — it gets its own
# issue instead of escaping the self-healing loop.
if [ "${PLAN_RESULT:-success}" != "success" ]; then
  file_or_comment plan "Plan (change detection + versions)" ""
  failed_legs+="plan "
  echo "| Plan | - | ❌ ${PLAN_RESULT} | [daily run]($daily_url) |" >> "$rows"
else
  close_if_open plan
fi

# pub.dev status override — display names MUST match the workflow job names
# exactly ("Leg: <name>"): the log-prefix filter relies on them.
pubdev_override=""
case "${LEG_PUBDEV_STATUS:-}" in
  private)    pubdev_override="private (publish_to: none)";;
  recovered)  pubdev_override="recovered — tag-publish rerun, pub.dev serves ${LEG_PUBDEV_PUBLISHED:-?}";;
  up-to-date) pubdev_override="up-to-date (pub.dev serves ${LEG_PUBDEV_PUBLISHED:-?})";;
  # gh-1192/#1368: the tag-publish outcome is UNOBSERVED (still executing or
  # the bounded wait lapsed) — neutral, no issue filed, none closed, and the
  # summary renders it as a skip, never a ✅.
  release-in-flight) pubdev_override="skipped: release in flight (tag-publish outcome unobserved this run; the next daily re-verifies)";;
esac

process_leg testflight "TestFlight" "${LEG_TESTFLIGHT:-}" "${LEG_TESTFLIGHT_URL:-}" \
  "$next_tag (est.)" "[release](https://github.com/${repo}/releases/tag/${next_tag})"
process_leg play "Play (Android beta)" "${LEG_PLAY:-}" "${LEG_PLAY_URL:-}" \
  "$next_tag (est.)" "[release](https://github.com/${repo}/releases/tag/${next_tag})"
process_leg pubdev "pub.dev" "${LEG_PUBDEV:-}" "${LEG_PUBDEV_URL:-}" \
  "${LEG_PUBDEV_PUBSPEC:-}" "[pub.dev](https://pub.dev/packages/flutter_agent_harness)" "$pubdev_override"
process_leg cli "CLI + macOS desktop" "${LEG_CLI:-}" "${LEG_CLI_URL:-}" \
  "$next_tag (est.)" "[release](https://github.com/${repo}/releases/tag/${next_tag})"
process_leg website "Website" "${LEG_WEBSITE:-}" "${LEG_WEBSITE_URL:-}" \
  "" "[fa1.dev](https://fa1.dev)"
process_leg addin "Outlook add-in" "${LEG_ADDIN:-}" "${LEG_ADDIN_URL:-}" \
  "" "[manifest](https://fa1.dev/outlook/manifest.xml)"

# ── job summary ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
{
  echo "## Daily auto-publish"
  echo
  echo "Run: $daily_url • est. next tag: \`$next_tag\` (each leg derives latest+1 at its own dispatch)"
  echo "| Leg | Version | Status | Links |"
  echo "| --- | --- | --- | --- |"
  cat "$rows"
  echo
  if [ -n "$actions" ]; then
    echo "### Self-healing issues"
    echo
    printf '%s' "$actions"
  else
    echo "_No issue lifecycle actions this run._"
  fi
} >> "${GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY:-/dev/stdout}"

if [ -n "$failed_legs" ]; then
  echo "::error::daily-publish legs failed: ${failed_legs% } — issues filed/updated, see the job summary"
  exit 1
fi
echo "daily-publish report complete — no failing legs"

Senior Developer Engineer specializing in root cause analysis and bug fixing ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Coding Guidelines — follow existing codebase patterns and conventions"] G2["Before implementing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists in project root or subdirectories → READ and FOLLOW it — it contains agent-specific instructions, coding styles, and conventions"] G4["If skills are available in the project → USE them — they provide specialized capabilities, workflows, and tool integrations"] G5["Instructions may be extended via project configuration — always follow the full set of provided instructions"] G6["Never invent new patterns when the codebase already has an established way of doing things"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 --> G5 --> G6 ``` ## input_context_reading.md ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph INPUT_ORDER["⚠️ MANDATORY: Read input files FIRST before anything else"] I0["find input/ -type f | sort — list all available files"] I1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, deployment constraints, approved frameworks"] I2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/request.md — ticket description, requirements, solution design, diagrams"] I3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — existing discussion, prior decisions, linked info"] I4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/existing_questions.json — answered questions = binding requirements"] I5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — specifications already downloaded"] I6["6️⃣ Check for images in input/TICKET/ — *.png *.jpg *.gif *.svg"] I7["7️⃣ If present: input/TICKET/parent-KEY.md — parent story summary, description, ACs"] I8["8️⃣ If present: input/TICKET/parent_context_ba.md / sa.md / vd.md — BA/SA/VD context"] I0 --> I1 --> I2 --> I3 --> I4 --> I5 --> I6 --> I7 --> I8 end subgraph CONFLUENCE_RULE["Confluence pages in input/ — READ THEM, don't re-fetch"] C1["✅ DO: read input/TICKET/confluence/PageName.md"] C2["❌ DON'T: call dmtools confluence_* to re-fetch pages already in input/"] C3["✅ DO: read image files in input/TICKET/confluence/ — they are attachments from that page"] end subgraph ATTACH_RULE["Attachments — check before fetching via API"] A1["Search glob 'input/**/*.png' and 'input/**/*.jpg' — find pre-downloaded images"] A2["If image found locally → analyze it directly, no API call needed"] A3["If attachment NOT in input/ → use dmtools confluence_get_content_attachments "] A1 --> A2 A1 -->|not found| A3 end subgraph DMTOOLS_RULE["When to use dmtools for external data"] D1["ONLY if you need data NOT already in input/"] D2["dmtools jira_get_ticket KEY, dmtools confluence_search QUERY, etc."] D3["See instructions/common/dmtools_cli.md for full reference"] end INPUT_ORDER --> CONFLUENCE_RULE --> ATTACH_RULE --> DMTOOLS_RULE ``` ## general_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD START([Bug ticket ready for fix]) --> READ["⚠️ MANDATORY: Read ALL input files FIRST — see instructions/common/input_context_reading.md"] READ --> RETURNED{Ticket returned to development?} RETURNED -->|Yes| PREV["Review previous PR diff and QA feedback in comments.md"] PREV --> RCA_RET["Write/Update RCA explaining why previous fix failed — see output_rules.md for rca.md format"] RETURNED -->|No| RCA_FRESH["Write fresh RCA from ticket description and linked_tests.md"] RCA_RET --> REPRO RCA_FRESH --> REPRO["Write a unit test that reproduces the bug. Run it — it MUST FAIL"] REPRO --> EXISTS{Test fails?} EXISTS -->|No| ALREADY["Check git history, current code, and linked tests.
⚠️ If linked test exists: verify it passes AND the test was created/updated BEFORE the fix commit — not after.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

# Daily auto-publish (issue #161): thin orchestrator over the existing
# publish channels. Each channel is an isolated leg — one leg failing never
# kills the others — and every failure self-files a d…

blocks.text:
# Daily auto-publish (issue #161): thin orchestrator over the existing
# publish channels. Each channel is an isolated leg — one leg failing never
# kills the others — and every failure self-files a deduplicated GitHub
# issue (label `bug`, assigned to the owner) that auto-closes when the leg
# goes green again. No publish logic is duplicated here: legs dispatch the
# existing workflows via `gh workflow run` and watch them.
#
#   testflight  build-mobile.yml   ios_content=all (the iOS half of the
#                                 mobile build)
#   play        build-mobile.yml   android_content=all,
#                                 android_track=beta (Android external
#                                 beta / open testing — issue #289 lifts
#                                 the standing "Android excluded" owner
#                                 decision for the release track; #947
#                                 adds the listing deploy — texts +
#                                 whole-set image replace + verify — so
#                                 the listing never trails the goldens;
#                                 the leg green-skips while the Play
#                                 secrets are absent)
#   pubdev      in-job OIDC publish, only when pubspec > pub.dev; otherwise
#               a green up-to-date check. The tag-time OIDC publish job
#               (ci.yml) stays the primary path; this leg is the catch-up +
#               loud-failure detector (e.g. expired publish credentials)
#   cli         build-macos.yml    desktop DMG + macOS CLI bundles +
#                                 extension, attached to the next-tag
#                                 release (version passed explicitly so
#                                 mobile/desktop never mint diverging tags)
#   website     pages.yml          fa1.dev (landing + web demo +
#                                 the /outlook add-in slice; gh-1684:
#                                 the extension zip moved to GitHub
#                                 Releases and is no longer site-hosted)
#   addin       office-addin.yml   manifest/taskpane acceptance suite; the
#                                 fa1.dev publish itself rides the website
#                                 leg (pages.yml assembles /outlook)
#
# Legs run only when main moved since the last GREEN daily run — skip-no-
# change is green-neutral, never red (#159 lesson). One exception (gh-1192):
# while main's pubspec version is not yet served by pub.dev the plan gate
# (scripts/daily_plan.sh) forces the legs anyway — a release-in-flight
# green must not become a skip baseline that stalls re-verification and
# rerun-recovery on a quiet main. Versioning stays the
# existing scheme: auto_release.sh patch-bumps + tags every main push
# (2h coalesce); the daily attaches mobile/desktop artifacts to the next
# tag and verifies/republishes pub.dev. See docs/ci.md.
#
# Pause: gh workflow disable daily-publish.yml -R IstiN/flutter_agent_harness

name: Daily auto-publish

run-name: "Daily auto-publish (${{ inputs.legs || 'all' }})"

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '17 5 * * *' # once daily, 05:17 UTC
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      legs:
        description: 'Leg(s) to run'
        type: choice
        default: all
        options:
          - all
          - testflight
          - play
          - pubdev
          - cli
          - website
          - addin
      force:
        description: 'Run even if main has not moved since the last green daily'
        type: boolean
        default: false
      inject_failure:
        description: 'TEST ONLY — fail this leg before any dispatch, to exercise the self-filing issue cycle'
        type: choice
        default: none
        options:
          - none
          - testflight
          - play
          - pubdev
          - cli
          - website
          - addin

permissions:
  contents: read

# One daily at a time; a queued run must not cancel an in-flight one.
concurrency:
  group: daily-publish
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  plan:
    name: Plan (change detection + versions)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # gh-1477: 10m was the same time bomb as the derive-version jobs — a
    # full-history fetch under a 10m ceiling. 20m + the blobless filter
    # below.
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: read
    outputs:
      changed: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.changed }}
      next_tag: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.next_tag }}
      latest_tag: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.latest_tag }}
      pubspec_version: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.pubspec_version }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # gh-1477: daily_plan.sh reads tags / commit metadata / one file
          # at origin/main — never historical blobs. Blobless keeps full
          # tag/commit metadata without the blobs (the full fetch outgrew
          # the old 10m ceiling in the twin derive-version job, run
          # 38027695551).
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none

      - name: Detect main movement and derive versions
        id: plan
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          FORCE: ${{ inputs.force }}
        # gh-1192: the gate (baseline + the release-unresolved re-arm that
        # keeps AC1's «the next daily re-verifies» true on a quiet main)
        # lives in the extracted script — shell-harness tested by
        # test/release_flow_race_test.dart.
        run: bash scripts/daily_plan.sh

  # ── Dispatch legs ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Shape per leg: dispatch the child workflow pinned to main, capture the
  # new run id, watch it, fail on any non-success conclusion. The child run
  # URL is exported even on failure so the report can excerpt its log.
  #
  # ── Timeout arithmetic (#351) ────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Invariants: watch budget > child worst-case (a legitimate slow child is
  # NEVER cancelled by the watcher — that was the #351 bug), leg
  # timeout > budget (the watcher, including its one cancel + re-dispatch
  # cycle, always outlives the child), and where the math fits under
  # GitHub's 360m job cap, leg timeout ≥ 2×budget + ~15m so the SECOND
  # wedge's fail-fast can actually fire inside the leg.
  #
  # Child worst-case = sum of the serialized job timeout-minutes along the
  # child's critical path (every job in a watched chain carries an explicit
  # timeout for exactly this). Margin = appear window (60×10s) + cancel
  # wait (180s) + poll slack ≈ 15m.
  #
  #   leg        child worst-case (serialized chain)          budget    leg timeout
  #   testflight version 20 → build-ios 90 → submit-ios 120   230m  →  250m (15000s) ; 360m
  #             (∥ release-mobile 15, covered by the max)
  #   play       version 20 → build-android 45 →              95m   →  110m (6600s) ; 240m
  #             submit-android 30 (∥ release-mobile 15)
  #   cli        version 20 → build-macos 150×2 (arm64 +      335m  →  350m (21000s) ; 360m
  #             x86_64 SERIALIZE on the single self-hosted
  #             runner) → release-macos 15
  #             (∥ cli matrix 45, extension 30 — shorter paths)
  #   (gh-1477: the version/plan jobs' ceiling moved 10 → 20m — a
  #   full-history fetch outgrew the 10m bomb; the fetch is now blobless
  #   and 20m is the seatbelt. Worst-cases and budgets grew by exactly
  #   the +10m.)
  #   website    pages build 45 → deploy 15                   60m   →   75m (4500s)  ; 180m
  #   addin      office-addin-suite 45 (single job)           45m   →   60m (3600s)  ; 150m
  #
  # Second-wedge headroom (2×budget + ~15m vs leg timeout): play 235 ≤
  # 240 ✓, website 163 ≤ 180 ✓, addin 133 ≤ 150 ✓. testflight (515 > 360)
  # and cli (715 > 360) CANNOT fit two full budgets under GitHub's 360m
  # job cap — their first wedge still self-heals (cancel at budget +
  # re-dispatch ≈ budget+13m), and a second wedge is bounded by the leg
  # timeout instead of the watcher's fail-fast; both children carry

        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          IPA_PATH=$(find flutter_app/build/ios -name "*.ipa" -type f | head -1)
