#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Dispatch a child workflow and watch it — with correct run correlation
# (issue #343) and wedge self-healing (issue #344). Shared by every
# dispatching daily-publish leg so the nightly legs cannot regress to the
# old inline watchers.
#
# #343 — the TestFlight and Play legs dispatch the SAME workflow
# (build-mobile.yml) as concurrent `needs: plan` siblings; the old inline
# watcher identified "our" run by event + a 60s createdAt window only and
# grabbed [0] of the timestamp-ordered list, so the Play leg could latch
# the TestFlight run (or a stale same-shaped run inside the trailing
# window) and watch a build that never builds Android. Correlation here:
#   * exact displayTitle match (--title) — the child workflow's run-name
#     embeds its inputs, so the sibling's differently-shaped run can never
#     be adopted (`gh run list` cannot filter by inputs; displayTitle is
#     the only distinguisher in the list API);
#   * the NEWEST matching run ([-1]) — never [0];
#   * a tight 30s createdAt window (clock-skew headroom; a run from
#     minutes ago, like today's stale iOS failure, is out of scope).
#
# #344 — a self-hosted runner that lost its final job-completion report
# holds a SUCCEEDED job in_progress forever (GitHub has no stale-run
# detection for self-hosted jobs below the workflow timeout), blocking the
# single-runner pool and every watcher leg until their 300m timeout. The
# watch here is budgeted: a run still unfinished after --budget-seconds
# (≈2x historical duration) is CANCELLED and re-dispatched exactly once;
# if the retry also wedges we fail fast naming both runs, so the pool
# problem surfaces in the leg log instead of silently eating 5 hours.
# gh-172 refines the wedge detection: budget expiry alone misses the
# pool-held zombie (run alive, nothing running) — a not-completed run with
# no in_progress job for DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS wedges the same way. The
# window defaults to max(600, budget/8) so a healthy child queued behind a
# SIBLING leg's job on the shared single-runner pool is not false-wedged
# (the window cannot tell zombie-held from legitimately busy — see the
# queue_stall comment below).
#
# Usage:
#   dispatch_and_watch.sh WORKFLOW.yml --repo OWNER/REPO --ref main \
#     [--title 'run-name exact match'] [--budget-seconds N] \
#     [--out-run-id FILE] [-f key=value]...
#
# The run id is written to --out-run-id as soon as correlation succeeds
# (BEFORE the watch), so callers can export the run URL even when the
# child run later fails. Env knobs (test shims): DW_POLL_SECONDS (60),
# DW_APPEAR_POLL_SECONDS (10), DW_APPEAR_ATTEMPTS (60),
# DW_CANCEL_WAIT_SECONDS (180), DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS (default
# max(600, budget/8) — gh-172: no-running-job wedge window).
set -euo pipefail

workflow=""
repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:-}"
ref="main"
title=""
budget=$((2 * 60 * 60))
out_run_id=""
inputs=()

while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --repo) repo="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --ref) ref="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --title) title="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --budget-seconds) budget="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --out-run-id) out_run_id="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    -f) inputs+=( -f "$2" ); shift 2 ;;
    -*) echo "dispatch_and_watch: unknown flag: $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
    *)
      if [ -n "$workflow" ]; then
        echo "dispatch_and_watch: unexpected extra arg: $1" >&2; exit 2
      fi
      workflow="$1"; shift
      ;;
  esac
done
if [ -z "$workflow" ] || [ -z "$repo" ]; then
  echo "usage: dispatch_and_watch.sh WORKFLOW.yml --repo OWNER/REPO [--ref main] [--title T] [--budget-seconds N] [-f k=v]" >&2
  exit 2
fi

poll="${DW_POLL_SECONDS:-60}"
appear_poll="${DW_APPEAR_POLL_SECONDS:-10}"
appear_attempts="${DW_APPEAR_ATTEMPTS:-60}"
cancel_wait="${DW_CANCEL_WAIT_SECONDS:-180}"
# gh-172: how long a not-completed run may sit with NO job in_progress
# (everything queued or already done) before it is treated as a wedge —
# the 2026-10-20 TestFlight leg (run 39374894901) burned ~107m of leg time
# watching a re-dispatched child queued forever on a zombie self-hosted
# worker and then died as a bare 360m ceiling kill with no diagnostic.
#
# The window CANNOT distinguish a zombie-held pool from a healthy child
# queued behind a SIBLING leg's job on the shared single-runner macOS pool
# (testflight's build-ios/submit-ios and cli's build-macos matrix contend
# for the same fa-m5-1; one cli matrix leg can hold it for ~150m — and a
# hosted-runner queue crunch does the same to the play/website/addin
# children), so the default is scaled off the watch budget:
# max(600, budget/8). Long-budget legs wait out realistic sibling
# occupancy (testflight 15000s → ~31m) before wedging a quiet-but-alive
# child; short-budget legs keep the fast 10-minute zombie trip.
# Accepted residual class: a sibling occupancy longer than budget/8 can
# still false-wedge into the one self-heal — bounded, diagnosed damage
# inside the leg ceiling beats the gh-172 silent full-budget burn.
# DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS overrides (test shims).
if [ -n "${DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS:-}" ]; then
  queue_stall="$DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS"
else
  queue_stall=$(( budget / 8 > 600 ? budget / 8 : 600 ))
fi

# jq selector: optional exact displayTitle match (#343).
title_select=""
if [ -n "$title" ]; then
  title_select=" | select(.displayTitle == \"${title}\")"
fi

dispatch() {
  gh workflow run "$workflow" --repo "$repo" --ref "$ref" ${inputs[@]+"${inputs[@]}"}
}

# The id of OUR run: workflow_dispatch runs created at/after the floor,
# matching --title when given, NEWEST of the matches (#343).
find_run_id() {
  local floor="$1"
  gh run list --repo "$repo" --workflow "$workflow" --event workflow_dispatch \
    --limit 20 --json databaseId,createdAt,displayTitle \
    --jq "[.[] | select((.createdAt | fromdateiso8601) >= $floor)${title_select}] | sort_by(.createdAt) | .[-1].databaseId // 0" \
    2>/dev/null || echo 0
}

wait_for_run() {
  local floor="$1" id=0 i=0
  while [ "$i" -lt "$appear_attempts" ]; do
    id=$(find_run_id "$floor")
    if [ "$id" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then echo "$id"; return 0; fi
    sleep "$appear_poll"
    i=$((i + 1))
  done
  return 1
}

attempt=1
while :; do
  dispatch
  epoch=$(date +%s)
  if ! run_id=$(wait_for_run "$((epoch - 30))"); then
    echo "::error::dispatched $workflow run never appeared (no workflow_dispatch run${title:+ titled \"$title\"} in the trailing window after $((appear_attempts * appear_poll))s)" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "watching $workflow run $run_id${title:+ (\"$title\")} — https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id (queue-stall window ${queue_stall}s)"
  if [ -n "$out_run_id" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$run_id" > "$out_run_id"; fi

  started=$(date +%s)
  last_running="$started"
  while :; do
    # One poll = one API call (gh-172 review): status, conclusion and the
    # running-job count arrive atomically — half the per-poll traffic and
    # no race where the two calls straddle a completion and one iteration
    # ticks the stall clock on an already-dead run. A failed poll cannot
    # observe, so it cannot judge: it refreshes the stall clock (no
    # signal — no accumulation) and never trips the guard; an outage
    # outliving the window is accepted bounded debt (during one, `gh run
    # cancel` hits the same unreachable API anyway) — the budget stays
    # the backstop.
    observed="$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status,conclusion,jobs \
      --jq '"\(.status)/" + (.conclusion // "-") + " " + ([.jobs[] | select(.status == "in_progress")] | length | tostring)' 2>/dev/null)" || observed=""
    status="${observed%% *}"
    running="${observed##* }"
    if [ -z "$observed" ] || [ "$status" = "$observed" ]; then
      status="error/-"
      running=""
      # gh-172 rework: refresh the stall clock on error polls too — a
      # sustained gh/API outage (longer than the window, starting while
      # the child was quiet) must not read as "no running job for Ns"
      # and false-wedge a healthy child into the one self-heal.
      last_running="$(date +%s)"
    fi
    if [ "${status%%/*}" = "completed" ]; then break; fi
    now=$(date +%s)
    # gh-172 job-level liveness: a run that is not completed but has NO job
…

Wait... let me check what the run status was during the watch. Run status: "in_progress"? The poll output format is `"\(.status)/" + (.conclusion // "-") + " + count`. The wedge branch requires:
1. `[ -n "$running" ]` — running must be non-empty.
2. `[ "$running" -gt 0 ]` false.
3. `[ -n "$running" ] && [ $((now - last_running)) -gt "$queue_stall" ]`.

So `running` was exactly "0" every successful poll for 31 minutes, while the run had an in_progress job.

Hypothesis A: The jobs API for THIS run genuinely reported no in_progress job because the self-hosted runner job's status on the API was... hmm.

Wait — actually, let me look again at the jobs data I got for run 39527524: `"status":"completed"` for Build iOS IPA with conclusion cancelled. During the run it would have been in_progress. Unless...

Hypothesis B: There's a **jq bug in the poll expression**. Let me test the exact poll command against a live running run to see what it returns. Actually, let me test the jq expression itself with a synthetic JSON.

Actually — WAIT. Look very carefully at the jq expression:

```jq
"\"\(.status)/" + (.conclusion // "-") + " + ([.jobs[] | select(.status == "in_progress")] | length | tostring)
``

Note the first string: `"\"\(.status)/"`. That's a jq string containing an escaped quote `\"` then `\(.status)` interpolation then `/`. So output = `"<status>/- N`. status="in_progress" → `in_progress/- 1`. OK.

Then in bash:
```bash
status="${observed%% *}"    # "in_progress/-"
running="${observed##* }"   # "1"
``

Then:
```bash
if [ -z "$observed" ] || [ "$status" = "$observed" ]; then # error check
``
`status="in_progress/-"`, observed="in_progress/- 1" — not equal → no error. OK.

`[ "${status%%/*}" = "completed" ]` → "in_progress" ≠ completed → continue.

`if [ $((now - started)) -gt "$budget" ]` → no.
`elif [ -n "$running" ] && [ "$running" -gt 0 ]` → running="1" → `[ "1" -gt 0 ]` true → last_running=now. Fine.

So if the API returned the truth, the wedge would never fire. But it did fire. Therefore the API returned 0 in_progress jobs — OR the jq expression has a real bug.

Let me test the jq expression locally right now with a mock. There might be a subtle issue: `select(.status == "in_progress")` — but jobs on this self-hosted runner... Hmm wait, what if the JOB status is not "in_progress" but something else while it's running on a self-hosted runner? GitHub job statuses: queued, in_progress, completed. Self-hosted runners report the same.

Hmm, but what if... the job was "queued" on the API while the runner was building? There's a known class of issue with self-hosted runners behind proxies: the runner claims the job and starts it, but the job status update to GitHub fails/lags. But for 31 minutes on BOTH attempts?

If gh fails → observed="" → error branch → last_running refreshed → no wedge. So polls must have SUCCEEDED and returned `... 0`.

Hmm, wait. Let me recheck: could `observed` be a NON-EMPTY string that parses weirdly, e.g. `"in_progress/-"` with NO trailing number? Then status="in_progress/-" (whole string, since no space), running="${observed##* }" = "in_progress/-" (no space → whole string). Then `[ "$status" = "$observed" ]` → TRUE → error branch. No wedge. Not it.

What if observed = "in_progress/- 0" genuinely every time? Then the jobs API really said 0 in_progress.

{"completedAt":"2026-10-21T06:31:44Z","conclusion":"cancelled","name":"Build iOS IPA","startedAt":"2026-10-21T06:00:57Z","status":"completed","steps":[]}

"steps":[] — EMPTY! The Build iOS IPA job ran for 31 minutes and its `steps` array is EMPTY?! Every job in both cancelled runs has `"steps":[]`. Senior Developer Engineer specializing in root cause analysis and bug fixing ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Coding Guidelines — follow existing codebase patterns and conventions"] G2["Before implementing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists in project root or subdirectories → READ and FOLLOW it — it contains agent-specific instructions, coding styles, and conventions"] G4["If skills are available in the project → USE them — they provide specialized capabilities, workflows, and tool integrations"] G5["Instructions may be extended via project configuration — always follow the full set of provided instructions"] G6["Never invent new patterns when the codebase already has an established way of doing things"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 --> G5 --> G6 ``` ## input_context_reading.md ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph INPUT_ORDER["⚠️ MANDATORY: Read input files FIRST before anything else"] I0["find input/ -type f | sort — list all available files"] I1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, deployment constraints, approved frameworks"] I2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/request.md — ticket description, requirements, solution design, diagrams"] I3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — existing discussion, prior decisions, linked info"] I4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/existing_questions.json — answered questions = binding requirements"] I5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — specifications already downloaded"] I6["6️⃣ Check for images in input/TICKET/ — *.png *.jpg *.gif *.svg"] I7["7️⃣ If present: input/TICKET/parent-KEY.md — parent story summary, description, ACs"] I8["8️⃣ If present: input/TICKET/parent_context_ba.md / sa.md / vd.md — BA/SA/VD context"] I0 --> I1 --> I2 --> I3 --> I4 --> I5 --> I6 --> I7 --> I8 end subgraph CONFLUENCE_RULE["Confluence pages in input/ — READ THEM, don't re-fetch"] C1["✅ DO: read input/TICKET/confluence/PageName.md"] C2["❌ DON'T: call dmtools confluence_* to re-fetch pages already in input/"] C3["✅ DO: read image files in input/TICKET/confluence/ — they are attachments from that page"] end subgraph ATTACH_RULE["Attachments — check before fetching via API"] A1["Search glob 'input/**/*.png' and 'input/**/*.jpg' — find pre-downloaded images"] A2["If image found locally → analyze it directly, no API call needed"] A3["If attachment NOT in input/ → use dmtools confluence_get_content_attachments "] A1 --> A2 A1 -->|not found| A3 end subgraph DMTOOLS_RULE["When to use dmtools for external data"] D1["ONLY if you need data NOT already in input/"] D2["dmtools jira_get_ticket KEY, dmtools confluence_search QUERY, etc."] D3["See instructions/common/dmtools_cli.md for full reference"] end INPUT_ORDER --> CONFLUENCE_RULE --> ATTACH_RULE --> DMTOOLS_RULE ``` ## general_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD START([Bug ticket ready for fix]) --> READ["⚠️ MANDATORY: Read ALL input files FIRST — see instructions/common/input_context_reading.md"] READ --> RETURNED{Ticket returned to development?} RETURNED -->|Yes| PREV["Review previous PR diff and QA feedback in comments.md"] PREV --> RCA_RET["Write/Update RCA explaining why previous fix failed — see output_rules.md for rca.md format"] RETURNED -->|No| RCA_FRESH["Write fresh RCA from ticket description and linked_tests.md"] RCA_RET --> REPRO RCA_FRESH --> REPRO["Write a unit test that reproduces the bug. Run it — it MUST FAIL"] REPRO --> EXISTS{Test fails?} EXISTS -->|No| ALREADY["Check git history, current code, and linked tests.
⚠️ If linked test exists: verify it passes AND the test was created/updated BEFORE the fix commit — not after.
If bug is genuinely fixed — write outputs/already_fixed.json and stop"] ALREADY --> END_FIXED([End — bug already fixed]) EXISTS -->|Yes| BLOCKED{Fix requires external decision, secrets, or infra changes?} BLOCKED -->|Yes| BLOCK["Write outputs/blocked.json and stop — see output_rules.md"] BLOCK --> END_BLOCKED([End — blocked awaiting human input]) BLOCKED -->|No| FIX["Make minimum targeted fix for the root cause ONLY"] FIX --> VERIFY["Run reproduction test (must PASS) and full test suite (no regressions)"] VERIFY --> PASS{All tests pass?} PASS -->|No| ADJUST["Adjust fix and re-run tests"] ADJUST --> VERIFY PASS -->|Yes| GITSTATUS["Run git status and review every new/modified file"] GITSTATUS --> SECRETS{Sensitive or untracked non-code files present?} SECRETS -->|Yes| IGNORE["Add appropriate patterns to .gitignore"] SECRETS -->|No| SUMMARY["Write concise bug fix summary to outputs/response.md — see output_rules.md"] IGNORE --> SUMMARY SUMMARY --> END([End — post-processing handles git/PR]) ``` ## Returning from test-automation failure When this Bug has been sent back to development because a linked Test Case failed: 1. # AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

blocks.text:
# Daily auto-publish (issue #161): thin orchestrator over the existing
# publish channels. Each channel is an isolated leg — one leg failing never
# kills the others — and every failure self-files a deduplicated GitHub
# issue (label `bug`, assigned to the owner) that auto-closes when the leg
# goes green again. No publish logic is duplicated here: legs dispatch the
# existing workflows via `gh workflow run` and watch them.
#
#   testflight  build-mobile.yml   ios_content=all (the iOS half of the
#                                 mobile build)
#   play        build-mobile.yml   android_content=all,
#                                 android_track=beta (Android external
#                                 beta / open testing — issue #289 lifts
#                                 the standing "Android excluded" owner
#                                 decision for the release track; #947
#                                 adds the listing deploy — texts +
#                                 whole-set image replace + verify — so
#                                 the listing never trails the goldens;
#                                 the leg green-skips while the Play
#                                 secrets are absent)
#   pubdev      in-job OIDC publish, only when pubspec > pub.dev; otherwise
#               a green up-to-date check. The tag-time OIDC publish job
#               (ci.yml) stays the primary path; this leg is the catch-up +
#               loud-failure detector (e.g. expired publish credentials)
#   cli         build-macos.yml    desktop DMG + macOS CLI bundles +
#                                 extension, attached to the next-tag
#                                 release (version passed explicitly so
#                                 mobile/desktop never mint diverging tags)
#   website     pages.yml          fa1.dev (landing + web demo +
#                                 the /outlook add-in slice; gh-1684:
#                                 the extension zip moved to GitHub
#                                 Releases and is no longer site-hosted)
#   addin       office-addin.yml   manifest/taskpane acceptance suite; the
#                                 fa1.dev publish itself rides the website
#                                 leg (pages.yml assembles /outlook)
#
# Legs run only when main moved since the last GREEN daily run — skip-no-
# change is green-neutral, never red (#159 lesson). One exception (gh-1192):
# while main's pubspec version is not yet served by pub.dev the plan gate
# (scripts/daily_plan.sh) forces the legs anyway — a release-in-flight
# green must not become a skip baseline that stalls re-verification and
# rerun-recovery on a quiet main. Versioning stays the
# existing scheme: auto_release.sh patch-bumps + tags every main push
# (2h coalesce); the daily attaches mobile/desktop artifacts to the next
# tag and verifies/republishes pub.dev. See docs/ci.md.
#
# Pause: gh workflow disable daily-publish.yml -R IstiN/flutter_agent_harness

name: Daily auto-publish

run-name: "Daily auto-publish (${{ inputs.legs || 'all' }})"

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '17 5 * * *' # once daily, 05:17 UTC
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      legs:
        description: 'Leg(s) to run'
        type: choice
        default: all
        options:
          - all
          - testflight
          - play
          - pubdev
          - cli
          - website
          - addin
      force:
        description: 'Run even if main has not moved since the last green daily'
        type: boolean
        default: false
      inject_failure:
        description: 'TEST ONLY — fail this leg before any dispatch, to exercise the self-filing issue cycle'
        type: choice
        default: none
        options:
          - none
          - testflight
          - play
          - pubdev
          - cli
          - website
          - addin

permissions:
  contents: read

# One daily at a time; a queued run must not cancel an in-flight one.
concurrency:
  group: daily-publish
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  plan:
    name: Plan (change detection + versions)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # gh-1477: 10m was the same time bomb as the derive-version jobs — a
    # full-history fetch under a 10m ceiling. 20m + the blobless filter
    # below.
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: read
    outputs:
      changed: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.changed }}
      next_tag: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.next_tag }}
      latest_tag: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.latest_tag }}
      pubspec_version: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.pubspec_version }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # gh-1477: daily_plan.sh reads tags / commit metadata / one file
          # at origin/main — never historical blobs. Blobless keeps full
          # tag/commit metadata without the blobs (the full fetch outgrew
          # the old 10m ceiling in the twin derive-version job, run
          # 38027695551).
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none

      - name: Detect main movement and derive versions
        id: plan
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          FORCE: ${{ inputs.force }}
        # gh-1192: the gate (baseline + the release-unresolved re-arm that
        # keeps AC1's «the next daily re-verifies» true on a quiet main)
        # lives in the extracted script — shell-harness tested by
        # test/release_flow_race_test.dart.
        run: bash scripts/daily_plan.sh

  # ── Dispatch legs ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Shape per leg: dispatch the child workflow pinned to main, capture the
  # new run id, watch it, fail on any non-success conclusion. The child run
  # URL is exported even on failure so the report can excerpt its log.
  #
  # ── Timeout arithmetic (#351) ────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Invariants: watch budget > child worst-case (a legitimate slow child is
  # NEVER cancelled by the watcher — that was the #351 bug), leg
  # timeout > budget (the watcher, including its one cancel + re-dispatch
  # cycle, always outlives the child), and where the math fits under
  # GitHub's 360m job cap, leg timeout ≥ 2×budget + ~15m so the SECOND
  # wedge's fail-fast can actually fire inside the leg.
  #
  # Child worst-case = sum of the serialized job timeout-minutes along the
  # child's critical path (every job in a watched chain carries an explicit
  # timeout for exactly this). Margin = appear window (60×10s) + cancel
  # wait (180s) + poll slack ≈ 15m.
  #
  #   leg        child worst-case (serialized chain)          budget    leg timeout
  #   testflight version 20 → build-ios 90 → submit-ios 120   230m  →  250m (15000s) ; 360m
  #             (∥ release-mobile 15, covered by the max)
  #   play       version 20 → build-android 45 →              95m   →  110m (6600s) ; 240m
  #             submit-android 30 (∥ release-mobile 15)
  #   cli        version 20 → build-macos 150×2 (arm64 +      335m  →  350m (21000s) ; 360m
  #             x86_64 SERIALIZE on the single self-hosted
  #             runner) → release-macos 15
  #             (∥ cli matrix 45, extension 30 — shorter paths)
  #   (gh-1477: the version/plan jobs' ceiling moved 10 → 20m — a
  #   full-history fetch outgrew the 10m bomb; the fetch is now blobless
  #   and 20m is the seatbelt. Worst-cases and budgets grew by exactly
  #   the +10m.)
  #   website    pages build 45 → deploy 15                   60m   →   75m (4500s)  ; 180m
  #   addin      office-addin-suite 45 (single job)           45m   →   60m (3600s)  ; 150m
  #
  # Second-wedge headroom (2×budget + ~15m vs leg timeout): play 235 ≤
  # 240 ✓, website 163 ≤ 180 ✓, addin 133 ≤ 150 ✓. testflight (515 > 360)
  # and cli (715 > 360) CANNOT fit two full budgets under GitHub's 360m
  # job cap — their first wedge still self-heals (cancel at budget +
  # re-dispatch ≈ budget+13m), and a second wedge is bounded by the leg
  # timeout instead of the watcher's fail-fast; both children carry
  # per-job server-side timeouts (#344) so a wedged job self-fails even
  # without the watch…

          - metadata_only    # texts/descriptions only (no build, no upload, no screenshots)

      # debug dSYMs under Symbols/. App Store Connect strips that directory
      # from device delivery anyway (TestFlight reports ~157 MB — the
      # payload WITHOUT Symbols), so it is dead weight in the artifact.
      # Repack without it: Payload/ is untouched (codesign validity lives
      # inside the bundle), zip -y preserves the framework symlinks so the
      # manifest shape is unchanged. Idempotent — a future export that
      # omits Symbols/ skips straight through.
      - name: Strip debug symbols from IPA (#1331)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          IPA_PATH=$(find flutter_app/build/ios -name "*.ipa" -type f | head -1)
          if [ -z "$IPA_PATH" ]; then
            echo "::error::IPA file not found in flutter_app/build/ios"
            exit 1
          fi
          # gh-1403: absolutize BEFORE the rezip — find yields a RELATIVE
          # path, and the `(cd "$STRIP" && …)` subshell resolved
          # "$IPA_PATH.stripped" against the mktemp dir (no flutter_app/
          # ancestor) → "zip error: Could not create output file". The
          # atomic-swap mv below carried the same hazard.
          # (realpath: /usr/bin/realpath, macOS 13+ — the runner is newer.)
          IPA_PATH=$(realpath "$IPA_PATH")
          if ! unzip -l "$IPA_PATH" "Symbols/*" | grep -q "Symbols/"; then
            echo "no Symbols/ in the IPA — nothing to strip"
            exit 0
          fi
          STRIP=$(mktemp -d)
          trap 'rm -rf "$STRIP"' EXIT
          unzip -q "$IPA_PATH" -d "$STRIP"
          rm -rf "$STRIP/Symbols"
          BEFORE=$(stat -f%z "$IPA_PATH")
          # Atomic swap: the original IPA survives a failed rezip (the
          # un-stripped copy still beats no artifact for debugging).
          (cd "$STRIP" && find . -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -exec zip -qyr9 "$IPA_PATH.stripped" {} +)
          mv -f "$IPA_PATH.stripped" "$IPA_PATH"

      - name: Upload IPA Artifact

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Daily auto-publish report (issue #161): renders the per-run job-summary
# table and drives the self-healing issue lifecycle.
#
#   failing/cancelled leg -> file a bug issue assigned to the owner; dedup
#     guard: an OPEN issue labeled `daily-publish` with the same title gets
#     a fresh comment (new run link + log excerpt) instead of a duplicate
#   green leg -> auto-close that leg's still-open issue with a comment
#
# Inputs come from environment (set by the daily-publish.yml report job):
#   PLAN_RESULT         needs.plan.result — a plan failure files its own issue
#   LEG_<NAME>          needs result: success | failure | skipped | cancelled
#   LEG_<NAME>_URL      child run URL (empty on internal/skip paths)
#   LEG_PUBDEV_*        status (up-to-date/private/recovered/release-in-flight),
#                       versions, tag-run URL
#   NEXT_TAG            estimated next tag (informational; legs derive latest+1 themselves)
#   GITHUB_RUN_ID, GITHUB_REPOSITORY, GITHUB_SERVER_URL   runner defaults
#
# Exits non-zero when any leg failed or was cancelled (the daily run goes
# red too); all-skipped stays green (#159 lesson).
set -euo pipefail

repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"
daily_url="${GITHUB_SERVER_URL}/${repo}/actions/runs/${GITHUB_RUN_ID}"
assignee="${DAILY_PUBLISH_ASSIGNEE:-ai-teammate}"
next_tag="${NEXT_TAG:-}"
failed_legs=""
actions=""
rows="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$rows"' EXIT

gh label create daily-publish --repo "$repo" --color B60205 \
  --description "Auto-filed by the daily auto-publish pipeline" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

# ── log collection ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Failing job/step names and the last ~50 log lines, from the child run when
# one exists, else from this daily run's leg job (jobs API — the run is
# still in progress here, and GitHub serves no logs for it mid-run).
failing_steps() { # $1 = child run id ("" = this run), $2 = log prefix
  if [ -n "$1" ]; then
    gh run view "$1" --repo "$repo" --json jobs --jq '
      [.jobs[] | select(.conclusion == "failure" or .conclusion == "cancelled")
        | .name + " — " +
          ([.steps[] | select(.conclusion == "failure" or .conclusion == "cancelled")
            | .name] | join(", "))]
      | join("\n")' 2>/dev/null || true
  else
    # The report job runs INSIDE the daily run, so the run is still in
    # progress here — and GitHub serves no logs for in-progress runs
    # (--log-failed returns empty: issue #208 was filed as "unknown (job
    # cancelled or timed out)" for a leg that died in 4s with a clear
    # error). Job/step data IS served mid-run — read failed steps from it.
    gh run view "$GITHUB_RUN_ID" --repo "$repo" --json jobs 2>/dev/null \
      | jq -r --arg job "$2" '
          [.jobs[] | select(.name == $job
                              and (.conclusion == "failure"
                                or .conclusion == "cancelled"))
            | .name + " — " +
              ([.steps[] | select(.conclusion == "failure"
                               or .conclusion == "cancelled")
                | .name] | join(", "))]
          | join("\n")' 2>/dev/null || true
  fi
}

log_excerpt() { # $1 = child run id ("" = this run), $2 = job-name fragment
  # gh-1478: signal-first excerpt. Grep the failed log for error signal
  # lines and quote the first matches with context; the raw tail is only
  # the fallback when nothing matches (the #1473 tree-noise digest).
  local raw=""
  if [ -n "$1" ]; then
    raw=$(gh run view "$1" --repo "$repo" --log-failed 2>/dev/null \
      | tail -n 400 || true)
  fi
  if [ -z "$raw" ]; then
    # No child log (child in flight/cancelled, or never dispatched). The
    # RUN-level log zip is 409 while the daily run is in progress, but the
    # per-JOB log endpoint serves completed jobs — resolve the failed or
    # cancelled leg job and take ITS log (the #1472 empty-shrug class, and
    # the inject_failure TEST hook shape: a failed leg job, no child run).
    local job_id
    job_id=$(gh run view "$GITHUB_RUN_ID" --repo "$repo" --json jobs \
      2>/dev/null | jq -r --arg frag "$2" '
        [.jobs[] | select((.conclusion == "failure" or .conclusion == "cancelled")
                          and (.name | contains($frag))) | .databaseId]
        | last // empty' 2>/dev/null || true)
    if [ -n "$job_id" ]; then
      raw=$(gh run view --job "$job_id" --repo "$repo" --log 2>/dev/null \
        | tail -n 400 || true)
    fi
  fi
  [ -n "$raw" ] || return 0
  printf '%s\n' "$raw" | signal_excerpt
}

signal_excerpt() { # stdin: log text; stdout: first signal matches w/ context, else tail
  awk '
    { lines[NR] = $0
      if ($0 ~ /::error::|Message from server|(^|[^A-Za-z])error:|(^|[^A-Za-z])FAIL|[Ee]xit code|exited with/) {
        if (++hits <= 3)
          for (i = NR - 3; i <= NR + 3; i++) if (i >= 1) want[i] = 1
      }
    }
    END {
      if (hits == 0) { # no signal line — the raw tail is the fallback
        start = NR - 49; if (start < 1) start = 1
        for (i = start; i <= NR; i++) print lines[i]
        exit
      }
      i = 1; snip = 0
      while (i <= NR) {
        if (!want[i]) { i++; continue }
        if (snip++) print "[...]"
        while (i <= NR && want[i]) { print lines[i]; i++ }
      }
    }'
}

error_signature() { # stdin: excerpt/log; stdout: normalized root-cause signature
  # Priority order: ::error::, Message from server, error:, FAIL, exit-code
  # lines. The signature is the first line of the highest-priority class,
  # stripped of gh log prefixes (job<TAB>step<TAB>timestamp) — the dedup
  # key for the root-cause search (#1473 vs #1452).
  awk '
    {
      pr = 0
      if ($0 ~ /::error::/) pr = 1
      else if ($0 ~ /Message from server/) pr = 2
      else if ($0 ~ /(^|[^A-Za-z])error:/) pr = 3
      else if ($0 ~ /(^|[^A-Za-z])FAIL/) pr = 4
      else if ($0 ~ /[Ee]xit code|exited with/) pr = 5
      if (pr && (best == 0 || pr < best)) { best = pr; sig = $0 }
    }
    END { if (best) print sig }' \
    | awk -F '\t' '{print $NF}' \
    | sed -e 's/^[0-9]\{4\}-[0-9]\{2\}-[0-9]\{2\}T[0-9:.]\{1,\}Z *//' \
        -e 's/^::error:://' \
        -e 's/^Message from server: *//' \
        -e 's/[[:space:]][[:space:]]*/ /g' \
        -e 's/^ //' -e 's/ $//' \
    | cut -c1-200
}

find_issue_by_signature() { # $1 = normalized signature; echoes an open issue number or nothing
  # gh-1478 root-cause dedup: GitHub issue search matches open issues'
  # bodies AND comments — a hit means the root cause is already tracked, so
  # the caller comments there instead of filing a symptom duplicate.
  local q

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Dispatch a child workflow and watch it — with correct run correlation
# (issue #343) and wedge self-healing (issue #344). Shared by every
# dispatching daily-publish leg so the nightly legs cannot regress to the
# old inline watchers.
#
# #343 — the TestFlight and Play legs dispatch the SAME workflow
# (build-mobile.yml) as concurrent `needs: plan` siblings; the old inline
# watcher identified "our" run by event + a 60s createdAt window only and
# grabbed [0] of the timestamp-ordered list, so the Play leg could latch
# the TestFlight run (or a stale same-shaped run inside the trailing
# window) and watch a build that never builds Android. Correlation here:
#   * exact displayTitle match (--title) — the child workflow's run-name
#     embeds its inputs, so the sibling's differently-shaped run can never
#     be adopted (`gh run list` cannot filter by inputs; displayTitle is
#     the only distinguisher in the list API);
#   * the NEWEST matching run ([-1]) — never [0];
#   * a tight 30s createdAt window (clock-skew headroom; a run from
#     minutes ago, like today's stale iOS failure, is out of scope).
#
# #344 — a self-hosted runner that lost its final job-completion report
# holds a SUCCEEDED job in_progress forever (GitHub has no stale-run
# detection for self-hosted jobs below the workflow timeout), blocking the
# single-runner pool and every watcher leg until their 300m timeout. The
# watch here is budgeted: a run still unfinished after --budget-seconds
# (≈2x historical duration) is CANCELLED and re-dispatched exactly once;
# if the retry also wedges we fail fast naming both runs, so the pool
# problem surfaces in the leg log instead of silently eating 5 hours.
# gh-172 refines the wedge detection: budget expiry alone misses the
# pool-held zombie (run alive, nothing running) — a not-completed run with
# no in_progress job for DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS wedges the same way. The
# window defaults to max(600, budget/8) so a healthy child queued behind a
# SIBLING leg's job on the shared single-runner pool is not false-wedged
# (the window cannot tell zombie-held from legitimately busy — see the
# queue_stall comment below).
#
# Usage:
#   dispatch_and_watch.sh WORKFLOW.yml --repo OWNER/REPO --ref main \
#     [--title 'run-name exact match'] [--budget-seconds N] \
#     [--out-run-id FILE] [-f key=value]...
#
# The run id is written to --out-run-id as soon as correlation succeeds
# (BEFORE the watch), so callers can export the run URL even when the
# child run later fails. Env knobs (test shims): DW_POLL_SECONDS (60),
# DW_APPEAR_POLL_SECONDS (10), DW_APPEAR_ATTEMPTS (60),
# DW_CANCEL_WAIT_SECONDS (180), DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS (default
# max(600, budget/8) — gh-172: no-running-job wedge window).
set -euo pipefail

workflow=""
repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:-}"
ref="main"
title=""
budget=$((2 * 60 * 60))
out_run_id=""
inputs=()

while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --repo) repo="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --ref) ref="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --title) title="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --budget-seconds) budget="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --out-run-id) out_run_id="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    -f) inputs+=( -f "$2" ); shift 2 ;;
    -*) echo "dispatch_and_watch: unknown flag: $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
    *)
      if [ -n "$workflow" ]; then
        echo "dispatch_and_watch: unexpected extra arg: $1" >&2; exit 2
      fi
      workflow="$1"; shift
      ;;
  esac
done
if [ -z "$workflow" ] || [ -z "$repo" ]; then
  echo "usage: dispatch_and_watch.sh WORKFLOW.yml --repo OWNER/REPO [--ref main] [--title T] [--budget-seconds N] [-f k=v]" >&2
  exit 2
fi

poll="${DW_POLL_SECONDS:-60}"
appear_poll="${DW_APPEAR_POLL_SECONDS:-10}"
appear_attempts="${DW_APPEAR_ATTEMPTS:-60}"
cancel_wait="${DW_CANCEL_WAIT_SECONDS:-180}"
# gh-172: how long a not-completed run may sit with NO job in_progress
# (everything queued or already done) before it is treated as a wedge —
# the 2026-10-20 TestFlight leg (run 39374894901) burned ~107m of leg time
# watching a re-dispatched child queued forever on a zombie self-hosted
# worker and then died as a bare 360m ceiling kill with no diagnostic.
#
# The window CANNOT distinguish a zombie-held pool from a healthy child
# queued behind a SIBLING leg's job on the shared single-runner macOS pool
# (testflight's build-ios/submit-ios and cli's build-macos matrix contend
# for the same fa-m5-1; one cli matrix leg can hold it for ~150m — and a
# hosted-runner queue crunch does the same to the play/website/addin
# children), so the default is scaled off the watch budget:
# max(600, budget/8). Long-budget legs wait out realistic sibling
# occupancy (testflight 15000s → ~31m) before wedging a quiet-but-alive
# child; short-budget legs keep the fast 10-minute zombie trip.
# Accepted residual class: a sibling occupancy longer than budget/8 can
# still false-wedge into the one self-heal — bounded, diagnosed damage
# inside the leg ceiling beats the gh-172 silent full-budget burn.
# DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS overrides (test shims).
if [ -n "${DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS:-}" ]; then
  queue_stall="$DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS"
else
  queue_stall=$(( budget / 8 > 600 ? budget / 8 : 600 ))
fi

# jq selector: optional exact displayTitle match (#343).
title_select=""
if [ -n "$title" ]; then
  title_select=" | select(.displayTitle == \"${title}\")"
fi

dispatch() {
  gh workflow run "$workflow" --repo "$repo" --ref "$ref" ${inputs[@]+"${inputs[@]}"}
}

# The id of OUR run: workflow_dispatch runs created at/after the floor,
# matching --title when given, NEWEST of the matches (#343).
find_run_id() {
  local floor="$1"
  gh run list --repo "$repo" --workflow "$workflow" --event workflow_dispatch \
    --limit 20 --json databaseId,createdAt,displayTitle \
    --jq "[.[] | select((.createdAt | fromdateiso8601) >= $floor)${title_select}] | sort_by(.createdAt) | .[-1].databaseId // 0" \
    2>/dev/null || echo 0
}

wait_for_run() {
  local floor="$1" id=0 i=0
  while [ "$i" -lt "$appear_attempts" ]; do
    id=$(find_run_id "$floor")
    if [ "$id" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then echo "$id"; return 0; fi
    sleep "$appear_poll"
    i=$((i + 1))
  done
  return 1
}

attempt=1
while :; do
  dispatch
  epoch=$(date +%s)
  if ! run_id=$(wait_for_run "$((epoch - 30))"); then
    echo "::error::dispatched $workflow run never appeared (no workflow_dispatch run${title:+ titled \"$title\"} in the trailing window after $((appear_attempts * appear_poll))s)" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "watching $workflow run $run_id${title:+ (\"$title\")} — https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id (queue-stall window ${queue_stall}s)"
  if [ -n "$out_run_id" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$run_id" > "$out_run_id"; fi

  started=$(date +%s)
  last_running="$started"
  while :; do
    # One poll = one API call (gh-172 review): status, conclusion and the
    # running-job count arrive atomically — half the per-poll traffic and
    # no race where the two calls straddle a completion and one iteration
    # ticks the stall clock on an already-dead run. A failed poll cannot
    # observe, so it cannot judge: it refreshes the stall clock (no
    # signal — no accumulation) and never trips the guard; an outage
    # outliving the window is accepted bounded debt (during one, `gh run
    # cancel` hits the same unreachable API anyway) — the budget stays
    # the backstop.
    observed="$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status,conclusion,jobs \
      --jq '"\(.status)/" + (.conclusion // "-") + " " + ([.jobs[] | select(.status == "in_progress")] | length | tostring)' 2>/dev/null)" || observed=""
    status="${observed%% *}"
    running="${observed##* }"
    if [ -z "$observed" ] || [ "$status" = "$observed" ]; then
      status="error/-"
      running=""
      # gh-172 rework: refresh the stall clock on error polls too — a
      # sustained gh/API outage (longer than the window, starting while
      # the child was quiet) must not read as "no running job for Ns"
      # and false-wedge a healthy child into the one self-heal.
      last_running="$(date +%s)"
    fi
    if [ "${status%%/*}" = "completed" ]; then break; fi
    now=$(date +%s)
    # gh-172 job-level liveness: a run that is not completed but has NO job
…

The 2026-10-20 `Leg: TestFlight` watcher was killed at its 360m ceiling with no diagnostics while the re-dispatched child run ([39402285750](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/39402285750)) sat `queued` forever: the hung self-hosted worker ignored its own 90m job ceiling (250m actual), never processed the watcher's `gh run cancel` either, and kept holding the single-runner pool. `scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh` polls **run** status only — it saw `in_progress` throughout, burned the remaining ~107m of leg time on a child that could never start, and died as a bare timeout (hence "no failed-step log available"), leaving the orphan queued to publish unattended on pool revival.

The watcher now also cancels the child on the fail path so a server-side-dead run can never publish unattended when the pool revives. A second wedge now ends in a diagnostic inside the leg (testflight ≈ 273m < 360m ceiling).
- `.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml`: arithmetic comment updated (gh-172 case).

Over 10-20/10-21, build-ios's messages lost the race to the zombie session every time (or GitHub round-robins and we hit the zombie repeatedly).

Actually — alternative: ONE session whose worker is wedged in a state where the listener still ACKs message delivery (started_at) but the job-execution path never runs... but then the build-macos jobs at 05:28:20 couldn't have run on it. UNLESS the runner processes jobs SEQUENTIALLY: took build-ios at 05:28:18 (stamped started_at, handed to worker → worker wedged), and the runner's message loop — being "busy" with an unACKed job... no, then it couldn't take the 05:28:20 message either.

So: two sessions is the only story that fits all observations on 10-21. And that is exactly the "duplicate registration" pathology that PR #1723's note gestures at: "The physical fa-m5-1 worker itself needs ops attention (reboot/de-register)".

Everything is consistent. The root cause is 100% INFRA — the physical self-hosted runner box fa-m5-1 has a wedged/duplicate registration session that eats build-ios job messages (no execution, no telemetry), and since 10-20 no iOS build has been able to start. The repo-side machinery all behaved as designed:
- The job never went in_progress (correct — the runner never ran it).
- The gh-172 queue-stall guard correctly detected the zombie signature at 31m15s (budget/8), cancelled + re-dispatched once, failed fast on the second wedge (correct containment).
- The self-filing issue cycle filed this ticket (correct).
- The leg cannot go green until ops fixes the runner — "auto-closes when this leg goes green" cannot happen from a repo change.

Additional finding: the filed digest was empty ("(no failed-step log available)", empty failing steps) because (a) the cancelled jobs have no steps/logs at all (the zombie's signature — nothing to excerpt from the child), and (b) the per-job log fallback raced the log-upload eventual-consistency lag (report started 3s after the leg job completed; the log was not yet served; one-shot fetch, no retry). The leg log DID contain the full diagnostics (::error:: wedge lines). That's a real minor defect in daily_publish_report.sh of the gh-1472 class, but it's a DIGEST QUALITY defect, not the leg failure's root cause. Fixing it would NOT make the leg green (the ticket's auto-close condition) and is beyond "minimum targeted fix for the root cause ONLY" — the root cause is the runner.

Hold on, though. Let me think again about whether the maintainer would want the digest fix as part of this ticket... The flowchart is explicit:

- REPRO → write a unit test that reproduces the bug; run it — MUST FAIL.
- The "bug" here (leg failed) — can a repo test reproduce it? The leg failure is environmental (zombie runner). A repro test would need the zombie. Can't.
- BLOCKED{Fix requires external decision, secrets, or infra changes?} → YES (infra: physical runner).

So the canonical path: **outputs/blocked.json + outputs/rca.md + outputs/response.md** (response.md is still the completion artifact per session_ephemerality — "The ONLY completion artifact is outputs/response.md"; for a blocked run, post-processing reads blocked.json; I'll write response.md summarizing the RCA + blocked verdict, and rca.md with the full analysis).

Wait, let me re-check the output_rules: O1 rca.md always; O2 already_fixed.json only if fixed; O3 blocked.json only if blocked; O4 response.md — "concise PR description". For a blocked run there's no PR, but session_ephemerality says missing response.md = interrupted. So: rca.md + blocked.json + response.md (pointing to blocked.json).

Hmm, hold on. Before I settle on blocked, let me do the required diligence on the alternative one more time — is there ANY repo-side change that makes the testflight leg green without touching the box?

1. Re-pin build-ios to fa-m5-2? — NO: fa-m5-2 is the OTHER box with a BROKEN signing env (10-17/10-18 archive failures — gh-1692's whole reason for pining fa-m5-1). Swapping zombies for a known-broken signer = red leg with real build failures. Also an owner decision.

2. Hosted macOS runners — cost/quota + owner decision (they deliberately self-host). Not a unilateral "minimum fix".

3. Watcher changes — the guard behaved correctly; loosening it (longer stall window / more retries) just burns leg time against a zombie that will never process the message. The 10-20 evidence: the zombie state persisted 05:28→12:27 (7 hours) and beyond (2 more days). No realistic retry policy survives it. Correct behavior = fail fast + file (what happened).

4. Auto-de-register the runner from CI — requires admin token + re-register on the box (impossible remotely) + destructive to the healthy session too (same name). Way outside "minimum", dangerous, and an owner decision.

So: genuinely blocked on infra. 

One more validation of the "duplicate/zombie session" theory — can I find any direct evidence of the SECOND session? The runner list API is 403 (no admin). Indirect evidence: the job records with empty runner_name (delivered to a session that never reported = GitHub doesn't even know which runner name to attribute... actually interesting: when a job runs normally, runner_name comes from the reporting session. Empty runner_name + started_at = delivery recorded, attribution never happened).

Also worth checking: the fa-m5-1 history around 10-19 → 10-20. What happened between 10-19 05:59 (last good build) and 10-20 05:28 (first eaten message)? Maybe a merge changed the runner setup? Let me check git log for runner/CI changes around 10-19/10-20 — e.g., something in scripts/update_git_mirror.sh (gh-164/gh-1665) or build-ios steps that could wedge the RUNER itself (a step that hangs the runner process BEFORE reporting?). 

Hmm wait — THAT deserves a hard look. What if a REPO change between 10-19 and 10-20 introduced something in the build-ios job that kills/wedges the runner's job-execution path so early that nothing is ever reported? The job message IS delivered to the healthy session, the runner process forks the worker, and the worker dies instantly (e.g. OM, disk full from the gh-160 stale-workspace accumulation!) BEFORE it can POST job-started/step telemetry. GitHub then shows: started_at (delivery), no steps, no logs, job stuck in limbo (never in_progress). And the RUNER (healthy, single session, one message at a time... no — again, the 05:28:20 macos job ran fine 2 seconds later on the same box; a runner does not take a second job while the first message is un-ACKed... unless the message was delivered to a DIFFERENT session).

OK the two-session conclusion is inescapable for 10-21 05:28:18 vs 05:28:20. But let me STILL check what merged between 10-19 and 10-20 that touches the runner/checkout — because if a repo change wedges the job-execution path, "fix the repo" could still be the answer. Actually wait — no. If the message went to a zombie SESSION, repo content is irrelevant (the job never even read the repo — no logs at all; the first thing the runner does before steps is set up the workspace... those produce no logs? Actually "Set up job" produces logs (runner version etc.) — attempt-1 on 10-21 for the LEG job shows "Set up job" logs. For the build-ios jobs: ZERO logs = the worker never even reached "Set up job" = pre-execution death = runner-level, not repo-level. A repo change can't kill the runner before "Set up job" — that phase is purely runner-side (message → worker → set up job → download action refs...). The only repo-dependent part there is fetching `actions/checkout` — that logs too.

So: pre-"Set up job" death = the session's worker never launched = zombie session. Repo content NOT implicated. 

And the 10-19→10-20 transition? The box's state changed (ops action? auto-update of the runner service? disk filled by gh-160's accumulating stale-workspace sidecars in RUNER_TEMP on 10-19's successful runs?). The stale-workspace accumulation is a plausible box-side killer the repo's gh-160 rework already warns about ("unbounded growth until manual cleanup")! But whether it's disk-full or a half-dead duplicate registration, the FIX is the same: box-side ops (clean + reboot + de-register/re-register). Not repo code.

Let me do a final couple of verifications:
1. Check the CLI leg (gh-1736) is a SEPARATE root cause (Bad CPU type = the x86_64 flutter zip on arm64 box without Rosetta — the setup-flutter-selfhosted action downloaded flutter_macos_x64 for an arm64... wait, "Bad CPU type in executable" happened for 3.47.7 dart-sdk bin on the x86_64 leg... The x86_64 build-macos job runs on fa-m5-1 (arm64!) — a "macos-m5" M1/M2/M3/M4 box (M5 in the name, cute). An x86_64 matrix leg on an arm64 host needs Rosetta; the flutter 3.47.7 x64 dart-sdk binary failed with "Bad CPU type" = Rosetta not installed (or the runner label lies about arch). That's gh-1736's problem, NOT mine — different leg, different ticket, dev job already started on it.

2. Double-check the testflight child attempt-2 could NOT have succeeded even without the watcher: its build-ios job was eaten the same way (06:00:57, zero telemetry) — so the re-dispatch was doomed regardless; the watcher just bounded the damage. And the watcher cancelling the child also cancelled "Submit iOS to TestFlight"/"Create Mobile GitHub Release" (which is why THEY appear as failing jobs in the issue with empty steps).

3. For completeness — the daily run ALSO shows the earlier 10-21 ~05:59 attempt-1 cancel → "Submit iOS"/"Create Mobile GitHub Release" cancelled at 05:59:05/06.

Also let me look at the gh-1735 issue comments — the ticket input only has the body; there may be new comments (machine jobs) since. And check whether some OTHER dev agent already has a run in flight for #1735 (the #1736 issue showed a dev job started 06:33). If #1735 has its own machine job, fine — I AM that machine job's agent, most likely.

Now let me also sanity-check my claim about the queue-stall math producing the exact timings, by computing from the log timestamps:
- Attempt 1 watch start 05:27:42.84 → +1875s = 05:58:57.84 → next poll ≈ 05:59:04.9 (polls every ~62s: 05:27:42→05:59:04 is 31m22s = 1882s ≈ 30.4 polls) ✓ warning at 05:59:04.95.
- Attempt 2 watch start 06:00:20.35 → +1875s = 06:31:35.35 → polls every ~60s → next ≈ 06:31:44.3 ✓ error at 06:31:44.3.

Both land exactly on the stall threshold with a fresh clock at watch start — i.e., EVERY poll from the first one onward observed zero in_progress jobs. Rock solid.

And the important nuance for the RCA: the FIRST poll of attempt 1 was at ~05:28:44 (60s after watch start 05:27:42) — the build-ios job's started_at was already set (05:28:18) yet running=0 already. So the job was never in_progress even for a single poll cycle. The runner NEVER ACKed. (Not "went in_progress then silently stopped" — never in_progress at all.)

Alright — the RCA is airtight. Let me also grab a couple of artifact URLs for the report:
- Attempt 1 run: 395496070 (created 05:27:30, cancelled 05:59:05).
- Attempt 2 run: 39527524 (created 06:00:07, cancelled 06:31:44).
- Daily run: 39549568592.
- Leg job id 119056636, its log (fetched, 30KB) has the wedge lines.
- PR #1723 (gh-172 fix) already flagged the box: "The physical fa-m5-1 worker itself needs ops attention (reboot/de-register); the guard only bounds the leg damage and makes the signature visible in the leg log." ← THIS ISSUE IS EXACTLY THAT PREDICTED DAMAGE.

Interesting! So gh-1735 is the THIRD consecutive day of the same infra state (10-20: gh-172 + this, 10-21: gh-1735), and PR #1723 explicitly predicted it. The human action needed: on the fa-m5-1 Mac box — inspect runner services (look for duplicate/stale registrations, e.g. two actions-runner services both labeled fa-m5-1/macOS), reboot, de-register + re-register the runner, clean RUNER_TEMP stale-workspace sidecars (gh-160), verify with a manual dispatch of build-mobile (none/all).

Wait, one more consideration — should I double check the "two sessions" idea against the git history of runner labels? fa-m5-2: does it exist and have the fa-m5-1 label by accident? build-ios pins fa-m5-1; if fa-m5-2's box ALSO carries a stale fa-m5-1 label (misconfiguration), the build-ios message could land on fa-m5-2 (broken box, possibly unresponsive execution env — "signing env unverified") — and fa-m5-2 would be the zombie eating messages! The CLI leg's build-macos (macos-m5 only) landed on fa-m5-1 (runner_name recorded) — consistent with EITHER box serving it. The 10-17/10-18 archive failures were on fa-m5-2 per gh-1692's comment ("fa-m5-2 (10-17/10-18 ** ARCHIVE FAILED **, signing env unverified)") — so fa-m5-2 DID run jobs (with logs) on those days. 

Without runner-list admin access I can't enumerate registrations from here; the blocked.json "needs" must include checking BOTH boxes' registrations (and specifically whether any registration carries the fa-m5-1 label besides the healthy one). Good ops checklist item.

Now, the repro-test requirement. The TDD flow says write a failing repro test. For a blocked verdict, the flow exits at BLOCKED BEFORE the FIX step — the repro test requirement (REPRO) comes BEFORE BLOCKED in the flowchart. Hmm: REPRO → EXISTS{Test fails?} → BLOCKED. Strictly, the flowchart wants a repro test first. Can I write a repo test that "reproduces the failure"? The failure is environmental. The honest repro: a test that asserts "a build-ios job message dispatched to the fa-m5-1-labeled pool gets executed" — can't run in unit tests.

Alternative interpretation: the repro for a CI-infra bug is the pipeline run itself — re-dispatching the leg reproduces it (it did, twice, two days running). I could ACTUALLY re-dispatch build-mobile (none/all) right now as a live repro and watch the build-ios job get eaten again... That costs ~31 minutes and touches the shared runner pool + publishes a TestFlight build if the box somehow got fixed in the meantime. Hmm — risky side effects (a release train!). The instructions say minimum targeted action; a live re-dispatch of a PUBLISH workflow is a side-effectful action I should not take unilaterally... BUT the "test that reproduces the bug MUST FAIL" requirement for a CI bug = the leg must be observed failing. It's already observed failing 4 times (two days × two attempts). I'll cite those as the reproduction evidence instead of burning another publish dispatch.

Hmm, actually, wait. Let me reconsider whether there is a CHEAP, side-effect-free live probe that adds real diagnostic value for the blocked.json: dispatch build-mobile with ios_content=metadata_only? That exercises NO build (skips build-ios) — useless as a probe. ios_content=all → full train (release draft, TestFlight submit) — side-effectful. A manual dispatch of a NO-OP probe job on the fa-m5-1 labels? There's no such workflow. Creating one = repo change; over-scope for a blocked verdict.

Hmm, but hold on — actually, let me check something first: maybe the box got FIXED since this morning (the owner may have acted on PR #1723's note / gh-172 / gh-1736). If a manual testflight re-run would now go green, then "the leg goes green" auto-closes and the blocked verdict is stale. Let me probe: check recent build-mobile runs since 06:32 — any newer dispatches? And check if fa-m5-1 has processed ANY job since 05:32 (the CLI leg). A no-side-effect probe: list recent runs of build-macos.yml (its jobs also run on the box) — or the nightly.yml etc. Let me look at what's run since.

Senior Developer Engineer specializing in root cause analysis and bug fixing ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. blocks.text:
# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…
