  themselves (`latest tag + 1` at the child's own dispatch moment). A tag
  pinned once in the orchestrator would race `auto_release.sh` — the daily
  could attach assets to a tag minted at a different commit than the built
  code. Self-derivation keeps tag and code consistent; the two children
  derive within minutes of each other and converge on the same tag
  (`gh release create` attaches to an existing tag rather than moving it);
- never publishes to pub.dev itself (see the pub.dev row above) — pub.dev
  movement stays 100% in the auto_release → ci.yml tag job path, with the
  daily as verifier and rerun-recovery;
- keeps NO daily-side wedge alarm for a tag that never publishes (#1368):
  a freshly cut tag reads `release-in-flight` ⏭️ in the daily for as long
  as its outcome is unobservable (young tag inside the grace window, run
  queued past the terminal-wait budget). The version under test is the
  LATEST REMOTE TAG (`git ls-remote`), never a file read. The remaining
  tripwires for a genuinely stuck release: the plan job's
  release-unresolved re-arm (every daily re-verifies while pub.dev is
  behind the latest tag), and the tag-run selector in
  `scripts/verify_pubdev_release.sh`, which alarms `only non-push run(s)`
  once a tag exists but only non-push runs registered.

**Change baseline**: legs run only when `main` moved since the last green
daily **that ran all legs** (schedule runs, or `legs=all` dispatches). A
single-leg green dispatch never advances the baseline, so a partial smoke
can't make the next scheduled run skip the legs it never exercised.
One exception (gh-1192, reworked gh-1522): a release-in-flight pubdev leg
exits 0, so that green daily becomes the baseline — the plan gate
(`scripts/daily_plan.sh`) therefore still forces the legs while the
LATEST TAG's version is not yet served by pub.dev, keeping the
re-verification and the failed-run recovery alive on a quiet main. A
failing `plan` job
(not just legs) files its own
`[daily-publish] plan leg failed` issue — nothing escapes the loop.

## Self-healing issues

On a failing (or timed-out) leg the `report` job files an issue:

- title `[daily-publish] <leg> leg failed`, label `bug` + `daily-publish`,
  assigned to `vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit`;
- body: daily run link, leg run link, failing job/step names, the last ~50
  lines of the failed step's log;
- **dedup**: an open issue with the same signature gets a comment instead
  of a duplicate;
- **auto-close**: when the leg goes green in a later daily run, the open
  issue is closed with a comment.

Each run also writes a single job-summary table (leg → version → status →
links) and exits red itself when any leg failed.

KEY FINDING:

- 9de855f1 (2026-10-19 09:33:45Z): "gh-1692 [daily-publish] TestFlight dry 5 days: 4 chained failures — current: fa-m5-2 archive fails silently (xcpretty swallows xcodebuild error), **routing still unpinned**" — this is the commit that added the `fa-m5-1` pin + xcbeautify.

So the fa-m5-1 PIN merged on **10-19 at 09:33Z** — AFTER the 10-19 morning SUCCESS (05:28–05:59, which ran on fa-m5-1 via the unpinned `[self-hosted, macos-m5]` list).

The FIRST day the pin was active in a daily run = **10-20 at 05:27** — exactly the first day the build-ios jobs started being eaten (10-20 05:28:04 started_at, zero telemetry).

WOW. That reframes the root cause:

- On 10-19 (and earlier), build-ios matched `[self-hosted, macos-m5]` → GitHub could route it to EITHER box; it landed on whichever was free. On 10-19 it landed on the good one (runner_name recorded = fa-m5-1... hmm, or fa-m5-2? The API said runner_name "fa-m5-1" for the 10-19 job — so the box NAMED fa-m5-1 built successfully on 10-19 unpinned).
- On 10-20+, with the pin `[self-hosted, macos-m5, fa-m5-1]` — every build-ios job message is eaten (started_at, zero telemetry). Meanwhile jobs pinned only by macos-m5 (build-macos CLI leg jobs on 10-21 05:28) run FINE and record runner_name fa-m5-1.

Interpretation A (duplicate/stale registration carrying the `fa-m5-1` label): there are (at least) TWO online registrations that match `[self-hosted, macos-m5, fa-m5-1]`: a healthy one (which served build-macos at 05:28:20 and recorded runner_name fa-m5-1) and a zombie (which eats the build-ios messages). When BOTH labels must match, GitHub's balancer picks between the two matching sessions; the build-ios job drew the zombie twice on 10-20 and twice on 10-21 (4 for 4). The unpinned macos-m5 jobs drew the healthy one (or, when the zombie is busy... it's never busy — it never runs anything).

Hmm wait, that doesn't quite work either: with TWO matching online registrations, each job message goes to one of them. 4/4 build-ios draws hit the zombie while the macos-m5 jobs (a superset pool incl. both boxes) drew the healthy session. Unlucky but possible — or the zombie session (idle, no job) long-polls with a fresh connection and reliably wins the race against the busy healthy box.

Interpretation B (the `fa-m5-1` LABEL name is a lie / misdirected routing): the label `fa-m5-1` is attached to a registration whose session is wedged (e.g. the registration token was re-issued, or an old `.runner` state on the box under a different service still claims labels self-hosted+macos-m5+fa-m5-1 and is "online" but its worker can't launch). The healthy fa-m5-1 box's CURRENT registration might NOT carry the `fa-m5-1` label at all! Wait — but then how did build-macos (labels: self-hosted+macos-m5, no fa-m5-1) record runner_name "fa-m5-1"? The runner's NAME is fa-m5-1 (the registration name), but its LABELS are only [self-hosted, macos-m5, X] where X ≠ fa-m5-1... If the gh-1692 pin added a label that the box was never actually given (the pin's author ASSUMED the runner-name-label auto-matches — GitHub does auto-add the runner NAME as a label? NO — GitHub does NOT auto-label runners by name! Runner labels are only what's in the registration's --labels config + defaults. The gh-1692 comment says "the runner-name label `fa-m5-1`" — the author believed the runner name acts as a label. For GitHub-hosted runners, names aren't labels either. BUT custom labels can be added at registration time (--labels flag) or via the UI.)

Hmm wait — if NO registration carried the `fa-m5-1` label, build-ios would sit QUED forever (started_at NEVER set). But started_at IS set — a session with matching labels received the message. So SOME online session DOES claim the fa-m5-1 label. And jobs sent to it die silently.

So the zombie session (which claims self-hosted+macos-m5+fa-m5-1) exists and eats build-ios messages. The healthy box (name fa-m5-1) either also matches (duplicate registration with same labels — Interpretation A) or the healthy box's registration lacks the fa-m5-1 label and only serves the macos-m5-generic jobs (Interpretation B').

Either way — infra: **the registration(s) matching the gh-1692 pin are a wedged session; the pin routed the iOS lane into it since 10-20**. The repo-side contribution: the gh-1692 pin (9de855f1) changed routing the morning after the last good run, and every run since has died at the pin's target. Before the pin, the same workflow on the same pool landed on the good box and BUILT successfully (10-19 05:59 success).

Hmm!! Now THIS changes the calculus about "repo fix possible?":

Option: **remove/revisit the fa-m5-1 pin** (revert to `[self-hosted, macos-m5]`) so build-ios can land on the healthy box again?

Counter-evidence: the pin exists because fa-m5-2 was producing silent archive failures (10-17/10-18, gh-1692's raison d'être) and the pin was the fix for gh-1692 ("routing still unpinned"). Reverting the pin sends build-ios back to the coin flip: good box (build works) or fa-m5-2 (silent archive failure). With fa-m5-2 broken, unpining trades a 100% eaten message for a ~50% silent build failure. NOT a fix.

BUT — what if the "zombie" IS fa-m5-2 carrying a spurious `fa-m5-1` label?! The gh-1692 comment says fa-m5-2 is "signing env unverified" and produced ARCHIVE FAILED on 10-17/10-18 — those runs DID produce logs and steps (real builds failing at archive). So fa-m5-2's session wasn't a zombie then; it RAN jobs. A box can't be both "runs the build and fails at archive" (10-18) and "eats messages pre-Set-up-job" (10-20+) — unless its runner service degraded further in between (possible: the 10-19/10-20 boundary could be fa-m5-2's disk finally filling / service half-dead).

I can't distinguish A / B / B' from here (no admin API access). What I CAN do: check whether build-ios jobs before 10-20 but after... the pin merged 10-19 09:33; between 10-19 09:33 and 10-20 05:27, did any build-ios job run pinned? Let me check the 10-20 09:39 attempt-2 (queued forever — that one never even got started_at? Earlier query: 10-20 attempt-2 job 118559997592: started_at 09:40:18, steps 0, runner_name "" — ALSO eaten-but-stamped). Interesting — gh-172 described attempt-2 as "sat queued forever"; the API stamps started_at even in the limbo state. OK.

So since the pin merged, build-ios has run ZERO successful jobs: 4 messages, all eaten (10-20 ×2, 10-21 ×2). And on 10-19 05:28 the SAME pool (unpinned) built fine on the box named fa-m5-1.

Given all this — is a repo-side fix possible and CORECT? The candidates:

1. Remove the pin → coin flip with broken fa-m5-2 → likely silent failures. NO.
2. Pin to fa-m5-2 instead → its signing env is unverified/broken. NO.
3. Hosted runners → cost/quota + owner decision + secrets/signing re-validation. External decision. NO (unilaterally).
4. Ops fix the box/registrations → THE actual fix. This is what PR #1723 and gh-1692 both point to ("the physical fa-m5-1 worker itself needs ops attention (reboot/de-register)", "until fa-m5-2 is fixed").

Therefore: BLOCKED on infra/ops — with a precise, evidence-backed checklist of what ops must do:
- Audit runner registrations matching labels [self-hosted, macos-m5, fa-m5-1] (repo Settings → Actions → Runers, or GET /actions/runers with admin): look for a duplicate/stale fa-m5-1 registration and/or whether the healthy box's registration actually CARRIES the fa-m5-1 label.
- On the box(es): reboot, de-register stale registrations (config.cmd remove / deleting from the UI), re-register with explicit labels incl. fa-m5-1; verify fa-m5-2's signing env or de-register it too.
- Clean the gh-160 stale-workspace sidecar accumulation in RUNER_TEMP (possible disk-pressure cause).
- Probe: dispatch build-mobile (none/all) once; confirm Build iOS IPA records runner_name + steps + logs (the healthy signature), i.e. not the started_at-with-zero-telemetry limbo.

Now the TDD/repro question one final time. The flowchart: REPRO (unit test that reproduces the bug; run — MUST FAIL) → EXISTS → BLOCKED. For an infra-routed failure, the honest "repro" is: the observed production evidence (4 eaten messages across 10-20/10-21) + the pin-merge timeline correlation…

Root-cause chain is now solid. The `fa-m5-1` pin merged **10-19 09:33Z** (gh-1692), and every build-ios job dispatched **since** has been eaten (started_at stamped, zero telemetry, no logs), while unpinned `macos-m5` jobs on the same pool built normally. Before writing the verdict, I'll run a cheap, side-effect-safe live probe: dispatch the same inputs the leg uses — if the box got fixed, the lane goes healthy; if not, I cancel the run myself within minutes (no release draft, no publish — `release-mobile`/`submit-ios` both require `build-ios` success).

The 2026-10-20 `Leg: TestFlight` watcher was killed at its 360m ceiling with no diagnostics while the re-dispatched child run ([39402285750](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/39402285750)) sat `queued` forever: the hung self-hosted worker ignored its own 90m job ceiling (250m actual), never processed the watcher's `gh run cancel` either, and kept holding the single-runner pool. `scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh` polls **run** status only — it saw `in_progress` throughout, burned the remaining ~107m of leg time on a child that could never start, and died as a bare timeout (hence "no failed-step log available"), leaving the orphan queued to publish unattended on pool revival.

### Fix

- `scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh`: added a job-level liveness guard — a not-completed run with **no job in `in_progress` for `DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS` (600s)** is a wedge and rides the existing one-shot self-heal (cancel + re-dispatch once, then fail fast naming the pool). The watcher now also cancels the child on the fail path so a server-side-dead run can never publish unattended when the pool revives. A second wedge now ends in a diagnostic inside the leg (testflight ≈ 273m < 360m ceiling).
- `.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml`: arithmetic comment updated (gh-172 case).
- Ops: cancelled the orphaned queued run `39402285750` (the containment the fixed watcher performs).

### Test Coverage

- `test/dispatch_watch_test.dart` — `gh-172` group: pool-held child (alive, nothing running) stalls into the one self-heal, fails fast with the pool signature on attempt 2, cancels the orphan; plus a transient between-jobs pickup gap that must NOT trip the guard. New stub fixture (`jobs-<id>.txt`) models `gh run view --json jobs`.
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` — **11376 passed, 11 skipped, 0 failed**.

### Notes

- No leg budget/ceiling arithmetic changed — the #351 table is untouched.
- The physical `fa-m5-1` worker itself needs ops attention (reboot/de-register); the guard only bounds the leg damage and makes the signature visible in the leg log.

  themselves (`latest tag + 1` at the child's own dispatch moment). A tag
  pinned once in the orchestrator would race `auto_release.sh` — the daily
  could attach assets to a tag minted at a different commit than the built
  code. Self-derivation keeps tag and code consistent; the two children
  derive within minutes of each other and converge on the same tag
  (`gh release create` attaches to an existing tag rather than moving it);
- never publishes to pub.dev itself (see the pub.dev row above) — pub.dev
  movement stays 100% in the auto_release → ci.yml tag job path, with the
  daily as verifier and rerun-recovery;
- keeps NO daily-side wedge alarm for a tag that never publishes (#1368):
  a freshly cut tag reads `release-in-flight` ⏭️ in the daily for as long
  as its outcome is unobservable (young tag inside the grace window, run
  queued past the terminal-wait budget). The version under test is the
  LATEST REMOTE TAG (`git ls-remote`), never a file read. The remaining
  tripwires for a genuinely stuck release: the plan job's
  release-unresolved re-arm (every daily re-verifies while pub.dev is
  behind the latest tag), and the tag-run selector in
  `scripts/verify_pubdev_release.sh`, which alarms `only non-push run(s)`
  once a tag exists but only non-push runs registered.

**Change baseline**: legs run only when `main` moved since the last green
daily **that ran all legs** (schedule runs, or `legs=all` dispatches). A
single-leg green dispatch never advances the baseline, so a partial smoke
can't make the next scheduled run skip the legs it never exercised.
One exception (gh-1192, reworked gh-1522): a release-in-flight pubdev leg
exits 0, so that green daily becomes the baseline — the plan gate
(`scripts/daily_plan.sh`) therefore still forces the legs while the
LATEST TAG's version is not yet served by pub.dev, keeping the
re-verification and the failed-run recovery alive on a quiet main. A
failing `plan` job
(not just legs) files its own
`[daily-publish] plan leg failed` issue — nothing escapes the loop.

## Self-healing issues

On a failing (or timed-out) leg the `report` job files an issue:

- title `[daily-publish] <leg> leg failed`, label `bug` + `daily-publish`,
  assigned to `vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit`;
- body: daily run link, leg run link, failing job/step names, the last ~50
  lines of the failed step's log;
- **dedup**: an open issue with the same signature gets a comment instead
  of a duplicate;
- **auto-close**: when the leg goes green in a later daily run, the open
  issue is closed with a comment.

Each run also writes a single job-summary table (leg → version → status →
links) and exits red itself when any leg failed.

blocks.text:
KEY FINDING:

- 9de855f1 (2026-10-19 09:33:45Z): "gh-1692 [daily-publish] TestFlight dry 5 days: 4 chained failures — current: fa-m5-2 archive fails silently (xcpretty swallows xcodebuild error), **routing still unpinned**" — this is the commit that added the `fa-m5-1` pin + xcbeautify.

So the fa-m5-1 PIN merged on **10-19 at 09:33Z** — AFTER the 10-19 morning SUCCESS (05:28–05:59, which ran on fa-m5-1 via the unpinned `[self-hosted, macos-m5]` list).

The FIRST day the pin was active in a daily run = **10-20 at 05:27** — exactly the first day the build-ios jobs started being eaten (10-20 05:28:04 started_at, zero telemetry).

WOW. That reframes the root cause:

- On 10-19 (and earlier), build-ios matched `[self-hosted, macos-m5]` → GitHub could route it to EITHER box; it landed on whichever was free. On 10-19 it landed on the good one (runner_name recorded = fa-m5-1... hmm, or fa-m5-2? The API said runner_name "fa-m5-1" for the 10-19 job — so the box NAMED fa-m5-1 built successfully on 10-19 unpinned).
- On 10-20+, with the pin `[self-hosted, macos-m5, fa-m5-1]` — every build-ios job message is eaten (started_at, zero telemetry). Meanwhile jobs pinned only by macos-m5 (build-macos CLI leg jobs on 10-21 05:28) run FINE and record runner_name fa-m5-1.

Interpretation A (duplicate/stale registration carrying the `fa-m5-1` label): there are (at least) TWO online registrations that match `[self-hosted, macos-m5, fa-m5-1]`: a healthy one (which served build-macos at 05:28:20 and recorded runner_name fa-m5-1) and a zombie (which eats the build-ios messages). When BOTH labels must match, GitHub's balancer picks between the two matching sessions; the build-ios job drew the zombie twice on 10-20 and twice on 10-21 (4 for 4). The unpinned macos-m5 jobs drew the healthy one (or, when the zombie is busy... it's never busy — it never runs anything).

Hmm wait, that doesn't quite work either: with TWO matching online registrations, each job message goes to one of them. 4/4 build-ios draws hit the zombie while the macos-m5 jobs (a superset pool incl. both boxes) drew the healthy session. Unlucky but possible — or the zombie session (idle, no job) long-polls with a fresh connection and reliably wins the race against the busy healthy box.

Interpretation B (the `fa-m5-1` LABEL name is a lie / misdirected routing): the label `fa-m5-1` is attached to a registration whose session is wedged (e.g. the registration token was re-issued, or an old `.runner` state on the box under a different service still claims labels self-hosted+macos-m5+fa-m5-1 and is "online" but its worker can't launch). The healthy fa-m5-1 box's CURRENT registration might NOT carry the `fa-m5-1` label at all! Wait — but then how did build-macos (labels: self-hosted+macos-m5, no fa-m5-1) record runner_name "fa-m5-1"? The runner's NAME is fa-m5-1 (the registration name), but its LABELS are only [self-hosted, macos-m5, X] where X ≠ fa-m5-1... If the gh-1692 pin added a label that the box was never actually given (the pin's author ASSUMED the runner-name-label auto-matches — GitHub does auto-add the runner NAME as a label? NO — GitHub does NOT auto-label runners by name! Runner labels are only what's in the registration's --labels config + defaults. The gh-1692 comment says "the runner-name label `fa-m5-1`" — the author believed the runner name acts as a label. For GitHub-hosted runners, names aren't labels either. BUT custom labels can be added at registration time (--labels flag) or via the UI.)

Hmm wait — if NO registration carried the `fa-m5-1` label, build-ios would sit QUED forever (started_at NEVER set). But started_at IS set — a session with matching labels received the message. So SOME online session DOES claim the fa-m5-1 label. And jobs sent to it die silently.

So the zombie session (which claims self-hosted+macos-m5+fa-m5-1) exists and eats build-ios messages. The healthy box (name fa-m5-1) either also matches (duplicate registration with same labels — Interpretation A) or the healthy box's registration lacks the fa-m5-1 label and only serves the macos-m5-generic jobs (Interpretation B').

Either way — infra: **the registration(s) matching the gh-1692 pin are a wedged session; the pin routed the iOS lane into it since 10-20**. The repo-side contribution: the gh-1692 pin (9de855f1) changed routing the morning after the last good run, and every run since has died at the pin's target. Before the pin, the same workflow on the same pool landed on the good box and BUILT successfully (10-19 05:59 success).

Hmm!! Now THIS changes the calculus about "repo fix possible?":

Option: **remove/revisit the fa-m5-1 pin** (revert to `[self-hosted, macos-m5]`) so build-ios can land on the healthy box again?

Counter-evidence: the pin exists because fa-m5-2 was producing silent archive failures (10-17/10-18, gh-1692's raison d'être) and the pin was the fix for gh-1692 ("routing still unpinned"). Reverting the pin sends build-ios back to the coin flip: good box (build works) or fa-m5-2 (silent archive failure). With fa-m5-2 broken, unpining trades a 100% eaten message for a ~50% silent build failure. NOT a fix.

BUT — what if the "zombie" IS fa-m5-2 carrying a spurious `fa-m5-1` label?! The gh-1692 comment says fa-m5-2 is "signing env unverified" and produced ARCHIVE FAILED on 10-17/10-18 — those runs DID produce logs and steps (real builds failing at archive). So fa-m5-2's session wasn't a zombie then; it RAN jobs. A box can't be both "runs the build and fails at archive" (10-18) and "eats messages pre-Set-up-job" (10-20+) — unless its runner service degraded further in between (possible: the 10-19/10-20 boundary could be fa-m5-2's disk finally filling / service half-dead).

I can't distinguish A / B / B' from here (no admin API access). What I CAN do: check whether build-ios jobs before 10-20 but after... the pin merged 10-19 09:33; between 10-19 09:33 and 10-20 05:27, did any build-ios job run pinned? Let me check the 10-20 09:39 attempt-2 (queued forever — that one never even got started_at? Earlier query: 10-20 attempt-2 job 118559997592: started_at 09:40:18, steps 0, runner_name "" — ALSO eaten-but-stamped). Interesting — gh-172 described attempt-2 as "sat queued forever"; the API stamps started_at even in the limbo state. OK.

So since the pin merged, build-ios has run ZERO successful jobs: 4 messages, all eaten (10-20 ×2, 10-21 ×2). And on 10-19 05:28 the SAME pool (unpinned) built fine on the box named fa-m5-1.

Given all this — is a repo-side fix possible and CORECT? The candidates:

1. Remove the pin → coin flip with broken fa-m5-2 → likely silent failures. NO.
2. Pin to fa-m5-2 instead → its signing env is unverified/broken. NO.
3. Hosted runners → cost/quota + owner decision + secrets/signing re-validation. External decision. NO (unilaterally).
4. Ops fix the box/registrations → THE actual fix. This is what PR #1723 and gh-1692 both point to ("the physical fa-m5-1 worker itself needs ops attention (reboot/de-register)", "until fa-m5-2 is fixed").

Therefore: BLOCKED on infra/ops — with a precise, evidence-backed checklist of what ops must do:
- Audit runner registrations matching labels [self-hosted, macos-m5, fa-m5-1] (repo Settings → Actions → Runers, or GET /actions/runers with admin): look for a duplicate/stale fa-m5-1 registration and/or whether the healthy box's registration actually CARRIES the fa-m5-1 label.
- On the box(es): reboot, de-register stale registrations (config.cmd remove / deleting from the UI), re-register with explicit labels incl. fa-m5-1; verify fa-m5-2's signing env or de-register it too.
- Clean the gh-160 stale-workspace sidecar accumulation in RUNER_TEMP (possible disk-pressure cause).
- Probe: dispatch build-mobile (none/all) once; confirm Build iOS IPA records runner_name + steps + logs (the healthy signature), i.e. not the started_at-with-zero-telemetry limbo.

Now the TDD/repro question one final time. The flowchart: REPRO (unit test that reproduces the bug; run — MUST FAIL) → EXISTS → BLOCKED. For an infra-routed failure, the honest "repro" is: the observed production evidence (4 eaten messages across 10-20/10-21) + the pin-merge timeline correlation…

Root-cause chain is now solid. The `fa-m5-1` pin merged **10-19 09:33Z** (gh-1692), and every build-ios job dispatched **since** has been eaten (started_at stamped, zero telemetry, no logs), while unpinned `macos-m5` jobs on the same pool built normally. Before writing the verdict, I'll run a cheap, side-effect-safe live probe: dispatch the same inputs the leg uses — if the box got fixed, the lane goes healthy; if not, I cancel the run myself within minutes (no release draft, no publish — `release-mobile`/`submit-ios` both require `build-ios` success).

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis — gh-1735 `[daily-publish] testflight leg failed`

**Bug**: The daily-publish TestFlight leg (daily run 39549568592 → child run 39552755224) failed with three jobs listed as failing — `Build iOS IPA`, `Create Mobile GitHub Release`, `Submit iOS to TestFlight` — and an empty failure excerpt.

**Root cause**: The self-hosted runner registration session matching the `[self-hosted, macos-m5, fa-m5-1]` pin (added by gh-1692, commit 9de855f1, merged 2026-10-19 09:33Z) is a **zombie: it consumes `Build iOS IPA` job messages and never executes or reports them**. GitHub stamps the job's `startedAt` at message delivery, but the job never enters `in_progress`, records zero steps, zero logs, and no `runner_name`; the job-log blob is never uploaded (`BlobNotFound` from the job-log endpoint). No repo code runs at all in this state — the failure is pre-`Set up job`, i.e. runner-infrastructure, not product code.

**Evidence chain**:

| When | Run | Build iOS IPA | Signature |
|---|---|---|---|
| 10-19 05:28 (pre-pin) | 39204704151 | SUCCESS 05:28:48→05:59:54 | `runner_name=fa-m5-1`, 24 steps, logs ✅ |
| 10-20 05:28 (first daily after the pin) | 39374977270 | "started" 05:28:04, cancelled 09:38:29 | `runner_name=""`, 0 steps, no logs |
| 10-20 09:40 (gh-172's queued-forever run) | 39402285750 | "started" 09:40:18, cancelled 12:27 | `runner_name=""`, 0 steps |
| 10-21 05:28 (leg attempt 1) | 39549660700 | "started" 05:28:18, cancelled 05:59:05 | `runner_name=""`, 0 steps, job log = BlobNotFound |
| 10-21 06:00 (leg attempt 2) | 39552755224 | "started" 06:00:57, cancelled 06:31:44 | `runner_name=""`, 0 steps, no logs |
| 10-21 06:51 (**live probe, this session**) | 39557953541 | "started" 06:51:08, cancelled 07:05 after 14 min in limbo | `runner_name=""`, 0 steps — reproduced live |

- The watcher's queue-stall guard (gh-172 / PR #1723) fired **correctly**, twice: `no running job for 1875s` at watch-start + 1875s + one poll interval (05:27:42→05:59:04 and 06:00:20→06:31:44 — exact to the second), cancelled each child, re-dispatched once, and failed fast with the pool signature on attempt 2. The guard did its job; the job was genuinely never `in_progress` on the API, so this is not a false positive.
- The same physical box (`fa-m5-1`) served the CLI leg's unpinned `[self-hosted, macos-m5]` jobs **normally** minutes earlier on 10-21 (05:28:20–05:32:08: `runner_name=fa-m5-1`, 30 steps each, logs present). The box is alive; the session that matches the `fa-m5-1` label eats pinned jobs.
- Correlation with the pin: the last good build (10-19 05:28) ran **before** the pin merged (10-19 09:33); **every** pinned build since (4/4 + the live probe) was eaten, while unpinned `macos-m5` jobs land healthy. Most consistent shape: a stale/duplicate registration carries the literal `fa-m5-1` label (GitHub does **not** auto-label runners by name — the label must have been configured explicitly at some registration) and wins the pinned jobs; the healthy session either lacks the label or loses the delivery race to the idle zombie.
- Why `Create Mobile GitHub Release` and `Submit iOS to TestFlight` appear in the issue: both are `needs: [build-ios]` and were cancelled as a cascade when the watcher's containment cancelled the child runs — not independent failures.

**Impact**: The TestFlight leg cannot go green (so gh-1735 cannot auto-close) until the runner registration/box is fixed. Each daily burn is ~31m × 2 attempts of watcher time and one filed/updated issue. No release, no TestFlight upload, no user-visible harm; pub.dev/desktop/website legs are unaffected.

**Fix approach (infra, not code)** — on the fa-m5 boxes (needs owner/admin):

1. Audit runner registrations whose labels include `fa-m5-1` (repo Settings → Actions → Runners, or `GET /repos/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runners` with admin — the CI token gets 403). Expect a stale/online-but-wedged registration; also verify whether the healthy fa-m5-1 box's registration actually carries the `fa-m5-1` label at all.
2. On the physical fa-m5-1 Mac: stop the runner service(s), `config.sh remove` every registration, clean `RUNNER_TEMP` stale-workspace sidecars (gh-160 accumulation) and check disk, then re-register ONE service with explicit labels `self-hosted,macos-m5,fa-m5-1`.
3. Audit fa-m5-2 as well (10-17/10-18 `** ARCHIVE FAILED **`, signing env still unverified per gh-1692) — fix its signing env or keep it out of the iOS pool.
4. Verify: dispatch `build-mobile.yml` (`android_content=none`, `ios_content=all`) — `Build iOS IPA` must show steps + `runner_name` + a growing log within ~2 minutes (healthy signature), never `startedAt`-stamped-but-`queued`.

**Repo-side notes (not this bug's root cause, follow-up candidates)**:

- The filed digest is empty ("no failed-step log available", bare job names) because the report job started 3s after the leg job finished and lost GitHub's log-upload eventual-consistency race; `log_excerpt`'s per-job fallback (`daily_publish_report.sh`) is a one-shot fetch with no bounded retry. The leg log did contain the full `::error::` diagnostics (verified fetchable minutes later). gh-1472-class digest gap.
- The queue-stall guard behaved per design; no watcher change is warranted (loosening it only burns leg time against a zombie that never processes the re-dispatch either — the 10-20 zombie state persisted ≥7 hours).

**Previous attempt**: none (first development leg for gh-1735). Related: gh-1722/PR #1723 (the guard that correctly detected this) explicitly predicted "the physical fa-m5-1 worker itself needs ops attention (reboot/de-register)"; gh-1735 is that predicted damage surfacing.

All outputs are in place, the git tree is clean, and the probe run is cancelled with no orphaned self-hosted job left behind.

## Summary

**gh-1735 is an infrastructure failure, not a product regression** — verdict: `outputs/blocked.json`.

**Root cause**: The runner registration session matching `build-ios`'s `[self-hosted, macos-m5, fa-m5-1]` pin (added by gh-1692, `9de855f1`, merged 10-19 09:33Z) is a zombie: it **consumes `Build iOS IPA` job messages and never executes them**. Jobs sit `startedAt`-stamped but `queued` — 0 steps, no `runner_name`, log blob never uploaded (`BlobNotFound`). The last good build (10-19, pre-pin) preceded four eaten messages (10-20 ×2, 10-21 ×2), while *unpinned* `macos-m5` jobs on the same physical box minutes earlier ran with full telemetry.

**Key findings**:
- The gh-172 queue-stall guard fired *correctly* (05:59:04 / 06:31:44 — exactly watch-start + 1875s): the job was genuinely never `in_progress`, so the "leg failure" is the guard's designed containment; PR #1723 explicitly predicted this damage ("fa-m5-1 needs ops attention (reboot/de-register)").
- `Submit iOS` / `Create Mobile GitHub Release` in the issue are cascade-cancellations, not independent failures.
- **Live reproduction** during this leg: dispatched `build-mobile (none/all)` (run 39557953541) — job delivered 06:51:08Z, queued with zero telemetry for 14 min; cancelled cleanly (no release draft, no publish possible without `build-ios` success).
- Secondary finding (follow-up, not the root cause): the filed digest was empty because the report job raced GitHub's log-upload lag by 3s — `daily_publish_report.sh`'s per-job log fetch is a one-shot.

**Ops checklist** (in `rca.md`/`blocked.json`): de-register the stale `fa-m5-1`-labeled registration, re-register one service on the box with explicit labels, clean gh-160 sidecars, audit fa-m5-2's signing env. The next healthy daily auto-closes gh-1735.

1. Job claimed 05:28:18, no logs ever, no steps, cancelled 05:59:05 by watcher.
2. Attempt 2 re-dispatched 06:00:07; job claimed 06:00:57, no logs, cancelled 06:31:44.
3. Both cancellations came from the watcher's queue-stall detection because the jobs API showed ZERO in_progress jobs.

Wait — point 3 deserves scrutiny again. If the job were in "running" state on the API, the count would be 1. The watcher saw 0. So GitHub's API also considered the job NOT in_progress. Combined with started_at being set and no steps/logs... 

What status does a job have between "queued" and "in_progress"? Hmm, there's `queued` → `in_progress` → `completed`. But there's ALSO the notorious state where a self-hosted runner receives the job, sets started_at, but the API still lists the job as "queued"! That's EXACTLY the gh-172 "zombie" class described: "a self-hosted runner that lost its final job-completion report holds a SUCCEEDED job in_progress forever" — that's the reverse. Hmm.

OH WAIT. That's it! The run status might have been **`queued`** — no wait, the poll only breaks on "completed". The wedge logic doesn't distinguish run status values; it only counts in_progress JOBS. So whether the run was queued or in_progress, if no JOB is in_progress, the stall clock accumulates.

Closes #1722
### Root Cause

The 2026-10-20 `Leg: TestFlight` watcher was killed at its 360m ceiling with no diagnostics while the re-dispatched child run ([39402285750](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/39402285750)) sat `queued` forever: the hung self-hosted worker ignored its own 90m job ceiling (250m actual), never processed the watcher's `gh run cancel` either, and kept holding the single-runner pool. `scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh` polls **run** status only — it saw `in_progress` throughout, burned the remaining ~107m of leg time on a child that could never start, and died as a bare timeout (hence "no failed-step log available"), leaving the orphan queued to publish unattended on pool revival.

### Fix

- `scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh`: added a job-level liveness guard — a not-completed run with **no job in `in_progress` for `DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS` (600s)** is a wedge and rides the existing one-shot self-heal (cancel + re-dispatch once, then fail fast naming the pool). The watcher now also cancels the child on the fail path so a server-side-dead run can never publish unattended when the pool revives. A second wedge now ends in a diagnostic inside the leg (testflight ≈ 273m < 360m ceiling).
- `.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml`: arithmetic comment updated (gh-172 case).
- Ops: cancelled the orphaned queued run `39402285750` (the containment the fixed watcher performs).

### Test Coverage

- `test/dispatch_watch_test.dart` — `gh-172` group: pool-held child (alive, nothing running) stalls into the one self-heal, fails fast with the pool signature on attempt 2, cancels the orphan; plus a transient between-jobs pickup gap that must NOT trip the guard. New stub fixture (`jobs-<id>.txt`) models `gh run view --json jobs`.
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` — **11376 passed, 11 skipped, 0 failed**.

### Notes

- No leg budget/ceiling arithmetic changed — the #351 table is untouched.
- The physical `fa-m5-1` worker itself needs ops attention (reboot/de-register); the guard only bounds the leg damage and makes the signature visible in the leg log.

- gh-172/PR #1723 (merged 10-20 22:49) added the queue-stall wedge detector with DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS = max(600, budget/8) = 1875s for testflight.
- On 10-21 at 05:27 the testflight leg's first child run's Build iOS IPA job was claimed by the fa-m5-1 self-hosted runner at 05:28:18 but never reported ANY step telemetry, logs, or even its in_progress status to GitHub's API (steps: [], runner_name: "", log blob missing).
- Because the jobs API showed no `in_progress` job (the job stayed in a state other than in_progress — consistent with the runner never ACKing), the new queue-stall guard read this as the "pool-held zombie" signature, cancelled the child at 05:59 and re-dispatched.
- The re-dispatched child (06:00:07) hit the same dead runner state (job claimed 06:00:57, no telemetry), the guard fired again at 06:31:44 and — since attempt 2 — failed the leg with the containment error.
- The issue filer then could not excerpt logs (nothing was ever uploaded), hence "(no failed-step log available)".

Now — WAIT. I need to double-check the claim "the job was not in_progress in the API". Because the job HAS startedAt set (05:28:18). Hmm — but does the watcher's jq count it? Let me verify by checking the jobs API state transitions more carefully. Actually, hmm, there's an important subtlety I glossed over.

Let me look again at the watcher's poll and the ACTUAL jobs API semantics. `gh run view <run> --json status,conclusion,jobs` calls the "List jobs for a workflow run" endpoint... Actually `gh run view --json jobs` uses that endpoint. The jobs in it each carry status: queued|in_progress|completed.

Given the evidence (steps [], runner_name "", no logs, BlobNotFound), I hypothesize the job on the API was in status `queued` even though started_at was set. This is the documented self-hosted pathology where the runner process took the job, GitHub marked started_at on dispatch, but the runner never posted the "job started" event (the first POST fails or hangs), so the job's API status stays `queued` and no runner_name is recorded. Actually runner_name empty + steps empty + logs missing = the runner never reported ANYTHING.

Hmm, wait. Actually, is it possible that the job never even reached a runner and sat queued? But started_at 05:28:18 was set... For QUED jobs started_at is typically null/empty. Here it's set. So the job WAS dispatched to a runner (fa-m5-1), the runner ACKed at the transport level (message delivered → started_at), but then the runner's worker never reported "Job started" processing events (steps, runner_name, logs).

Either way — the ROOT CAUSE is: **the fa-m5-1 self-hosted macOS runner claimed the build-ios job and hung without reporting anything** (the "zombie worker" pathology called out in gh-172: "The physical fa-m5-1 worker itself needs ops attention (reboot/de-register); the guard only bounds the leg damage"). The queue-stall guard then behaved AS DESIGNED: it detected the zombie signature, cancelled + re-dispatched once, and failed fast on the second wedge. The leg "failure" is the guard working; the underlying root cause is the hung self-hosted runner.

Hmm. But wait — is this ticket asking me to FIX something in the repo? The task is a "Senior Developer Engineer specializing in root cause analysis and bug fixing". The ticket: "[daily-publish] testflight leg failed". Auto-filed, auto-closes when the leg goes green.

Let me think about what the right fix is here. Two candidate framings:

**Framing 1 (infra)**: fa-m5-1 is physically hung; needs ops (reboot/de-register). Per the "Returning from test-automation failure" rules: "If the failure is caused by a missing token, missing permission, missing secret, or any other access/credential/infra issue that you cannot fix in product code, write outputs/blocked.json and stop." — But is it really pure infra? Hmm.

**Framing 2 (product/CI code defect)**: There IS a genuine defect visible in the product code paths here. Look at the poll logic in dispatch_and_watch.sh again:

```bash
elif [ -n "$running" ] && [ "$running" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
 last_running="$now"
elif [ -n "$running" ] && [ $((now - last_running)) -gt "$queue_stall" ]; then
 wedge="no running job for ${queue_stall}s ..."
``

  themselves (`latest tag + 1` at the child's own dispatch moment). A tag
  pinned once in the orchestrator would race `auto_release.sh` — the daily
  could attach assets to a tag minted at a different commit than the built
  code. Self-derivation keeps tag and code consistent; the two children
  derive within minutes of each other and converge on the same tag
  (`gh release create` attaches to an existing tag rather than moving it);
- never publishes to pub.dev itself (see the pub.dev row above) — pub.dev
  movement stays 100% in the auto_release → ci.yml tag job path, with the
  daily as verifier and rerun-recovery;
- keeps NO daily-side wedge alarm for a tag that never publishes (#1368):
  a freshly cut tag reads `release-in-flight` ⏭️ in the daily for as long
  as its outcome is unobservable (young tag inside the grace window, run
  queued past the terminal-wait budget). The version under test is the
  LATEST REMOTE TAG (`git ls-remote`), never a file read. The remaining
  tripwires for a genuinely stuck release: the plan job's
  release-unresolved re-arm (every daily re-verifies while pub.dev is
  behind the latest tag), and the tag-run selector in
  `scripts/verify_pubdev_release.sh`, which alarms `only non-push run(s)`
  once a tag exists but only non-push runs registered.

**Change baseline**: legs run only when `main` moved since the last green
daily **that ran all legs** (schedule runs, or `legs=all` dispatches). A
single-leg green dispatch never advances the baseline, so a partial smoke
can't make the next scheduled run skip the legs it never exercised.
One exception (gh-1192, reworked gh-1522): a release-in-flight pubdev leg
exits 0, so that green daily becomes the baseline — the plan gate
(`scripts/daily_plan.sh`) therefore still forces the legs while the
LATEST TAG's version is not yet served by pub.dev, keeping the
re-verification and the failed-run recovery alive on a quiet main. A
failing `plan` job
(not just legs) files its own
`[daily-publish] plan leg failed` issue — nothing escapes the loop.

## Self-healing issues

On a failing (or timed-out) leg the `report` job files an issue:

- title `[daily-publish] <leg> leg failed`, label `bug` + `daily-publish`,
  assigned to `vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit`;
- body: daily run link, leg run link, failing job/step names, the last ~50
  lines of the failed step's log;
- **dedup**: an open issue with the same signature gets a comment instead
  of a duplicate;
- **auto-close**: when the leg goes green in a later daily run, the open
  issue is closed with a comment.

Each run also writes a single job-summary table (leg → version → status →
links) and exits red itself when any leg failed.

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis — gh-1735 `[daily-publish] testflight leg failed`

**Bug**: The daily-publish TestFlight leg (daily run 39549568592 → child run 39552755224) failed with three jobs listed as failing — `Build iOS IPA`, `Create Mobile GitHub Release`, `Submit iOS to TestFlight` — and an empty failure excerpt.

**Root cause**: The self-hosted runner registration session matching the `[self-hosted, macos-m5, fa-m5-1]` pin (added by gh-1692, commit 9de855f1, merged 2026-10-19 09:33Z) is a **zombie: it consumes `Build iOS IPA` job messages and never executes or reports them**. GitHub stamps the job's `startedAt` at message delivery, but the job never enters `in_progress`, records zero steps, zero logs, and no `runner_name`; the job-log blob is never uploaded (`BlobNotFound` from the job-log endpoint). No repo code runs at all in this state — the failure is pre-`Set up job`, i.e. runner-infrastructure, not product code.

**Evidence chain**:

| When | Run | Build iOS IPA | Signature |
|---|---|---|---|
| 10-19 05:28 (pre-pin) | 39204704151 | SUCCESS 05:28:48→05:59:54 | `runner_name=fa-m5-1`, 24 steps, logs ✅ |
| 10-20 05:28 (first daily after the pin) | 39374977270 | "started" 05:28:04, cancelled 09:38:29 | `runner_name=""`, 0 steps, no logs |
| 10-20 09:40 (gh-172's queued-forever run) | 39402285750 | "started" 09:40:18, cancelled 12:27 | `runner_name=""`, 0 steps |
| 10-21 05:28 (leg attempt 1) | 39549660700 | "started" 05:28:18, cancelled 05:59:05 | `runner_name=""`, 0 steps, job log = BlobNotFound |
| 10-21 06:00 (leg attempt 2) | 39552755224 | "started" 06:00:57, cancelled 06:31:44 | `runner_name=""`, 0 steps, no logs |
| 10-21 06:51 (**live probe, this session**) | 39557953541 | "started" 06:51:08, cancelled 07:05 after 14 min in limbo | `runner_name=""`, 0 steps — reproduced live |

- The watcher's queue-stall guard (gh-172 / PR #1723) fired **correctly**, twice: `no running job for 1875s` at watch-start + 1875s + one poll interval (05:27:42→05:59:04 and 06:00:20→06:31:44 — exact to the second), cancelled each child, re-dispatched once, and failed fast with the pool signature on attempt 2. The guard did its job; the job was genuinely never `in_progress` on the API, so this is not a false positive.
- The same physical box (`fa-m5-1`) served the CLI leg's unpinned `[self-hosted, macos-m5]` jobs **normally** minutes earlier on 10-21 (05:28:20–05:32:08: `runner_name=fa-m5-1`, 30 steps each, logs present). The box is alive; the session that matches the `fa-m5-1` label eats pinned jobs.
- Correlation with the pin: the last good build (10-19 05:28) ran **before** the pin merged (10-19 09:33); **every** pinned build since (4/4 + the live probe) was eaten, while unpinned `macos-m5` jobs land healthy. Most consistent shape: a stale/duplicate registration carries the literal `fa-m5-1` label (GitHub does **not** auto-label runners by name — the label must have been configured explicitly at some registration) and wins the pinned jobs; the healthy session either lacks the label or loses the delivery race to the idle zombie.
- Why `Create Mobile GitHub Release` and `Submit iOS to TestFlight` appear in the issue: both are `needs: [build-ios]` and were cancelled as a cascade when the watcher's containment cancelled the child runs — not independent failures.

**Impact**: The TestFlight leg cannot go green (so gh-1735 cannot auto-close) until the runner registration/box is fixed. Each daily burn is ~31m × 2 attempts of watcher time and one filed/updated issue. No release, no TestFlight upload, no user-visible harm; pub.dev/desktop/website legs are unaffected.

**Fix approach (infra, not code)** — on the fa-m5 boxes (needs owner/admin):

1. Audit runner registrations whose labels include `fa-m5-1` (repo Settings → Actions → Runners, or `GET /repos/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runners` with admin — the CI token gets 403). Expect a stale/online-but-wedged registration; also verify whether the healthy fa-m5-1 box's registration actually carries the `fa-m5-1` label at all.
2. On the physical fa-m5-1 Mac: stop the runner service(s), `config.sh remove` every registration, clean `RUNNER_TEMP` stale-workspace sidecars (gh-160 accumulation) and check disk, then re-register ONE service with explicit labels `self-hosted,macos-m5,fa-m5-1`.
3. Audit fa-m5-2 as well (10-17/10-18 `** ARCHIVE FAILED **`, signing env still unverified per gh-1692) — fix its signing env or keep it out of the iOS pool.
4. Verify: dispatch `build-mobile.yml` (`android_content=none`, `ios_content=all`) — `Build iOS IPA` must show steps + `runner_name` + a growing log within ~2 minutes (healthy signature), never `startedAt`-stamped-but-`queued`.

**Repo-side notes (not this bug's root cause, follow-up candidates)**:

- The filed digest is empty ("no failed-step log available", bare job names) because the report job started 3s after the leg job finished and lost GitHub's log-upload eventual-consistency race; `log_excerpt`'s per-job fallback (`daily_publish_report.sh`) is a one-shot fetch with no bounded retry. The leg log did contain the full `::error::` diagnostics (verified fetchable minutes later). gh-1472-class digest gap.
- The queue-stall guard behaved per design; no watcher change is warranted (loosening it only burns leg time against a zombie that never processes the re-dispatch either — the 10-20 zombie state persisted ≥7 hours).

**Previous attempt**: none (first development leg for gh-1735). Related: gh-1722/PR #1723 (the guard that correctly detected this) explicitly predicted "the physical fa-m5-1 worker itself needs ops attention (reboot/de-register)"; gh-1735 is that predicted damage surfacing.

## Summary

**gh-1735 is an infrastructure failure, not a product regression** — verdict: `outputs/blocked.json`.

**Root cause**: The runner registration session matching `build-ios`'s `[self-hosted, macos-m5, fa-m5-1]` pin (added by gh-1692, `9de855f1`, merged 10-19 09:33Z) is a zombie: it **consumes `Build iOS IPA` job messages and never executes them**. Jobs sit `startedAt`-stamped but `queued` — 0 steps, no `runner_name`, log blob never uploaded (`BlobNotFound`). The last good build (10-19, pre-pin) preceded four eaten messages (10-20 ×2, 10-21 ×2), while *unpinned* `macos-m5` jobs on the same physical box minutes earlier ran with full telemetry.

**Key findings**:
- The gh-172 queue-stall guard fired *correctly* (05:59:04 / 06:31:44 — exactly watch-start + 1875s): the job was genuinely never `in_progress`, so the "leg failure" is the guard's designed containment; PR #1723 explicitly predicted this damage ("fa-m5-1 needs ops attention (reboot/de-register)").
- `Submit iOS` / `Create Mobile GitHub Release` in the issue are cascade-cancellations, not independent failures.
- **Live reproduction** during this leg: dispatched `build-mobile (none/all)` (run 39557953541) — job delivered 06:51:08Z, queued with zero telemetry for 14 min; cancelled cleanly (no release draft, no publish possible without `build-ios` success).
- Secondary finding (follow-up, not the root cause): the filed digest was empty because the report job raced GitHub's log-upload lag by 3s — `daily_publish_report.sh`'s per-job log fetch is a one-shot.

**Ops checklist** (in `rca.md`/`blocked.json`): de-register the stale `fa-m5-1`-labeled registration, re-register one service on the box with explicit labels, clean gh-160 sidecars, audit fa-m5-2's signing env. The next healthy daily auto-closes gh-1735.

Wait... let me check what the run status was during the watch. Run status: "in_progress"? The poll output format is `"\(.status)/" + (.conclusion // "-") + " + count`. The wedge branch requires:
1. `[ -n "$running" ]` — running must be non-empty.
2. `[ "$running" -gt 0 ]` false.
3. `[ -n "$running" ] && [ $((now - last_running)) -gt "$queue_stall" ]`.

So `running` was exactly "0" every successful poll for 31 minutes, while the run had an in_progress job.

Hypothesis A: The jobs API for THIS run genuinely reported no in_progress job because the self-hosted runner job's status on the API was... hmm.

Wait — actually, let me look again at the jobs data I got for run 39527524: `"status":"completed"` for Build iOS IPA with conclusion cancelled. During the run it would have been in_progress. Unless...

Hypothesis B: There's a **jq bug in the poll expression**. Let me test the exact poll command against a live running run to see what it returns. Actually, let me test the jq expression itself with a synthetic JSON.

Actually — WAIT. Look very carefully at the jq expression:

```jq
"\"\(.status)/" + (.conclusion // "-") + " + ([.jobs[] | select(.status == "in_progress")] | length | tostring)
``

Note the first string: `"\"\(.status)/"`. That's a jq string containing an escaped quote `\"` then `\(.status)` interpolation then `/`. So output = `"<status>/- N`. status="in_progress" → `in_progress/- 1`. OK.

Then in bash:
```bash
status="${observed%% *}"    # "in_progress/-"
running="${observed##* }"   # "1"
``

Then:
```bash
if [ -z "$observed" ] || [ "$status" = "$observed" ]; then # error check
``
`status="in_progress/-"`, observed="in_progress/- 1" — not equal → no error. OK.

`[ "${status%%/*}" = "completed" ]` → "in_progress" ≠ completed → continue.

`if [ $((now - started)) -gt "$budget" ]` → no.
`elif [ -n "$running" ] && [ "$running" -gt 0 ]` → running="1" → `[ "1" -gt 0 ]` true → last_running=now. Fine.

So if the API returned the truth, the wedge would never fire. But it did fire. Therefore the API returned 0 in_progress jobs — OR the jq expression has a real bug.

Let me test the jq expression locally right now with a mock. There might be a subtle issue: `select(.status == "in_progress")` — but jobs on this self-hosted runner... Hmm wait, what if the JOB status is not "in_progress" but something else while it's running on a self-hosted runner? GitHub job statuses: queued, in_progress, completed. Self-hosted runners report the same.

Hmm, but what if... the job was "queued" on the API while the runner was building? There's a known class of issue with self-hosted runners behind proxies: the runner claims the job and starts it, but the job status update to GitHub fails/lags. But for 31 minutes on BOTH attempts?

Wait, actually, let me reconsider Hypothesis B more carefully — maybe the poll command FAILS (exit non-zero) on every poll but with set -euo pipefail... no wait: `observed="$(... 2>/dev/null)" || observed=""`. If gh fails → observed="" → error branch → last_running refreshed → no wedge. So polls must have SUCCEEDED and returned `... 0`.

Hmm, wait. Let me recheck: could `observed` be a NON-EMPTY string that parses weirdly, e.g. `"in_progress/-"` with NO trailing number? Then status="in_progress/-" (whole string, since no space), running="${observed##* }" = "in_progress/-" (no space → whole string). Then `[ "$status" = "$observed" ]` → TRUE → error branch. No wedge. Not it.

What if observed = "in_progress/- 0" genuinely every time? Then the jobs API really said 0 in_progress.

Let me now verify what the GitHub API reports for a live self-hosted job. I can reproduce: check the CURRENT state of things. Is there a live run right now? Let me check what the API says for job status of a run in progress... I can't go back in time.

``
{"completedAt":"2026-10-21T06:31:44Z","conclusion":"cancelled","name":"Build iOS IPA","startedAt":"2026-10-21T06:00:57Z","status":"completed","steps":[]}
``

"steps":[] — EMPTY! The Build iOS IPA job ran for 31 minutes and its `steps` array is EMPTY?! Every job in both cancelled runs has `"steps":[]`.   themselves (`latest tag + 1` at the child's own dispatch moment). A tag
  pinned once in the orchestrator would race `auto_release.sh` — the daily
  could attach assets to a tag minted at a different commit than the built
  code. Self-derivation keeps tag and code consistent; the two children
  derive within minutes of each other and converge on the same tag
  (`gh release create` attaches to an existing tag rather than moving it);
- never publishes to pub.dev itself (see the pub.dev row above) — pub.dev
  movement stays 100% in the auto_release → ci.yml tag job path, with the
  daily as verifier and rerun-recovery;
- keeps NO daily-side wedge alarm for a tag that never publishes (#1368):
  a freshly cut tag reads `release-in-flight` ⏭️ in the daily for as long
  as its outcome is unobservable (young tag inside the grace window, run
  queued past the terminal-wait budget). The version under test is the
  LATEST REMOTE TAG (`git ls-remote`), never a file read. The remaining
  tripwires for a genuinely stuck release: the plan job's
  release-unresolved re-arm (every daily re-verifies while pub.dev is
  behind the latest tag), and the tag-run selector in
  `scripts/verify_pubdev_release.sh`, which alarms `only non-push run(s)`
  once a tag exists but only non-push runs registered.

**Change baseline**: legs run only when `main` moved since the last green
daily **that ran all legs** (schedule runs, or `legs=all` dispatches). A
single-leg green dispatch never advances the baseline, so a partial smoke
can't make the next scheduled run skip the legs it never exercised.
One exception (gh-1192, reworked gh-1522): a release-in-flight pubdev leg
exits 0, so that green daily becomes the baseline — the plan gate
(`scripts/daily_plan.sh`) therefore still forces the legs while the
LATEST TAG's version is not yet served by pub.dev, keeping the
re-verification and the failed-run recovery alive on a quiet main. A
failing `plan` job
(not just legs) files its own
`[daily-publish] plan leg failed` issue — nothing escapes the loop.

## Self-healing issues

On a failing (or timed-out) leg the `report` job files an issue:

- title `[daily-publish] <leg> leg failed`, label `bug` + `daily-publish`,
  assigned to `vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit`;
- body: daily run link, leg run link, failing job/step names, the last ~50
  lines of the failed step's log;
- **dedup**: an open issue with the same signature gets a comment instead
  of a duplicate;
- **auto-close**: when the leg goes green in a later daily run, the open
  issue is closed with a comment.

Each run also writes a single job-summary table (leg → version → status →
links) and exits red itself when any leg failed.

KEY FINDING:

- 9de855f1 (2026-10-19 09:33:45Z): "gh-1692 [daily-publish] TestFlight dry 5 days: 4 chained failures — current: fa-m5-2 archive fails silently (xcpretty swallows xcodebuild error), **routing still unpinned**" — this is the commit that added the `fa-m5-1` pin + xcbeautify.

So the fa-m5-1 PIN merged on **10-19 at 09:33Z** — AFTER the 10-19 morning SUCCESS (05:28–05:59, which ran on fa-m5-1 via the unpinned `[self-hosted, macos-m5]` list).

The FIRST day the pin was active in a daily run = **10-20 at 05:27** — exactly the first day the build-ios jobs started being eaten (10-20 05:28:04 started_at, zero telemetry).

WOW. That reframes the root cause:

- On 10-19 (and earlier), build-ios matched `[self-hosted, macos-m5]` → GitHub could route it to EITHER box; it landed on whichever was free. On 10-19 it landed on the good one (runner_name recorded = fa-m5-1... hmm, or fa-m5-2? The API said runner_name "fa-m5-1" for the 10-19 job — so the box NAMED fa-m5-1 built successfully on 10-19 unpinned).
- On 10-20+, with the pin `[self-hosted, macos-m5, fa-m5-1]` — every build-ios job message is eaten (started_at, zero telemetry). Meanwhile jobs pinned only by macos-m5 (build-macos CLI leg jobs on 10-21 05:28) run FINE and record runner_name fa-m5-1.

Interpretation A (duplicate/stale registration carrying the `fa-m5-1` label): there are (at least) TWO online registrations that match `[self-hosted, macos-m5, fa-m5-1]`: a healthy one (which served build-macos at 05:28:20 and recorded runner_name fa-m5-1) and a zombie (which eats the build-ios messages). When BOTH labels must match, GitHub's balancer picks between the two matching sessions; the build-ios job drew the zombie twice on 10-20 and twice on 10-21 (4 for 4). The unpinned macos-m5 jobs drew the healthy one (or, when the zombie is busy... it's never busy — it never runs anything).

Hmm wait, that doesn't quite work either: with TWO matching online registrations, each job message goes to one of them. 4/4 build-ios draws hit the zombie while the macos-m5 jobs (a superset pool incl. both boxes) drew the healthy session. Unlucky but possible — or the zombie session (idle, no job) long-polls with a fresh connection and reliably wins the race against the busy healthy box.

Interpretation B (the `fa-m5-1` LABEL name is a lie / misdirected routing): the label `fa-m5-1` is attached to a registration whose session is wedged (e.g. the registration token was re-issued, or an old `.runner` state on the box under a different service still claims labels self-hosted+macos-m5+fa-m5-1 and is "online" but its worker can't launch). The healthy fa-m5-1 box's CURRENT registration might NOT carry the `fa-m5-1` label at all! Wait — but then how did build-macos (labels: self-hosted+macos-m5, no fa-m5-1) record runner_name "fa-m5-1"? The runner's NAME is fa-m5-1 (the registration name), but its LABELS are only [self-hosted, macos-m5, X] where X ≠ fa-m5-1... If the gh-1692 pin added a label that the box was never actually given (the pin's author ASSUMED the runner-name-label auto-matches — GitHub does auto-add the runner NAME as a label? NO — GitHub does NOT auto-label runners by name! Runner labels are only what's in the registration's --labels config + defaults. The gh-1692 comment says "the runner-name label `fa-m5-1`" — the author believed the runner name acts as a label. For GitHub-hosted runners, names aren't labels either. BUT custom labels can be added at registration time (--labels flag) or via the UI.)

Hmm wait — if NO registration carried the `fa-m5-1` label, build-ios would sit QUED forever (started_at NEVER set). But started_at IS set — a session with matching labels received the message. So SOME online session DOES claim the fa-m5-1 label. And jobs sent to it die silently.

So the zombie session (which claims self-hosted+macos-m5+fa-m5-1) exists and eats build-ios messages. The healthy box (name fa-m5-1) either also matches (duplicate registration with same labels — Interpretation A) or the healthy box's registration lacks the fa-m5-1 label and only serves the macos-m5-generic jobs (Interpretation B').

Either way — infra: **the registration(s) matching the gh-1692 pin are a wedged session; the pin routed the iOS lane into it since 10-20**. The repo-side contribution: the gh-1692 pin (9de855f1) changed routing the morning after the last good run, and every run since has died at the pin's target. Before the pin, the same workflow on the same pool landed on the good box and BUILT successfully (10-19 05:59 success).

Hmm!! Now THIS changes the calculus about "repo fix possible?":

Option: **remove/revisit the fa-m5-1 pin** (revert to `[self-hosted, macos-m5]`) so build-ios can land on the healthy box again?

Counter-evidence: the pin exists because fa-m5-2 was producing silent archive failures (10-17/10-18, gh-1692's raison d'être) and the pin was the fix for gh-1692 ("routing still unpinned"). Reverting the pin sends build-ios back to the coin flip: good box (build works) or fa-m5-2 (silent archive failure). With fa-m5-2 broken, unpining trades a 100% eaten message for a ~50% silent build failure. NOT a fix.

BUT — what if the "zombie" IS fa-m5-2 carrying a spurious `fa-m5-1` label?! The gh-1692 comment says fa-m5-2 is "signing env unverified" and produced ARCHIVE FAILED on 10-17/10-18 — those runs DID produce logs and steps (real builds failing at archive). So fa-m5-2's session wasn't a zombie then; it RAN jobs. A box can't be both "runs the build and fails at archive" (10-18) and "eats messages pre-Set-up-job" (10-20+) — unless its runner service degraded further in between (possible: the 10-19/10-20 boundary could be fa-m5-2's disk finally filling / service half-dead).

I can't distinguish A / B / B' from here (no admin API access). What I CAN do: check whether build-ios jobs before 10-20 but after... the pin merged 10-19 09:33; between 10-19 09:33 and 10-20 05:27, did any build-ios job run pinned? Let me check the 10-20 09:39 attempt-2 (queued forever — that one never even got started_at? Earlier query: 10-20 attempt-2 job 118559997592: started_at 09:40:18, steps 0, runner_name "" — ALSO eaten-but-stamped). Interesting — gh-172 described attempt-2 as "sat queued forever"; the API stamps started_at even in the limbo state. OK.

So since the pin merged, build-ios has run ZERO successful jobs: 4 messages, all eaten (10-20 ×2, 10-21 ×2). And on 10-19 05:28 the SAME pool (unpinned) built fine on the box named fa-m5-1.

Given all this — is a repo-side fix possible and CORECT? The candidates:

1. Remove the pin → coin flip with broken fa-m5-2 → likely silent failures. NO.
2. Pin to fa-m5-2 instead → its signing env is unverified/broken. NO.
3. Hosted runners → cost/quota + owner decision + secrets/signing re-validation. External decision. NO (unilaterally).
4. Ops fix the box/registrations → THE actual fix. This is what PR #1723 and gh-1692 both point to ("the physical fa-m5-1 worker itself needs ops attention (reboot/de-register)", "until fa-m5-2 is fixed").

Therefore: BLOCKED on infra/ops — with a precise, evidence-backed checklist of what ops must do:
- Audit runner registrations matching labels [self-hosted, macos-m5, fa-m5-1] (repo Settings → Actions → Runers, or GET /actions/runers with admin): look for a duplicate/stale fa-m5-1 registration and/or whether the healthy box's registration actually CARRIES the fa-m5-1 label.
- On the box(es): reboot, de-register stale registrations (config.cmd remove / deleting from the UI), re-register with explicit labels incl. fa-m5-1; verify fa-m5-2's signing env or de-register it too.
- Clean the gh-160 stale-workspace sidecar accumulation in RUNER_TEMP (possible disk-pressure cause).
- Probe: dispatch build-mobile (none/all) once; confirm Build iOS IPA records runner_name + steps + logs (the healthy signature), i.e. not the started_at-with-zero-telemetry limbo.

Now the TDD/repro question one final time. The flowchart: REPRO (unit test that reproduces the bug; run — MUST FAIL) → EXISTS → BLOCKED. For an infra-routed failure, the honest "repro" is: the observed production evidence (4 eaten messages across 10-20/10-21) + the pin-merge timeline correlation…

Root-cause chain is now solid. The `fa-m5-1` pin merged **10-19 09:33Z** (gh-1692), and every build-ios job dispatched **since** has been eaten (started_at stamped, zero telemetry, no logs), while unpinned `macos-m5` jobs on the same pool built normally. Before writing the verdict, I'll run a cheap, side-effect-safe live probe: dispatch the same inputs the leg uses — if the box got fixed, the lane goes healthy; if not, I cancel the run myself within minutes (no release draft, no publish — `release-mobile`/`submit-ios` both require `build-ios` success).
